# Majmu' al-Fatawa - Tome 28

## Page 13596

VOLUME TWENTY-EIGHT
THE BOOK OF ISLAMIC JURISPRUDENCE
PART EIGHT:
JIHAD

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

Shaykh al-Islām Ahmad ibn Taymiyyah—may Allah sanctify his soul—was asked about the hadith:

“Keeping watch on the seacoast for one night is better than a man’s deeds among his family for a thousand years.”

He was also asked about residing in Mecca, Jerusalem, and Medina the Radiant with the intention of worship and complete devotion to Allah Most High, and residing in Damietta, Alexandria, and Tripoli with the intention of guarding the frontiers: which is better?

He answered:

All praise is due to Allah. Rather, residing at the Muslims’ frontier posts, such as those in Syria and Egypt, is better than residing near the three mosques. I know of no disagreement among the scholars on this matter, and more than one of the leading scholars has explicitly stated it. This is because guarding the frontiers is a form of jihad, whereas residing near these mosques is, at most, a form of Hajj. As Allah Most High says:

“Do you consider providing water to pilgrims and maintaining the Sacred Mosque equal to one who believes in Allah and the Last Day and strives in Allah’s cause? They are not equal in Allah’s sight.”

In the two Sahīh collections, it is reported that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was asked: “Which

---

## Page 13597

deeds are best?”

He replied: “Faith in Allah and His Messenger.”

He was asked: “Then what?”

He replied: “Then jihad in His cause.”

He was asked: “Then what?”

He replied: “Then an accepted Hajj.”

It has also been reported:

“A military expedition in Allah’s cause is better than seventy pilgrimages.”

Muslim reported in his Sahīh, on the authority of Salmān al-Fārisī, that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Guarding the frontiers for a day and a night in Allah’s cause is better than fasting for a month and spending its nights in prayer. Whoever dies while guarding the frontiers dies as one engaged in jihad; his provision from Paradise will continue to reach him, and he will be safe from the one who puts him to trial.”

In the Sunan collections, it is reported on the authority of ‘Uthmān that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“One day guarding the frontiers in Allah’s cause is better than a thousand days spent in any other place.”

‘Uthmān related this from the pulpit of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, explaining that he told them this in order to convey the Sunnah.

Abū Hurayrah said:

“I would rather guard the frontiers for one night in Allah’s cause than spend the Night of Decree in prayer beside the Black Stone.”

The virtues of guarding the frontiers and keeping watch in Allah’s cause are too numerous to be contained on this sheet. And Allah knows best.

## Page 13598

The esteemed scholars, distinguished leaders and imams of the religion—may Allah be pleased with them all—are requested to inform us of the virtues of archery and teaching it, and of what has been reported concerning someone who abandons it after learning it. Which is superior: shooting with a bow, thrusting with a spear, or striking with a sword? Does each have its own specialized body of knowledge and an appropriate setting for its use?

If a man teaches another archery, spear fighting, or other skills involving weapons of war and jihad in the cause of Allah Most High, and the pupil denies having been taught by him, moves to another teacher and affiliates himself with him, does he thereby incur sin?

If someone says to this pupil who has changed teachers, “Your blood is forfeit,” or, “You are to be killed,” does the speaker thereby incur sin?

If he goes further and says to him, “You are a foundling,” or, “You are a child of fornication,” does this constitute an accusation of unlawful sexual intercourse for which the speaker is liable to the prescribed punishment?

Is it lawful for the second teacher to accept this pupil and discipline him for disowning his teacher?

If the pupil who has changed teachers says, “I am affiliated with so-and-so as the one who instructed and trained me, and with so-and-so as the one who imparted knowledge and understanding to me,” is that permissible for him?

And is a beginner permitted to

---

## Page 13599

stand among a group of teachers and pupils and say:
“O good people, I ask Allah Most High, and I ask you to request of so-and-so, that he accept me as his brother, companion, servant, pupil, or the like”; then one of those present rises, takes a pledge from him, imposes whatever conditions he wishes, and ties a cloth or something similar around his waist—is this practice permissible, given the defensive loyalty and partisanship toward a teacher that result from it? Each teacher thereby acquires brothers, companions, followers, and pupils who stand by him whenever he acts, whether rightly or wrongly, treating his enemies as their enemies and his allies as their allies.

If they gather to compete in archery for a stake, is that lawful? Does it compromise a teacher’s uprightness if his pupils do things that are unlawful in the religion and he allows them to continue? If the teacher ties the cloth around a pupil’s waist and this brings a gift and a token of appreciation—all of which customarily goes to the teacher—is it lawful for him to accept it? May the teacher accept a fee, a donation, or a gift? The teacher does, after all, incur expenses for equipment and other things. Give us a ruling—may you be rewarded—and guide us. May Allah be pleased with you all.

Shaykh al-Islām Ahmad ibn Taymiyyah—may Allah be pleased with him—replied:

Praise be to Allah, Lord of all worlds. Archery in the cause of Allah and thrusting with a spear in the cause of

---

## Page 13600

Allah, and striking in the cause of Allah—all of these are among the things commanded by Allah Most High and His Messenger. Allah Most High has mentioned all three, saying:

“So when you meet those who disbelieve, strike their necks until, when you have thoroughly subdued them, bind them firmly. Then either release them graciously or ransom them, until war lays down its burdens.”

He Most High also says:

“Strike above their necks, and strike all their fingertips.”

And He Most High says:

“O you who believe, Allah will surely test you with some game within reach of your hands and spears.”

And He Most High says:

“Prepare against them whatever strength you can and steeds of war, to terrify thereby the enemy of Allah and your enemy, and others besides them.”

It is established in Sahīh Muslim and elsewhere that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, recited this verse from the pulpit and said:

“Indeed, strength is archery! Indeed, strength is archery! Indeed, strength is archery!”

It is also authentically reported that he, peace and blessings be upon him, said:

“Practise archery and ride; practising archery is dearer to me than riding. Whoever learns archery and then forgets it is not one of us.”

Another narration reads:

“Whoever learns archery and then forgets it has been ungrateful for a blessing.”

In the Sunan collections, it is reported that he, peace and blessings be upon him, said:

“Every amusement a man engages in is vain except shooting with his bow, training his horse, and playing with his wife, for these are worthwhile pursuits.”

He also said:

“Lands will be conquered for you, and Allah will provide for you; so let none of you fail to enjoy practising with his arrows.”

Makhūl said: ‘Umar ibn al-Khattāb wrote to Syria: “Teach

---

## Page 13601

your children archery and horsemanship.”

In Sahīh al-Bukhārī, it is reported that he, peace and blessings be upon him, said:

“Shoot, children of Ishmael, for your father was an archer.”

He passed by some men of Aslam competing in archery, and said, peace and blessings be upon him: “Shoot, children of Ishmael, for your father was an archer. Shoot, and I am with the sons of so-and-so.” One of the two teams stopped shooting, so he asked: “Why are you not shooting?” They replied: “How can we shoot when you are with them?” He said: “Shoot, for I am with all of you.”

Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqās, may Allah be pleased with him, said: “The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, poured out his arrows for me—meaning that he emptied his quiver on the day of Uhud—and said: ‘Shoot! May my father and mother be sacrificed for you!’”

ʿAlī ibn Abī Tālib said: “I never saw the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, offer both his parents as a ransom for anyone except Saʿd. He said to him: ‘Shoot, Saʿd! May my father and mother be sacrificed for you!’”

Anas ibn Mālik said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said:

“The voice of Abū Talhah in the army is worth more than a hundred men.”

When Abū Talhah was with the army, he would kneel before the Prophet and empty his quiver, saying: “May my life be sacrificed for yours, and my face shield yours.”

The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, possessed a sword, a bow, and a spear.

In the Sunan collections, it is reported that he, peace and blessings be upon him, said:

---

## Page 13602

“Whoever shoots an arrow in Allah’s cause—whether it reaches the enemy or not—will receive a reward equivalent to freeing a slave.”

In the Sunan collections, it is reported that he, peace and blessings be upon him, said:

“Allah admits three people to Paradise through a single arrow: its maker, who seeks reward through making it; the one who shoots it; and the one who supplies it.”

This is because these are acts of jihad, and jihad is the best voluntary deed a person can undertake. Voluntary jihad is superior to voluntary Hajj and other acts of worship, as Allah Most High says:

“Do you consider providing water to pilgrims and maintaining the Sacred Mosque equal to the deeds of one who believes in Allah and the Last Day and strives in Allah’s cause? They are not equal before Allah, and Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.

“Those who believe, emigrate, and strive in Allah’s cause with their wealth and their lives are greater in rank before Allah. It is they who are successful.

“Their Lord gives them glad tidings of mercy from Him, His pleasure, and gardens in which they will enjoy lasting bliss,

“remaining there forever. Indeed, with Allah is a tremendous reward.”

In the Sahīh, it is reported that a man said: “After embracing Islam, I would not mind doing no deed other than maintaining the Sacred Mosque.” ʿAlī ibn Abī Tālib said: “Jihad in Allah’s cause is superior to all of this.” ʿUmar ibn al-Khattāb said: “Do not raise your voices by the pulpit of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him. Rather, when the prayer is over, I shall ask him about that.” He asked him, and Allah revealed this verse.

Thus He made clear to them that faith and jihad are superior to maintaining the Sacred Mosque, performing Hajj and ʿumrah, circumambulation, and to

---

## Page 13603

showing kindness to pilgrims by providing them with water. For this reason, Abū Hurayrah—may Allah be pleased with him—said: “I would rather spend one night on guard in Allah’s cause than spend the Night of Decree in prayer beside the Black Stone.” Thus, guarding the frontiers is superior to residing in Mecca and Medina, and using the spear and bow at the frontiers is superior to voluntary prayer. In towns far from the enemy, however, it is comparable to voluntary prayer.

In the two Sahīh collections, the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, is reported to have said:

“In Paradise there are a hundred ranks which Allah has prepared for those who strive in His cause. The distance between one rank and the next is like the distance between heaven and earth.”

Each of these activities has its appropriate setting, in which it is superior to the others: the sword when in direct contact with the enemy, spear-thrusting when drawing near, and archery when the enemy is distant or when there is an intervening barrier, such as a river, a fortress, or the like. Whatever inflicts greater harm on the enemy and brings greater benefit to the Muslims is superior. This varies according to the enemy’s circumstances and those of the Muslims fighting against them. In some situations, archery is more useful; in others, spear-thrusting is more useful. This is something combatants know.

---

## Page 13604

Section

Learning these skills is a righteous deed for anyone who thereby seeks the Face of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Whoever teaches them to another shares in the reward of every act of jihad that person undertakes using them, without either person’s reward being diminished in the least—like one who recites the Quran and imparts knowledge. The learner must make his intention sincere and seek the Face of Allah Most High. The teacher must sincerely seek the learner’s good and strive diligently to teach him. The learner must acknowledge the respect due to his teacher and thank him for his kindness, for whoever does not thank people does not thank Allah. He must neither deny his teacher’s rights nor fail to acknowledge his kindness.

Teachers must cooperate in righteousness and piety, as the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, commanded when he said:

“A Muslim is a Muslim’s brother: he neither abandons him nor wrongs him.”

He also said:

“The believers, in their mutual love and compassion, are like a single body: when one limb suffers, the rest of the body responds with fever and sleeplessness.”

And he, peace and blessings be upon him, said:

“By Him in Whose hand is my soul, none of you believes until he wishes for his brother the good he wishes for himself.”

He also said:

“One believer is to another like a building, each part strengthening the others.” He then interlaced his fingers.

And he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “Do not envy one another

---

## Page 13605

nor sever ties with one another, nor hate one another, nor turn your backs on one another. Be brothers, O servants of Allah.” All these reports are found in the authentic collections.

The Sunan collections report that he, peace and blessings be upon him, said:

“Shall I tell you of something higher in rank than prayer, fasting, charity, enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong?”

They replied, “Yes, O Messenger of Allah.”

He said, “Mending relations between people, for discord is a razor. I do not say that it shaves off hair; rather, it shaves away religion.”

An authentic collection reports that he, peace and blessings be upon him, said:

“The gates of Paradise are opened every Monday and Thursday, and every servant who associates nothing with Allah is forgiven, except a man between whom and his brother there is enmity. It is then said, ‘Grant these two a reprieve until they reconcile.’”

He, peace and blessings be upon him, also said:

“It is not lawful for a Muslim to shun his brother for more than three days. They meet, and each turns away from the other. The better of the two is the one who offers the greeting of peace first.”

No teacher may wrong another or harm him unjustly through word or deed, for Allah Most High says:

“Those who harm believing men and women for something they have not done bear the guilt of slander and manifest sin.”

No one may punish another merely to satisfy his own desires, when that person has committed no injustice, transgressed no limit and neglected no right. This is among the injustices forbidden by Allah and His Messenger. For Allah Most High said, as narrated

---

## Page 13606

from Him by His Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him:

“O My servants, I have forbidden injustice for Myself and have made it forbidden among you, so do not wrong one another.”

If someone commits an offence, he may not be punished except with a punishment prescribed by Islamic law. No student, nor either of the two masters, may punish him however he wishes. Nor may anyone assist him or go along with him in doing so—for example, by obeying his order to shun someone who has committed no offence under Islamic law, or by saying, “I have sidelined him,” or “I have stripped him of standing,” or something similar. This resembles what priests and monks do among Christians, and what the hazābūn (Jewish religious authorities) do among Jews. It also resembles what leaders of misguidance and error do with their followers.

Al-Siddīq, the successor of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, in leading his community, said:

“Obey me so long as I obey Allah. If I disobey Allah, you owe me no obedience.”

The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said:

“No created being may be obeyed in disobedience to the Creator.”

He also said:

“If anyone commands you to disobey Allah, do not obey him.”

Thus, if a teacher or master orders someone to be shunned, stripped of standing, discredited, excluded, or treated similarly, the matter must be examined. If that person has committed an offence under Islamic law, he is to be punished in proportion to his offence, without excess. If he has committed no such offence, he may not be subjected to any punishment merely to serve the purposes of the teacher or anyone else. Teachers may not divide people into factions or do anything that sows enmity among them

---

## Page 13607

and hatred. Rather, they should be like brothers who cooperate in righteousness and piety, as Allah Most High says:

“Cooperate in righteousness and piety, but do not cooperate in sin and aggression.”

None of them may exact a pledge from anyone to agree with everything he wants, to befriend whomever he befriends, and to oppose whomever he opposes. Whoever does this is like Genghis Khan and others of his kind, who regard those who agree with them as friends and allies, and those who disagree with them as enemies and aggressors. Rather, they and their followers are bound by the covenant of Allah and His Messenger: to obey Allah and His Messenger, to do what Allah and His Messenger have commanded, to regard as forbidden what Allah and His Messenger have forbidden, and to respect teachers’ rights as Allah and His Messenger have commanded.

If someone’s master is wronged, he should support him. If his master is committing injustice, he must not assist him in it; rather, he should prevent him from doing so. As authentically reported from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, he said:

“Help your brother, whether he is an oppressor or oppressed.” He was asked, “O Messenger of Allah, I can help him when he is oppressed, but how can I help him when he is an oppressor?” He replied, “Prevent him from committing injustice; that is how you help him.”

If a dispute or quarrel arises between two teachers, two students, or a teacher and a student, no one may assist either party until he knows where the truth lies. He must not lend support out of ignorance or personal inclination. Rather, he should examine the matter, and once the truth becomes clear to him, support the party in the right against the party in the wrong, whether the one in the right belongs to his own circle or someone else’s, and whether the one in the wrong belongs to his own circle or someone else’s. The aim must be to worship Allah alone, obey His Messenger, follow the truth, and uphold justice. Allah Most High says:

“O you who

---

## Page 13608

believe, stand firmly for justice as witnesses for Allah, even against yourselves, your parents, or close relatives. Whether someone is rich or poor, Allah has a greater claim over both. So do not follow your desires, lest you depart from justice. If you distort your testimony or turn away, Allah is fully aware of what you do.”

To “twist one’s tongue” means to speak falsely. To “turn away” means to conceal the truth, for whoever remains silent about the truth is a mute devil. Whoever sides with his companion, whether his companion is right or wrong, has judged according to the judgment of pre-Islamic ignorance and departed from the judgment of Allah and His Messenger.

They must all stand united with the one in the right against the one in the wrong. They should honour those whom Allah and His Messenger have honoured, give precedence to those whom Allah and His Messenger have given precedence, love those whom Allah and His Messenger have loved, and hold in contempt those whom Allah and His Messenger have abased—all according to what pleases Allah and His Messenger, not according to personal desires. Whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger is rightly guided, while whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger harms only himself. This is the foundation upon which they must rely. There is then no need for division and factionalism among them, for Allah Most High says:

“Indeed, those who have divided their religion and become sects—you have nothing to do with them.”

And He Most High says:

“Do not be like those who became divided and differed after clear proofs had come to them.”

If a man has been taught by a teacher, he should appreciate the kindness his teacher has shown him and thank him. He must not gird his waist for either his teacher or anyone else, for girding one’s waist for a person

---

## Page 13609

in particular, and affiliating oneself with him—as mentioned in the question—are among the innovations of pre-Islamic ignorance. They resemble the alliances that the polytheists used to make and the division between Qays and Yaman. If the purpose of this girding and affiliation is cooperation in righteousness and piety, Allah and His Messenger have already commanded this for him and everyone else, without any such girding. If its purpose is cooperation in sin and aggression, Allah and His Messenger have forbidden it. Whatever good is intended by this, the command of Allah and His Messenger to do all that is right removes the need for the teachers’ commands in this regard. Whatever evil is intended by it, Allah and His Messenger have forbidden it.

A teacher may not bind his pupils to such an alliance, nor may anyone else take any of that teacher’s pupils and have them affiliate themselves with him in this innovated manner, whether from the outset or through imparting instruction. A pupil may not deny his first teacher’s rights over him, nor may the first teacher prevent anyone from benefiting by learning from someone else. The second teacher may not say, “Gird your waist for me and affiliate yourself with me rather than with your first teacher.” Rather, if someone learns from two teachers, he must respect the rights of both without partisan attachment to either the first or the second. If the first teacher has taught him more, he should give greater consideration to that teacher’s rights.

When they unite in obedience to Allah and His Messenger and cooperate in righteousness and piety, no one should side with another in everything. Rather, each person should support every other person in obedience to Allah and His Messenger, and they must not support anyone in disobedience to Allah and His Messenger. Instead, they should cooperate in truthfulness, justice, kindness, enjoining what is right and forbidding

---

## Page 13610

what is wrong, supporting the oppressed, and everything that Allah and His Messenger love. They must not cooperate in oppression, partisan loyalty of the pre-Islamic kind, following desires without guidance from Allah, division, or discord. Nor should anyone gird his waist for someone in order to follow him in everything, or enter into an alliance with him on any basis other than what Allah and His Messenger have commanded. In that case, no one transfers his allegiance from one teacher to another, nor does anyone affiliate himself under such labels as laqīt (foundling), thaqīl, or any other names of pre-Islamic ignorance.

These practices arose only because a teacher wants his pupil to agree with whatever he wishes, unconditionally befriending those whom he befriends and opposing those whom he opposes. This is forbidden: no one may command anyone to do it, nor may anyone comply with such a demand. Rather, the Sunnah unites them, and innovation divides them. Doing what Allah and His Messenger have commanded unites them, while disobedience to Allah and His Messenger separates them, so that people become either those who obey Allah or those who disobey Him. Worship must therefore be devoted to Allah alone, the Almighty and Majestic, and unconditional obedience is due only to Him, Glorified is He, and to His Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

There is no doubt that if they follow their pre-Islamic custom—whereby anyone taught by a teacher becomes his sworn ally—then someone who transfers from the first teacher to the second is acting unjustly and transgressing, breaking his covenant and proving untrustworthy in his commitments. This too is forbidden, and his sin is greater than that of someone who has not acted as he has. Indeed, if such a person transfers to someone other than his teacher and enters into an alliance with him, he has committed a forbidden act. He is thus like the flesh of a dead pig, for he has not

---

## Page 13611

fulfilled the covenant of Allah and His Messenger, nor his covenant with his first teacher. Rather, he is like someone who treats such matters as a game, having neither commitment to a covenant, nor religion, nor fidelity. In the pre-Islamic era, a man would enter into an alliance with a tribe, then, upon finding a stronger tribe, break his covenant with the first and ally himself with the second—much like the conduct of these people. So Allah Most High revealed:

“Do not break oaths after confirming them, having made Allah your guarantor. Indeed, Allah knows what you do.”

“Do not be like the woman who unravels her yarn into loose strands after spinning it firmly, using your oaths to deceive one another because one community is greater than another. Allah is only testing you through this, and on the Day of Resurrection He will surely make clear to you that over which you differed.”

“Had Allah willed, He would have made you one community, but He leaves astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills. And you will surely be questioned about what you used to do.”

“Do not use your oaths to deceive one another, lest a foot slip after being firmly planted, and you taste suffering for having turned people away from the path of Allah, and a tremendous punishment be yours.”

They must enjoin what is right upon one another and forbid one another from what is wrong. They must not allow anyone among them to openly commit injustice or indecency. Nor must they allow a beardless boy to flaunt his adornments or display anything that tempts people, to associate with anyone whose companionship is suspect, or to be honored for a corrupt purpose.

Anyone who enters into an alliance with another person on the condition that he befriend whomever that person befriends and oppose whomever he opposes is of the same kind as the Tatars who strive in the path of Satan. Such a person is neither among those who strive in the path of Allah Most High nor among the Muslim forces, and it is not permissible for

---

## Page 13612

such people to be part of the Muslim army. Rather, they belong to Satan’s army. It is, however, appropriate for a teacher to say to his pupil:

“You are bound by Allah’s covenant and pledge to be loyal to whoever is loyal to Allah and His Messenger, to oppose whoever opposes Allah and His Messenger, to cooperate in righteousness and piety, and not to cooperate in sin and aggression. If the truth is on my side, you must support the truth; but if I am in the wrong, you must not support falsehood.”

Whoever commits himself to this is among those who strive in the path of Allah Most High, seeking that all religion be devoted to Allah and that Allah’s word be supreme.

It is reported in the two collections of authentic hadith that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was asked:

“O Messenger of Allah, a man may fight out of bravery, partisan zeal, or a desire to show off. Which of these is in the path of Allah?”

He replied: “Whoever fights so that Allah’s word may be supreme is in the path of Allah.”

Thus, if a warrior fights out of partisan zeal for the Muslims, to show off before people so that they will praise him, or because of his own bravery, his fighting is not in the path of Allah, Almighty and Majestic, unless he fights so that Allah’s word may be supreme. What, then, of someone whose finest training in the art of combat is built on a corrupt foundation: helping one created being against another?

Whoever does this ranks among those steeped in pre-Islamic ignorance and the Tatars who depart from Islamic law. Such people deserve a severe punishment under Islamic law that deters them and others like them from such division and discord, until all religion is devoted to Allah and obedience is to Allah and His Messenger

---

## Page 13613

and they uphold justice, show loyalty for the sake of Allah and His Messenger, love for Allah’s sake, hate for Allah’s sake, enjoin what is right, and forbid what is wrong.

Teachers may request a fee from those whom they teach this art, for accepting payment and compensation for teaching it is permissible, and earning a living in this way is among the best forms of earning. If a pupil gives his teacher a gift on account of his instruction and gives him what he has obtained from competition prizes or other sources as compensation for teaching him, procuring equipment, and renting the premises, the teacher may accept it. Providing such compensation is among the best deeds. Indeed, Islamic law permits someone other than the two contestants to provide their prize money. Thus, if the ruler allocates money from the public treasury for contestants in archery, horse racing, and camel racing, this is permissible by agreement of the imams.

If a Muslim voluntarily provides prize money for such contests, he will be rewarded for doing so. Likewise, a man will be rewarded for what he gives someone who teaches him these skills. This is because these activities benefit Muslims generally; it is therefore permissible for individual Muslims to provide such compensation.

If both contestants contribute the prize money and a third, evenly matched competitor joins them as a muhallil—a contestant who contributes no stake and whose participation makes the arrangement lawful—this is permissible. If there is no such third contestant, but one of the two freely gives something, without being under any obligation to do so, using it to feed the group or giving it to the teacher or his fellow contestant, this is permissible.

---

## Page 13614

The underlying principle here is to understand that these activities assist jihad in Allah’s cause, whose purpose is that religion should be entirely for Allah and that Allah’s word should be supreme.

Religion rests on two principles: first, that we worship none but Allah Most High; and second, that we worship Him as He has prescribed, not through religious innovations. As Allah Most High says:

“To test you as to which of you is best in deeds.”

Al-Fudayl ibn ‘Iyād said: “The most sincere and the most correct.” He was asked: “What do you mean by the most sincere and the most correct?” He replied: “If a deed is sincere but not correct, it will not be accepted. If it is correct but not sincere, it will not be accepted either, until it is both sincere and correct. Sincerity means that it is done for Allah, and correctness means that it accords with the Sunnah.”

‘Umar ibn al-Khattāb used to say in his supplication: “O Allah, make all my deeds righteous, make them sincerely for Your sake, and let no one else have any share in them.”

This is the religion of Islam with which Allah sent His messengers and revealed His books: submission to Allah alone. Whoever does not submit to Him is too proud to worship Him. Allah Most High has said:

“Indeed, those who are too proud to worship Me will enter

---

## Page 13615

Hell in humiliation.” Whoever submits to Allah and to others besides Him associates partners with Him. Allah Most High has said:

“Indeed, Allah does not forgive associating partners with Him.”

Thus, Allah has a right in which no created being has any share: one must worship none but Allah, fear none but Allah, be mindful of Allah alone, put one’s trust in Allah alone, and call upon none but Allah. As Allah Most High says:

“So when you have finished, strive diligently, and turn your longing to your Lord.”

Allah Most High also says:

“Your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him.”

And Allah Most High says:

“Whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger, fears Allah and is mindful of Him—it is they who will triumph.”

Obedience, then, is owed to Allah and His Messenger, while reverent fear and mindfulness are for Allah alone.

Allah Most High says:

“If only they had been content with what Allah and His Messenger gave them and had said, ‘Allah is sufficient for us. Allah will give us of His bounty, and so will His Messenger. To Allah alone we turn in hope.’”

Thus, longing is directed to Allah alone, and Allah alone is relied upon as sufficient. Giving, however, is attributed to both Allah and His Messenger, as Allah Most High says:

“Whatever the Messenger gives you, take it; and whatever he forbids you, refrain from it.”

What he has made lawful is lawful; what he has forbidden is unlawful; and what he has prescribed is the religion. No shaykh, king, scholar, ruler, teacher, or any other created being may depart from this. Rather, all creation must follow the religion of Islam with which Allah sent His messengers. Through it, they must all embrace the religion of the Seal of the Messengers, the foremost of Adam’s descendants, the leader of the mindful, the best of creation and the most honoured of them before Allah: Muhammad, His servant and Messenger—may Allah’s blessings and abundant peace be upon him. Whenever anyone issues a command, whoever he may be, that command must be measured against

---

## Page 13616

the Book and the Sunnah; if it accords with them, it is accepted; otherwise, it is rejected. As reported from the Prophet—may Allah’s blessings and peace be upon him—in the two Sahīh collections, he said:

“Whoever performs a deed that does not accord with our teaching, it is rejected.”

That is, it is not accepted.

If, then, the conduct and statements of shaykhs and scholars include right and wrong, guidance and misguidance, sound judgment and error, and they must refer all of this to Allah and the Messenger, accepting what Allah and His Messenger accept and rejecting what Allah and His Messenger reject—how much more must teachers and others like them do so? Allah Most High has said:

“O you who believe, obey Allah and obey the Messenger and those in authority among you. If you disagree over anything, refer it to Allah and the Messenger, if you believe in Allah and the Last Day. That is best and leads to the best outcome.”

He Most High has also said:

“Mankind was one community. Then Allah sent the prophets as bearers of good tidings and warners, and sent down with them the Scripture in truth to judge between people concerning their differences. None differed over it except those who had been given it, after clear proofs had come to them, out of jealous animosity among themselves. Then Allah, by His permission, guided those who believed to the truth concerning which they had differed. And Allah guides whom He wills to a straight path.”

We therefore ask Allah Most High to guide us and all our brothers to His straight path—the path of those whom He has blessed: the prophets, the steadfastly truthful, the martyrs, and the righteous. What excellent companions they are! And Allah, glorified is He, knows best.

## Page 13617

He also said—may Allah be pleased with him:

“A soldier must be devout and courageous.”

Then he said:

“People fall into four categories: the highest are those who are both devout and courageous; then those who are devout but lack courage; then those who are courageous but lack devotion; and finally those who possess neither.”

He was asked about a man who was a soldier but wished to cease serving.

He replied:

“If the Muslims benefit from his service and he is capable of providing it, he should not abandon it unless doing so serves a greater interest of the Muslims. Rather, taking a leading role in jihad, which Allah and His Messenger love, is better than voluntary acts of worship, such as voluntary prayer, voluntary Hajj, and voluntary fasting. And Allah knows best.”

## Page 13618

He was also asked—may Allah have mercy on him:

“May a soldier wear anything of silk, gold, or silver in battle, or when enemy envoys come to the Muslims?”

He replied:

Praise be to Allah. Wearing silk in battle out of necessity is permissible by the agreement of the Muslims. This applies when nothing else can serve its purpose in deflecting weapons and providing protection.

As for wearing it to intimidate the enemy, the scholars hold two views. The stronger view is that it is permissible. The troops of Syria wrote to Umar ibn al-Khattāb: “When we encounter the enemy and see that they have covered their weapons”—meaning with silk—“we feel fear in our hearts because of it.” Umar wrote back to them: “You too should cover your weapons as they cover theirs.”

Moreover, wearing silk involves a display of pride, and Allah loves such a display during battle. As reported in the Sunan collections, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“There is a kind of pride that Allah loves and a kind that Allah hates. The pride that Allah loves is a man’s proud bearing in battle and when giving charity. As for the pride that Allah hates, it is pride expressed in transgression and boasting.”

“On the day of Uhud, Abū Dujāna walked proudly

---

## Page 13619

—he was one of the Ansār—between the two battle lines. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘That is a manner of walking which Allah hates, except in this situation.’”

As for a small amount of silk, such as a strip four fingers wide or the like, it is permissible in all circumstances. Scholars disagree concerning gold trim; the stronger view is that it too is permissible. For it is reported in the Sunan collections that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, “forbade gold except in small pieces.”

He was asked:

“About travel by a man with dependants …?” and so forth.

He replied:

As for travel by a man with dependants, if his journey would harm them, he must not travel. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“It is sufficient sin for a man to neglect those whom he supports.”

This applies whether they would be harmed through insufficient maintenance or because of their vulnerability. Travel in such circumstances is forbidden.

If they would suffer no harm, but would experience distress and a decline in their circumstances, then remaining with them is better, unless the journey offers a substantial benefit outweighing the reward of staying with them—such as knowledge he fears missing, or a shaykh whom it is necessary for him to meet. This, by my life, assumes that his intention in travelling is sound, making the journey religiously sanctioned.

But if his journey resembles that of many people, who travel merely out of restlessness and to pass the time, then remaining at home worshipping Allah is better for him in every case. Such a person needs

---

## Page 13620

to consult about his personal circumstances a man who understands his condition and what would benefit him, and who can be trusted in this matter. People’s circumstances differ greatly in such matters. And Allah, glorified and exalted is He, knows best.

He was asked:

“About days and nights—for example, someone saying that travel is disliked on Wednesday, Thursday or Saturday; that cutting fabric, sewing or spinning is disliked on these days; or that intercourse is disliked on a particular night, for fear of harm to the child?”

He replied:

All praise is due to Allah. All of this is false and has no basis. Rather, when a man has sought Allah’s guidance concerning a permissible act, let him do it whenever it is convenient. Cutting fabric, sewing, spinning and similar activities are not disliked on any day, nor is intercourse disliked on any night or day.

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, forbade belief in ill omens, as recorded in the Sahīh from Mu‘āwiya ibn al-Hakam al-Sulamī, who said:

“I said, ‘O Messenger of Allah, some of us visit soothsayers.’

“He said, ‘Then do not visit them.’

“I said, ‘Some of us take things as ill omens.’

“He said, ‘That is something one of you feels within himself, but it must not deter you.’”

Since he forbade a person to let an ill omen deter him from what he had resolved to do, how, then, could particular days and nights be grounds for such avoidance?

A Letter from Shaykh al-Islām—May Allah Sanctify His Soul—to His Companions While He Was Imprisoned in Alexandria

He said:

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

“And proclaim the blessings of your Lord.”

What I wish to tell the brethren—may Allah be gracious to them in this world and the Hereafter, and perfect His outward and inward blessings upon them—is that, by Allah the Magnificent, besides whom there is no god, I am enjoying blessings from Allah unlike any I have experienced in my entire life. Allah, glorified and exalted is He, has opened doors of His bounty and blessing, and treasures of His generosity and mercy, that had never entered my mind or crossed my imagination—things beyond the reach of sight. Allah Most High has made them accessible, until they have become places of repose. Those who have some share in knowing Allah, affirming His oneness, understanding the realities of faith, and possessing the knowledge and faith sought by the earliest and latest generations know something of these blessings through direct experience.

## Page 13622

For delight, joy, happiness, the sweetness of life, and indescribable bliss are found only in knowing Allah, glorified and exalted is He, affirming His oneness, believing in Him, and having the realities of faith and the insights of the Quran opened to one. As one of the shaykhs said: “I once experienced a state in which I said: ‘If the people of Paradise experience this, they certainly enjoy a good life.’” Another said: “There are times when the heart dances for joy.” No bliss in this world resembles the bliss of the Hereafter except the bliss of faith and knowing Allah.

This is why the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to say:

“Give us rest through prayer, O Bilāl.”

He did not say, “Give us rest from it,” as those who find prayer burdensome say. As Allah Most High says:

“And indeed, it is difficult except for the humbly submissive.”

Humble submission means submitting to Allah Most High and finding calm and tranquillity in Him, in both heart and limb.

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, also used to say:

“Women and perfume have been made dear to me from your world.”

Then he would say:

“And my deepest joy has been placed in prayer.”

He did not say, “Three things from your world have been made dear to me,” as some people attribute to the Prophet. Rather, Imām Ahmad and al-Nasā’ī narrated it as given above: what was made dear to him from this world was women and perfume. As for the deepest joy, it comes from attaining what one seeks, and that is found in prayer.

Hearts are troubled by the whisperings of the self, while Satan urges desires and doubts that spoil the sweetness of their life. Whoever loves something other than Allah is tormented in this world

---

## Page 13623

and the Hereafter; if he attains what he desires, he is tormented by it; if he does not, he remains in torment, regret, and sorrow. Hearts find neither joy nor complete delight except in loving Allah and drawing near to Him through what He loves. Loving Him is possible only by turning away from everything loved besides Him. This is the reality of “None has the right to be worshipped but Allah.” It is the way of Abraham, Allah’s close friend—peace be upon him—and of all the other prophets and messengers, may Allah’s blessings and peace be upon them all.

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to tell his Companions:

“Say: ‘We begin this morning upon the natural disposition of Islam, the declaration of sincere devotion to Allah, the religion of our Prophet Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and the way of our father Abraham, upright in faith, submitting to Allah, and not one of those who associate partners with Him.’”

The early generations explained the term hanīf in three ways. Muhammad ibn Kaʿb said: “Upright.” ʿAtā’ said: “Sincere.” Others said: “A follower.” Thus, a hanīf is one whose heart is directed steadfastly towards Allah alone, and not towards anything besides Him. Allah Most High says:

“So take a straight course to Him and seek His forgiveness. And woe to those who associate partners with Him.”

He also says:

“Indeed, those who have said, ‘Our Lord is Allah,’ and then remained steadfast.”

Abū Bakr al-Siddīq, may Allah be pleased with him, said: “They did not turn away from Him, either to the right or to the left.” They did not turn their hearts towards anything besides Him, whether in love, fear, hope, supplication, or reliance. Rather, they love Allah alone and do not love rivals alongside Him. They love none but Him, not to obtain some benefit or ward off some harm. They fear no one besides Him, whoever it may be; they ask none but Him, nor do they look expectantly

---

## Page 13624

in their hearts to anyone besides Him. This is why the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said to ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him:

“Whatever comes to you of this wealth without your asking for it or looking expectantly for it, take it; but do not let your soul pursue what does not come to you.”

The one who asks does so with his tongue, while the one who looks expectantly does so in his heart. This hadith is agreed upon as authentic.

Abū Saʿīd reported that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Whoever seeks to refrain from asking, Allah will enable him to refrain; whoever seeks independence from others, Allah will grant him independence; and whoever is patient, Allah will grant him patience.”

This hadith is agreed upon as authentic. Thus, true wealth lies in the heart, as the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Wealth does not lie in having many possessions; rather, true wealth is richness of soul.”

The self-restrained person is one who does not ask with his tongue for either aid or provision. Allah Most High says:

An authentic hadith states:

“It is they who will have security, and they are rightly guided.”

That is, those who sincerely affirm Allah’s oneness. This is why Imam Ahmad said to someone: “If you set yourself right, you would fear no one.”

He, glorified and exalted is He, informs us that what the messengers and prophets—may Allah’s blessings and peace be upon them all—brought inevitably has enemies: devils from mankind and jinn who whisper embellished words. ## Page 13631

but if something contrary to his desires befalls him, he turns back, having worshipped Allah on an edge. An “edge” is a side, like the edge of a loaf or a mountain, where one has no firm footing.

“If good befalls him”—in this world—“he is content with it; but if a trial befalls him”—meaning an ordeal by which he is tested—“he turns back on his face, losing both this world and the Hereafter. That is the clear loss.”

The edge of a mountain affords no firm footing. The meaning is that he loses this world through the ordeal that befalls him, and loses the Hereafter by turning back from the religion.

“He calls upon, besides Allah, that which cannot harm him”—to the end of the verse.

That is, he calls upon created beings, fearing them and placing his hopes in them, although they have no power to harm or benefit him. Indeed, their harm is nearer than their benefit. Even if the occasion of its revelation concerned a particular individual who embraced Islam after having been a polytheist, its ruling applies generally to everyone encompassed by its wording and meaning until the Day of Resurrection. Thus, whoever calls upon anyone other than Allah is a polytheist. Direct observation bears this out: when a person complains to created beings, their harm is nearer than their benefit.

As for the Creator—majestic is His glory, holy are His names, and there is no god but Him—when a created being complains to Him, lays his needs before Him, and seeks His forgiveness for his sins, He supports and strengthens him, guides him, meets his needs, enriches him, draws him near, grants him contentment, loves him, and chooses him.

But when a servant lays his needs before a created being, that being considers him contemptible, looks down on him, and then turns away from him. The servant loses this world and the Hereafter, even if the other grants some of what he seeks, for he regards the servant as one of his subjects, enslaving him to serve his own desires.

Allah’s intimate friend, may the finest blessings and peace be upon him, said:

and give thanks to Him. To Him you will be returned.”

This is a vast subject about which I have written extensively, and which I have come to know through knowledge, inward experience, and practical experience.

Section

In short, the blessings Allah has bestowed upon me while I am in this place are greater in worth and more numerous than any account can convey. What I miss most is my companions. I wish for them to attain such pleasure, joy, and bliss as will delight their eyes, and to have such opportunities opened to them for knowing Allah, obeying Him, and striving in His cause that they may reach the highest ranks.

I make the value of this known to most people, though it can only be truly known through direct experience and inward feeling. Yet every believer has some share of it, and from the little he experiences he can infer the abundance beyond it, even if he cannot appreciate its immense worth.

I know the conditions of people, their various kinds, and their pleasures. Yet how can pearls compare with dung? How can fālūdhaj (a sweet confection) compare with syrup? How can angels compare with a beast—or beasts? But I know that the wisdom of

---

## Page 13633

Allah, His wise choice, His kindness, and His mercy require that everyone should seek to worship Allah and strive in His cause, through knowledge and action according to his ability, so that all devotion is to Allah and his aim is for Allah’s word to be supreme. His love, hatred, enmity, praise, and blame should be solely for Allah—not for any particular person.

The guide in the fullest sense—who guides to every good and whose guidance everyone needs at all times—is Allah’s Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. The best of his community are those who follow him most closely. This is achieved through faith, certainty, and striving, as Allah Most High says:

“The believers are only those who believe in Allah and His Messenger, then never doubt,”

up to His words:

“It is they who are the truthful.”

Thus Allah, glorified and exalted be He, explains that a believer must possess three things:

First: to believe in Allah and His Messenger.

Second: not to doubt thereafter—that is, to remain certain and steadfast.

Certainty is the opposite of doubt, and doubt is of two kinds: uncertainty arising from insufficient knowledge, and agitation within the heart. Both arise from a deficiency in one’s state of faith. Faith necessarily requires knowledge within the heart, and not in every place does one have knowledge that one understands. It also requires the heart’s action, or its insight, steadfastness, reassurance, tranquillity, reliance upon Allah, sincerity, and turning to Allah Most High. All these matters are mentioned in the Quran.

One says: “Such-and-such disquieted me

---

## Page 13634

—it disquiets me”—that is, it stirred my heart. This usage also occurs in the hadith reporting that Allah’s Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, passed by a gazelle lying curled up and said, “Let no one disturb it”—meaning, let no one cause it to move. Likewise, he said:

“Leave what makes you uneasy for what does not make you uneasy.”

For truthfulness brings tranquillity, while falsehood brings unease. The truthful person’s heart is not agitated, whereas the liar’s heart is agitated. This is not a matter of doubt; rather, it is clear that disquiet is broader in meaning than doubt.

Hence the transmitted supplication:

“O Allah, grant us such fear of You as will come between us and disobedience to You”—and so on to the end of the hadith.

In al-Musnad and al-Tirmidhī, Abū Bakra, may Allah be pleased with him, is reported to have said:

“Ask Allah for certainty and well-being, for nothing better than certainty and well-being has been granted. So ask Allah, glorified and exalted be He, for them.”

The Arabs use the expression mā’ yaqin (still water) when water is calm and motionless. Thus the believer’s heart is tranquil, free of disquiet. This is the meaning of His words, glorified and exalted be He:

“The believers are only those who believe in Allah and His Messenger, then never doubt, and strive with their wealth and their lives in Allah’s cause. It is they who are the truthful.”

In the two Sahīh collections, Sa‘d ibn Abī Waqqās, may Allah be pleased with him, said:

“Allah’s Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, gave to a group of men but gave nothing to a man who was dearer to me than they were. I said, ‘O Messenger of Allah, why have you passed over so-and-so? By Allah, I consider him a believer.’ He said, ‘Or a Muslim,’ twice or three times. Then he said, ‘I may give to a man although another is dearer to me than he is, for fear that Allah might cast him face down into the Fire.’”

For this reason, Abū Ja‘far al-Bāqir and others among the early generations said: Islam is a circle

---

## Page 13635

that is large, while faith is a circle within it. When a servant commits unlawful sexual intercourse, he passes from faith into Islam. As reported in the two Sahīh collections, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“No one who commits unlawful sexual intercourse is a believer while committing it; no thief is a believer while stealing; and no one who drinks wine is a believer while drinking it.”

The stronger of the two scholarly views is that these Bedouins who said, “We have submitted,” and other Muslims like them, whose hearts have not yet admitted the faith described above, are rewarded for their righteous deeds. As Allah Most High says:

“If you obey Allah and His Messenger, He will not diminish the reward of your deeds in the least.”

They are neither disbelievers nor hypocrites. Rather, they have not attained the reality and completeness of faith. Thus, what is denied them is the obligatory completeness of faith, although they are included under the designation of faith in such passages as His words:

“Then the freeing of a believing slave,”

and His words:

“O you who believe, when you rise to pray, wash your faces and your hands.”

This is an extensive subject. The purpose here is to inform the brethren that Allah’s blessings upon us are far, far greater than before. Praise be to Allah, His blessings upon us continue to increase. Though I cannot serve the brethren by meeting with them, I pray for them night and day, fulfilling some of what I owe them and seeking nearness to Allah Most High by dealing with them for His sake.

What I enjoin upon each of them is to fear Allah and work for Allah, seeking Allah’s help and striving in His cause, with the aim that

I write to you amid immense blessings from Allah, gracious favors, and abundant bounties, for which we thank Allah and ask Him for more of His grace. Allah’s blessings continue to grow and increase, and His favors are beyond counting.

## Page 13642

And you know that in this affair Allah, glorified be He, has bestowed blessings that provide means for the triumph of His religion, the supremacy of His word, victory for His hosts, honour for His allies, strength for the adherents of the Sunnah and communal unity, and humiliation for the adherents of innovation and division. These blessings have consolidated what was already established among you of the Sunnah and brought further gains: opening doors of guidance, victory, and clear evidence; making the truth manifest to multitudes whose number none but Allah Most High can count; and drawing people towards the path of the Sunnah and communal unity. These and other blessings require profound gratitude and patient perseverance, even though it is perseverance in prosperity.

You also know that among the great principles that encompass the religion are bringing hearts together, uniting people, and setting relations right. Allah Most High says:

And He says:

There are many other texts like these that command unity and harmony and forbid division and discord. Those who uphold this principle are the people of unity, just as those who depart from it are the people of division.

The essence of the Sunnah is obedience to the Messenger. Thus the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said in

## Page 13643

the authentic hadith narrated by Muslim in his Sahīh on the authority of Abū Hurayrah:

“Allah is pleased with three things for you: that you worship Him without associating anything with Him; that you hold firmly to the rope of Allah all together and do not become divided; and that you sincerely advise those whom Allah has placed in charge of your affairs.”

The Sunan collections also relate, on the authority of Zayd ibn Thābit and Ibn Mas‘ūd—two jurists among the Companions—that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“May Allah make radiant the face of someone who hears a hadith from us and conveys it to someone who has not heard it. Many a bearer of religious knowledge lacks understanding, and many a bearer of such knowledge conveys it to someone who understands it better than he does. There are three things towards which a Muslim’s heart harbours no resentment: devoting one’s deeds sincerely to Allah, sincerely advising those in authority, and remaining with the Muslim community, for their call encompasses those beyond them.”

His words, “harbours no resentment,” mean that the heart bears no rancour towards these qualities. A Muslim’s heart does not hate them; rather, it loves and approves of them.

The first matter I shall address under this principle is what concerns me personally. You know—may Allah be pleased with you—that I do not wish any Muslim whatsoever, let alone any of our companions, to suffer harm of any kind, inwardly or outwardly. Nor do I bear any grievance against any of them or blame them at all. Rather, my honour, esteem, love and reverence for them are many times greater than before, each according to his due; and inevitably

---

## Page 13644

a person is either one who strives to reach the right judgment and succeeds, one who strives but errs, or one who sins.

The first is rewarded and deserves appreciation. The second, besides being rewarded for his effort, is pardoned and forgiven. As for the third, may Allah forgive us, him and all the believers.

Let us therefore put an end to any talk contrary to this principle, such as saying: “So-and-so fell short; so-and-so did nothing; so-and-so caused the shaykh to suffer harm; so-and-so was the cause of this affair; so-and-so was talking about plotting against so-and-so,” and similar remarks that disparage some of our companions and brothers. I will not excuse anyone who harms them in this way. There is neither might nor power except through Allah. Rather, such talk brings blame upon the speaker himself, unless he has some good deed to his credit and is among those whom Allah forgives, if He wills. Allah has pardoned what is past.

You also know that any severity or harshness shown towards some of our companions and brothers—whether what used to occur in Damascus or what has now occurred in Egypt—neither diminishes nor detracts from the standing of the person concerned. Nor has it caused any change in our feelings towards him or any hatred. Rather, after being treated with such severity and harshness, he is held in higher esteem, enjoys greater recognition, and is more beloved and more honoured. These matters serve the believers’ welfare: through them Allah sets some believers right by means of others. For one believer is to another like two hands, each washing the other. And it may not

## Page 13646

and the more extreme case to illustrate the less extreme—I say:

I love goodness for all Muslims and desire for every believer the good that I desire for myself. Those who lied and acted unjustly are absolved of any claim on my part. As for Allah’s rights, if they repent, Allah will accept their repentance; otherwise, Allah’s judgment will take effect upon them.

If a person could be thanked for his wrongdoing, I would thank everyone who played a part in bringing about this affair, because of the good that results from it in this world

## Page 13649

And what Satan’s party sought was not merely to oppose the law of Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, but to oppose the religion of all the messengers: Abraham, Moses, the Messiah, and Muhammad, the Seal of the Prophets—may Allah bless them all.

They had sought to prevent any address or writing from emerging from the party of Allah and His Messenger, and they were alarmed by the appearance of al-Ikhnā’iyyah. Yet Allah Most High used them to bring to light many times as much, and something far greater. He compelled them to scrutinize and study it. Their purpose was to expose its faults and find arguments they could use against it, but they found nothing in it except evidence against themselves. Their ignorance, falsehood and inability became apparent to them, and this became widely known throughout the land. This is something that only Allah could bring about.

They could not expose any fault in our position concerning religious law or faith. The most they could claim was that a decree issued by a created being had been contravened. Yet any created being, whoever he may be, who opposes the command of Allah Most High and His Messenger must not be obeyed in that opposition. Such obedience is not merely unnecessary; it is impermissible, by the agreement of the Muslims.

As for someone’s claim that “he propagates religious innovations,” its falsity is apparent to anyone with discernment, who knows that the opposite is true. Someone who propagates an innovation does so either because he does not know the Messenger’s Sunnah or because he has an ulterior motive or desire that conflicts with it. Yet he is more deserving of being charged with ignorance of the Messenger’s Sunnah and following desires without guidance from Allah—

“And who is more astray than one who follows his own desires without guidance from Allah?”

—than those who know the Messenger’s Sunnah better than they do and are further removed from desires and ulterior motives that lead to opposing it.

## Page 13652

To proceed, this is:

“A Principle Concerning Hisbah (Enjoining Right and Forbidding Wrong)”

The foundation of this subject is to understand that all offices of authority in Islam aim to ensure that religion is devoted entirely to Allah and that Allah’s word is supreme. For this purpose Allah, glorified and exalted, created His creatures, revealed the Scriptures, and sent the messengers; and for this the Messenger and the believers strove.

Allah Most High says:

“I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me.”

He also says:

“We never sent a messenger before you without revealing to him: ‘There is no god but Me, so worship Me.’”

And He says:

“We certainly sent a messenger to every nation, saying: ‘Worship Allah and shun false gods.’”

He has told us that every messenger said to his people:

“Worship Allah; you have no god other than Him.”

Worshipping Him consists in obeying Him and obeying His Messenger. This is goodness, righteousness, piety, good deeds, acts that draw one near to Allah, enduring deeds, righteous deeds, and righteous action—although there are subtle distinctions between these terms that are beyond the scope of this discussion.

It is for this that people fight, as Allah Most High says:

“Fight them until there is no more fitnah and religion is devoted entirely to Allah.”

And in the two Sahīh collections, it is related from Abū Mūsā

---

## Page 13653

al-Ash'arī, may Allah be pleased with him, who said:

“The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was asked about a man who fights out of bravery, another who fights out of partisan zeal, and another who fights for show: ‘Which of these is fighting in Allah’s cause?’ He replied: ‘Whoever fights so that Allah’s word is supreme is fighting in Allah’s cause.’”

The welfare of all the children of Adam, both in this world and in the Hereafter, can only be secured through association, cooperation, and mutual support. They cooperate and support one another in securing benefits, and support one another in warding off harms. Hence the saying: “Man is by nature a social being.”

When people come together, they must undertake certain actions to secure their welfare and avoid others because of the harm they entail. They must obey whoever commands them to pursue those aims and forbids those harmful things. Thus, all the children of Adam must obey someone who issues commands and prohibitions. Those who follow neither revealed scriptures nor any religion obey their kings in whatever they believe will serve their worldly interests, sometimes judging correctly and sometimes incorrectly.

The followers of corrupt religions—among the polytheists and the People of the Book who continue to adhere to their scripture after its alteration, or after its abrogation and alteration—obey in whatever they believe will serve their religious and worldly interests. Among those who are not People of the Book, some believe in recompense after death, while others do not. As for the People of the Book, they all agree that there is recompense after death. Yet all the peoples of the earth agree on recompense in this world, for people have never disagreed about

---

## Page 13654

the fact that injustice leads to a dire outcome, whereas justice leads to an honorable one. Hence it is related:

“Allah supports a just state even if it is unbelieving, but does not support an unjust state even if it is believing.”

Since obedience to someone who commands and forbids is inevitable, it is clear that a person is better served by obeying Allah and His Messenger—the unlettered Prophet written of in the Torah and the Gospel, who enjoins what is right, forbids what is wrong, makes good things lawful for them, and forbids them impure things. Such obedience is obligatory upon all creation. Allah Most High says:

“We sent no messenger except to be obeyed by Allah’s permission. If, when they wronged themselves, they had come to you and sought Allah’s forgiveness, and the Messenger had sought forgiveness for them, they would have found Allah ever Accepting of repentance, Most Merciful.”

“But no, by your Lord, they will not believe until they make you judge in their disputes, then find within themselves no resistance to your judgment and submit wholeheartedly.”

He also says:

“Whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger will be with those whom Allah has blessed: the prophets, the steadfastly truthful, the martyrs, and the righteous. What excellent companions they are!”

He also says:

“Whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger, He will admit them into Gardens beneath which rivers flow, to abide therein forever. That is the supreme triumph.”

“But whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger and oversteps His limits, He will admit him into a Fire, to abide therein forever, and he will suffer a humiliating punishment.”

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to say in his Friday sermon:

“Indeed, the best speech is Allah’s speech; the best guidance is Muhammad’s guidance; and the worst of matters

---

## Page 13655

are newly introduced matters.”

He would also say in the sermon of need:

“Whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger has followed right guidance, while whoever disobeys them harms only himself and will not harm Allah in the least.”

Allah sent His Messenger Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, with the finest ways and laws, and revealed to him the finest of Books. He sent him to the best community ever raised up for mankind, perfected the religion for him and his community, and completed His favor upon them. He forbade Paradise to all except those who believe in him and what he brought, and accepts from no one anything other than the Islam he brought. Whoever seeks a religion other than it will never have it accepted from him, and in the Hereafter he will be among the losers.

He stated in His Book that He sent down the Book and iron so that people might uphold justice. Allah Most High says:

“We certainly sent Our messengers with clear proofs and sent down with them the Book and the balance so that people might uphold justice. And We sent down iron, in which there is mighty power and benefits for people, so that Allah may know who supports Him and His messengers without seeing Him. Indeed, Allah is All-Strong, Almighty.”

For this reason, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, commanded his community to appoint rulers over them. He commanded those in authority to return trusts to their rightful owners and, when judging between people, to judge with justice. He also commanded the people to obey those in authority in matters of obedience to Allah Most High. Thus, in the Sunan of Abū Dāwūd, Abū Sa‘īd reports that the Messenger of Allah

---

## Page 13656

may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“When three people set out on a journey, let them appoint one of them as their leader.”

Abū Dāwūd also relates the same in his Sunan from Abū Hurayrah.

In the Musnad of Imam Ahmad, ‘Abdullāh ibn ‘Umar reports that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“It is not lawful for three people to be in an open wilderness without appointing one of them as their leader.”

Since he made it obligatory to appoint one of their number as leader even in the smallest groups and the briefest gatherings, this indicates that doing so is obligatory in larger gatherings. Thus, holding authority—for someone who undertakes it as an act of devotion through which he draws near to Allah and fulfills its duties to the best of his ability—is among the finest righteous deeds. Indeed, Imam Ahmad relates in his Musnad that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“The most beloved of creation to Allah is a just ruler, and the most hated of creation to Allah is an unjust ruler.”

Section

Since the essence of religion and of all offices of authority lies in commanding and forbidding, the commanding with which Allah sent His Messenger is enjoining what is right, and the forbidding with which He sent him is forbidding what is wrong. This is a characteristic of the Prophet and the believers, as Allah Most High says:

“The believing men and believing women are allies of one another. They enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong.”

This is obligatory upon every Muslim who is able. It is a collective obligation, and it becomes

---

## Page 13657

an individual obligation upon anyone capable of fulfilling it when no one else undertakes it. Ability lies in power and authority: those who possess authority are more capable than others, and their obligations are correspondingly greater. The basis of obligation is ability, so each person is obligated according to their ability. Allah Most High says:

“So fear Allah as much as you are able.”

The sole purpose of all Islamic offices of authority is to enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong. This applies equally to higher military offices, such as serving as the sultan’s deputy; lower military offices, such as command of the police; judicial office; financial administration, namely oversight of the financial bureaus; and the office of public oversight.

Some officeholders, however, occupy the position of a trusted witness, whose duty is truthfulness. Examples include witnesses before a judge; the official responsible for a financial bureau, whose duty is to record revenue collected and expenditure; and the group representative and headman, whose duty is to inform the person in authority about prevailing conditions. Others occupy the position of a trustee whose commands are obeyed, and whose duty is justice, such as the commander, the judge, and the official responsible for public oversight.

Truthfulness in all reports and justice in what is enacted through words and deeds set all affairs right. These two go hand in hand, as Allah Most High says:

“And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled in truth and in justice.”

When mentioning unjust rulers, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Whoever accepts their lies as true and assists them in

---

## Page 13658

their injustice is not of me, nor am I of him, and he will not come to me at the Cistern. Whoever does not accept their lies as true and does not assist them in their injustice is of me, and I am of him; he will come to the Cistern.”

In the two Sahīh collections, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, is reported to have said:

“Adhere to truthfulness, for truthfulness leads to righteousness, and righteousness leads to Paradise. A man continues to speak the truth and diligently pursue truthfulness until he is recorded with Allah as thoroughly truthful. Beware of lying, for lying leads to wickedness, and wickedness leads to the Fire. A man continues to lie and diligently pursue falsehood until he is recorded with Allah as a persistent liar.”

Hence Allah, Glorified and Exalted, says:

“Shall I inform you upon whom the devils descend? They descend upon every sinful liar.”

He also says:

“We will surely seize him by the forelock—a lying, sinful forelock.”

Thus, everyone in authority must seek the assistance of truthful and just people. If that is not possible, he should seek the assistance of the best available, in order of merit, even if they have some dishonesty and injustice. For Allah supports this religion through a wicked man and through people who have no share of good. What is obligatory is only to do what is within one’s ability.

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, or ‘Umar ibn al-Khattāb, said:

“Whoever appoints a man over a group when he can find among them someone more pleasing to Allah has betrayed Allah, betrayed His Messenger, and betrayed the believers.”

What is required, then, is to choose the one most pleasing to Allah from among those available; generally, there is no

---

## Page 13659

perfect candidate; one must therefore pursue the better of two good courses and avert the worse of two evils. Hence ‘Umar ibn al-Khattāb used to say:

“To You I complain of the vigor of the wicked and the incapacity of the trustworthy.”

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and his Companions would rejoice at the victory of the Romans and Christians over the Magians, although both sides were unbelievers, because one group was closer to Islam. Allah revealed Surah al-Rūm concerning this when the Romans and Persians fought; the account is well known. Likewise, Joseph served as deputy to the Pharaoh of Egypt, though Pharaoh and his people were polytheists. Joseph established as much justice and goodness as he could and called them to faith to the extent possible.

Section

The general or restricted scope of public offices, and the authority an officeholder derives from his appointment, are determined by the wording used, the circumstances, and customary practice. Islamic law prescribes no fixed scope for these. Thus, in some places and periods, the jurisdiction of judges may include matters that fall under military and executive authority elsewhere or at another time, and vice versa. The same applies to hisba (public oversight) and financial administration.

All these offices are, in principle, forms of authority sanctioned by Islamic law and religious positions. Whoever acts justly in any of them, administering it with knowledge and justice and obeying Allah and His Messenger to the extent possible, is among the righteous and upright; whereas anyone who acts unjustly

---

## Page 13660

and administers it in ignorance is among the wicked and unjust. The governing criterion is simply Allah’s statement:

“Indeed, the righteous will be in bliss.”

“And indeed, the wicked will be in Hellfire.”

Accordingly, under the present conventions in these lands of Syria and Egypt, military and executive authority has particular responsibility for carrying out prescribed punishments involving death or permanent bodily injury, such as amputating a thief’s hand, punishing brigands, and the like. Its jurisdiction may also include punishments that do not involve such injury, such as flogging a thief. It also includes adjudicating disputes, physical altercations, and matters giving rise to suspicion where there is neither documentary evidence nor witnesses. Judicial authority, by contrast, has particular responsibility for matters involving documentary evidence and witnesses, establishing rights and adjudicating such cases, and overseeing the administrators of endowments, the guardians of orphans, and other familiar duties.

In other lands, such as the Maghrib, the military governor has no adjudicative authority at all; he merely implements the orders of the judge. This follows the earlier practice. The reasons for these differences, rooted in legal schools and customary practices, are discussed elsewhere.

As for the public-oversight officer, his responsibility is to enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong in matters that do not fall within the exclusive jurisdiction of governors, judges, administrative officials, and the like. Many religious matters are shared responsibilities among those in authority. Whoever fulfils the required duty in any such matter must be obeyed in it. Thus, the public-oversight officer must instruct the public to perform the five daily prayers at their appointed times and punish those who do not pray with beating and imprisonment; execution, however, falls under another official’s authority. He must also oversee the prayer leaders and callers to prayer;

---

## Page 13661

and if any of them neglects the duties of leading prayer or departs from the prescribed call to prayer, he must require him to comply. In matters beyond his capacity, he must seek assistance from those holding military and judicial authority. Everyone whose authority is obeyed must also assist in this.

For “prayer” is the foremost of righteous deeds, the pillar of Islam, and the greatest of its prescribed observances. It is paired with the two testimonies of faith. Allah made it obligatory on the night of the Ascension, addressing the Messenger directly, without an intermediary; He did not send an angelic messenger with it.
