## Page 13801

to intercede, by His abundant mercy, as is established in numerous reports of the Sunnah from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Allah, Glorified and Exalted is He, knows best. O Allah, bless Muhammad and all his family and Companions.

He also said—may Allah have mercy on him:

Section

In the questions recorded by Ishāq ibn Mansūr—which al-Khallāl also cited in his Book of the Sunnah, in the chapter on avoiding those who say that the Quran is created—Ishāq reports that he said to Abū Abd Allāh:

“What of someone who says, ‘The Quran is created’?”

He replied: “Attribute every evil to him.”

I said: “Should one openly show enmity towards them, or deal tactfully with them?”

He replied: “The people of Khurāsān are no match for them.”

This reply of his, together with his statement concerning the Qadariyyah—“If we were to abandon transmitting reports from the Qadariyyah, we would have to abandon transmitting from most of the people of Basra”—and his treatment of them during the inquisition, responding in the best manner and addressing them with proofs, explains his statements and actions concerning shunning them and forbidding others to sit or converse with them. Indeed, at another time he even shunned certain eminent figures and ordered that they be shunned because of some form of Jahmī belief.

---

## Page 13802

For shunning is a form of disciplinary punishment, and punishment is a form of abandonment—that is, abandoning evil deeds. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“The emigrant is one who abandons evil deeds.”

He also said:

“One who abandons what Allah has forbidden.”

This is abandonment as an expression of piety. Shunning as a disciplinary measure and a form of jihad includes the shunning of the three who were left behind: he ordered the Muslims to shun them until Allah accepted their repentance.

Thus, abandonment is sometimes an expression of piety, when it consists of abandoning evil deeds. As Allah Most High said:

“When you see those who engage in offensive discourse about Our verses, turn away from them until they turn to another subject. And if Satan causes you to forget, then after remembering, do not sit with the wrongdoing people.”

“Those who fear Allah are not accountable for them in any way, but must remind them, so that perhaps they may fear Him.”

He, Glorified is He, thus made clear that the God-fearing are distinct from the wrongdoers, and that those commanded to leave gatherings where people engage in offensive discourse about Allah’s verses are the God-fearing.

At other times, shunning is a form of jihad, enjoining right and forbidding wrong, and enforcing the prescribed legal penalties. It constitutes punishment of someone who has transgressed and committed wrongdoing. Punishing and disciplining a wrongdoer is conditional upon having the ability to do so.

For this reason, the religious ruling concerning these two forms of abandonment differs according to whether one has the ability or lacks it, and whether wrongful innovators are few or many, strong or weak. The ruling similarly varies according to these factors in all other forms of wrongdoing, including disbelief, wickedness, and disobedience. Everything Allah has forbidden is wrongdoing, whether it infringes solely upon Allah’s rights, upon the rights of His servants, or upon both.

The abandonment He has commanded—whether through abstaining and desisting, or through shunning as punishment and discipline—applies only when it involves no benefit

---

## Page 13803

of religious significance that outweighs the harm of performing the act. Otherwise, if an evil deed contains an outweighing good, it is not evil. If punishment entails harm greater than that of the crime, it is not good; rather, it is evil. If the harms are equal, it is neither good nor evil.

Thus, abandonment may aim at avoiding the evil of religious innovation, which constitutes wrongdoing, sin, transgression, and corruption. Alternatively, shunning may aim at the good of jihad, forbidding wrong, and punishing wrongdoers so that they are deterred and restrained, and so that faith and righteous deeds are strengthened among those who uphold them.

Punishing a wrongdoer deters people from committing his wrongdoing and encourages them to pursue its opposite: faith, the Sunnah, and the like. If shunning him neither deters anyone nor causes anyone to desist, but instead prevents many commanded good deeds from being performed, then such shunning is not commanded. This is what Ahmad mentioned concerning the people of Khurāsān at that time: they lacked the strength to stand against the Jahmiyyah. When they were unable to show hostility towards them, the command to perform this good deed ceased to apply. Dealing tactfully with them would protect the weak believer from harm and might also win over the powerful evildoer. Likewise, when Qadarite doctrine became widespread among the people of Basra, abandoning the transmission of hadith from them would have caused the knowledge, Sunnah traditions, and transmitted reports preserved among them to die out.

If duties relating to knowledge, jihad, and other matters cannot be fulfilled except through someone whose religious innovation causes less harm than abandoning that duty, then securing the benefit of fulfilling the duty, despite the lesser harm accompanying it, is better than the reverse. For this reason, these questions require a nuanced discussion.

---

## Page 13804

Many answers given by Imam Ahmad and other imams were responses to questions from people whose circumstances they knew, or were addressed to particular individuals whose circumstances they knew. Such answers are comparable to the Messenger’s rulings on particular cases—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—which apply only to analogous cases.

Some people have treated these answers as general rulings and consequently practised forms of shunning and denunciation that they were not commanded to practise, and which are therefore neither obligatory nor recommended. In doing so, they may have neglected obligatory or recommended deeds and committed forbidden acts.

Others have disregarded this matter altogether, failing to shun the evil practices rooted in religious innovation that they were commanded to shun. Instead, they have merely kept away from them out of indifference, rather than abstaining from them with aversion, or have fallen into them themselves. They may also abstain from them with aversion, yet neither forbid others to engage in them nor punish those who deserve punishment for them through shunning or similar measures. They have thus neglected the forbidding of wrong that they were commanded to undertake, whether as an obligation or a recommendation. They therefore either commit wrong or fail to forbid it, doing what they were forbidden to do or neglecting what they were commanded to do.

That is how matters stand. Allah’s religion is the middle way between those who go to excess in it and those who neglect it. And Allah, Glorified is He, knows best.

---

## Page 13805

Shaykh al-Islām was asked about a Muslim who, in his youth, committed a sin warranting shunning and avoidance. One group said, “He should seek Allah’s forgiveness, and he should be pardoned and all his past deeds overlooked.” Another group said, “It is not permissible to take him as a brother or keep his company.” Which of the two groups is closer to the truth?

He replied:

There is no doubt that whoever sincerely repents to Allah will have his repentance accepted by Allah, as the Most High says:

“He is the One who accepts repentance from His servants, pardons their sins, and knows what you do.”

The Most High also says:

“Say, ‘O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of Allah’s mercy. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins.’”

That is, for those who repent. This being so, if the man repents, then does righteous deeds for a year without going back on his repentance, his repentance is to be accepted, and people may sit with him and speak to him. If, however, he repents but a year has not yet passed, the scholars have two well-known views concerning him.

Some say that people may sit with him immediately and his testimony may be accepted. Others say that a year must pass, as was the practice of ‘Umar ibn al-Khattāb with Sabīgh ibn ‘Isl. This is one of

---

## Page 13806

the matters open to scholarly judgment.

Whoever holds that this person’s repentance should be accepted and that people may sit with him immediately, before testing his sincerity, has adopted a defensible view. Whoever holds that this should be delayed for a time, until he does righteous deeds and demonstrates the sincerity of his repentance, has likewise adopted a defensible view. Neither view is objectionable.

The Shaykh also said:

Allah has forbidden the spreading of indecency, saying:

“Indeed, those who love to see indecency spread among the believers will suffer a painful punishment in this world and the Hereafter.”

He has likewise commanded that indecent acts be concealed, as the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Whoever falls into any of these filthy acts should conceal himself with the concealment Allah has granted him. For whoever reveals his wrongdoing to us, we shall enforce upon him the punishment prescribed in the Book.”

He also said:

“All of my community will be pardoned except those who publicize their sins. Publicizing one’s sins includes a man committing a sin at night, which Allah has concealed, then speaking about it the next morning.”

As long as a sin remains concealed, its harm falls upon the sinner alone. But when it is made public and goes unopposed, its harm becomes general. How much worse, then, if making it public encourages others to commit it!

For this reason, Imam Ahmad and others condemned forms of tender love poetry, lest people be stirred toward indecent acts. Hence, anyone afflicted with passionate love is enjoined to remain chaste and conceal it. He will then be among those of whom Allah says:

“Indeed, whoever is mindful of Allah and remains patient—surely Allah does not let the reward of those who do good go to waste.”

And Allah knows best.

---

## Page 13807

He also said—may Allah have mercy on him:

As for someone who abandons prayer, and others who openly display religious innovation or sinful conduct, the ruling governing a Muslim’s conduct toward them varies, just as the ruling applicable to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, differed between Mecca and Medina. The ruling for someone able to discipline them by shunning them is not the same as for someone unable to do so. Nor is shunning them the same for someone who has no need to sit with them as for someone who does.

The basic principle is that shunning the openly sinful is of two kinds: shunning by way of avoidance and shunning as a disciplinary measure.

The first is indicated by Allah’s words:

“And leave them in a gracious manner.”

And His words:

“He has already revealed to you in the Book that when you hear Allah’s verses being denied and ridiculed, you must not sit with them until they turn to another conversation.”

A Muslim’s migration from the abode of war also falls under this category. The purpose here is for a Muslim to abandon evil deeds and keep away from bad companions whose company harms him, except where there is a need or an overriding benefit.

As for “disciplinary shunning,” examples include “the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and his Companions shunning the three who were left behind,” and ‘Umar and the Muslims shunning Subaygh. This is a form of punishment. Thus, if it brings about

---

## Page 13808

good or the prevention of evil through such shunning, this punishment is prescribed. But if it causes harm greater than the harm of the sin, it is not prescribed. And Allah knows best.

He was asked:

Should someone who drinks wine be greeted with salām? If he offers the greeting, should it be returned? Should his funeral procession be attended? Does he become a disbeliever if he doubts that wine is forbidden?

He answered:

Praise be to Allah. Whoever commits evil deeds, such as sexual immorality, drinking wine, aggression, or the like, must be rebuked according to one’s ability, as the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Whoever among you sees an evil, let him change it with his hand. If he cannot, then with his tongue. If he cannot, then with his heart—and that is the weakest level of faith.”

If a man conceals such conduct rather than displaying it openly, he should be rebuked privately and his faults concealed, as the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Whoever conceals a servant’s faults, Allah will conceal his faults in this world and the Hereafter.”

The exception is when his harm extends to others: an aggressor’s aggression must be restrained. If someone privately tells him to desist but he does not, that person should take measures that will restrain him, such as shunning him or otherwise, if that is more beneficial for the religion. But if a man openly commits evil deeds, he must be rebuked publicly, and he no longer

---

## Page 13809

enjoys protection from backbiting. He must be punished publicly in a manner that deters him from such conduct, through shunning or other means. He should neither be greeted with salām nor have his greeting returned, provided the person doing so can act without causing greater harm.

Righteous and religious people should shun him in death as they shunned him in life, if this deters other wrongdoers like him. They should therefore refrain from accompanying his funeral procession, just as “the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, refrained from offering the funeral prayer for more than one wrongdoer.” Likewise, Samurah ibn Jundub was told, “Your son died (1) last night.” He replied, “Had he died, I would not have offered the funeral prayer for him.” He meant that his son had contributed to his own death and would therefore be like someone who killed himself. Indeed, “the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, refrained from offering the funeral prayer for someone who had killed himself.”

Similarly, the Companions shunned the three men whose sin of failing to undertake obligatory jihad had become known, until Allah accepted their repentance. When someone openly repents, he should openly be treated with kindness.

As for anyone who denies or doubts the prohibition of something whose prohibition is established by mass transmission, such as wine, carrion, or sexual immoralities, he must be called upon to repent and informed of its prohibition. If he repents, well and good; otherwise, he is to be put to death as an apostate from Islam. The funeral prayer is not to be offered for him, nor is he to be buried among the Muslims.

> **Footnotes:**
> (1) Thus in the printed edition. The correct reading is “bashima” (he suffered indigestion from overeating), meaning that his indigestion was so severe that he nearly died.

## Page 13810

He was also asked about the saying attributed to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, “An evildoer has no protection from backbiting,” and about what constitutes evildoing. A man quarreled with two men, one of whom drinks wine, keeps company with people while they drink, consumes unlawful earnings, or attends dancing or performances of the frame drum or flute. Is someone who does not greet him committing a sin?

He answered:

As for the hadith, these are not the words of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Rather, it is reported that al-Hasan al-Basrī said: “Do you shrink from mentioning the wicked man? Mention his faults so that people may beware of him.” Another hadith states:

“Whoever casts off the cloak of modesty has no protection from backbiting.”

Backbiting is permissible in these two cases, with no disagreement among the scholars.

The first is when a person openly engages in wickedness, such as injustice, sexual immoralities, or religious innovations contrary to the Sunnah. When he openly commits wrongdoing, it becomes obligatory to denounce it to the extent of one’s ability, as the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Whoever among you sees a wrong, let him change it with his hand. If he cannot, then with his tongue; and if he cannot, then with his heart—and that is the weakest level of faith.”

Reported by Muslim.

In al-Musnad and the Sunan collections, it is reported from Abū Bakr al-Siddīq, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: “O

---

## Page 13811

people, you read the Quran and recite this verse, yet apply it incorrectly: ‘O you who believe, take care of yourselves. Those who go astray will not harm you if you are rightly guided.’ I heard the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, say: ‘When people see wrongdoing and do not change it, Allah may soon afflict them all with a punishment from Him.’”

Whoever openly commits wrongdoing must be denounced, shunned, and censured for it. This is the meaning of their saying:

“Whoever casts off the cloak of modesty has no protection from backbiting.”

This differs from someone who conceals his sin and keeps it hidden. His sin should be concealed, but he should be advised privately. Anyone who knows his condition should shun him until he repents and mention his conduct by way of sincere counsel.

The second case is when someone is consulted about marrying a man, dealing with him, or calling him as a witness, and knows that he is unsuitable for that purpose. The person consulted should offer sincere advice by explaining the man’s condition, as is authentically reported:

Fātimah bint Qays said to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: “Abū Jahm and Muʿāwiyah have proposed marriage to me.” He told her: “As for Abū Jahm, he is a man who beats women. As for Muʿāwiyah, he is a poor man with no wealth.”

Thus, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, explained the condition of both suitors to the woman. This supports al-Hasan’s saying:

“Do you shrink from mentioning the wicked man? Mention his faults so that people may beware of him.”

Indeed, sincere counsel concerning religion is more important than sincere counsel concerning worldly affairs. Since the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, advised the woman concerning her worldly affairs, sincere counsel concerning religion is all the more important. If a man neglects the prayers and commits wrongful acts, and is in the company of

---

## Page 13812

someone whose faith he may corrupt, his conduct should be explained to that person so that he may avoid his company.

If he is an innovator who promotes beliefs contrary to the Quran and Sunnah, or follows a path contrary to the Quran and Sunnah, and it is feared that he may thereby lead people astray, his conduct should be explained publicly so that people may guard against his misguidance and know his condition.

All of this must be done out of sincere concern and in pursuit of Allah’s pleasure, not from personal motives against the individual. For example, there may be worldly enmity, envy, hatred, or rivalry for leadership between two people, so one speaks of the other’s faults under the guise of sincere advice, while inwardly intending to disparage him and exact revenge on him. This is the work of Satan, and:

“Actions are judged only by intentions, and each person will have only what he intended.”

Rather, the sincere adviser should intend that Allah reform that individual and protect the Muslims from his harm in their religious and worldly affairs. He should pursue this aim through the easiest means available to him.

No one may voluntarily attend gatherings where wrongdoing takes place unless necessity requires it, as stated in the hadith:

“Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day must not sit at a table where wine is being drunk.”

A group of people who had been drinking wine were brought before Umar ibn Abd al-Azīz, and he ordered that they be flogged. He was told, “There is someone fasting among them.”

He replied: “Begin with him! Have you not heard Allah say:

‘He has already revealed to you in the Book that when you hear Allah’s revelations being denied and ridiculed, you must not sit with them until they turn to another subject. Otherwise, you would be like them’?”

Umar ibn Abd al-Azīz, may Allah be pleased with him, explained that Allah has deemed the person attending

---

## Page 13813

wrongdoing to be like the one who commits it. Hence the scholars have said:

If someone is invited to a feast where there is wrongdoing, such as wine or flute-playing, he may not attend. This is because Allah Most High has commanded us to denounce wrongdoing to the extent possible. Whoever attends voluntarily without denouncing it has disobeyed Allah and His Messenger by neglecting His command to reject it with abhorrence and forbid it. Accordingly, someone who voluntarily attends gatherings where wine is drunk, without necessity, and does not denounce the wrongdoing as Allah has commanded, shares in the sinners’ sinfulness and is counted among them.

He—may Allah have mercy on him—was asked:

Is backbiting permissible concerning certain people, or may a particular individual be singled out? What is the ruling on this? Please give us a detailed answer, so that those who enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong may understand this, and each may draw upon knowledge and sound judgment according to his ability.

He answered:

All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds. The starting point in this discussion is to understand that backbiting is as the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, explained it in the authentic hadith. When asked about backbiting, he said:

“It is to mention your brother in a way he dislikes.”

He was asked: “O Messenger of Allah, what if my brother really has the fault I mention?”

He replied: “If he has the fault you mention, you have backbitten him; if he does not, you have slandered him.”

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, explained the difference between backbiting and slander, and that lying

---

## Page 13814

about him constitutes slander against him, as He, glorified be He, says:

“Why, when you heard it, did you not say, ‘It is not for us to speak of this. Glory be to You! This is a tremendous slander’?”

And Allah Most High says:

“Nor bring any slander they fabricate between their hands and feet.”

An authentic hadith states:

“The Jews are a people given to slander.”

Thus, all lying about a person is forbidden, whether that person is Muslim or unbeliever, righteous or wicked. Fabricating lies about a believer, however, is more grievous. Indeed, all lying is forbidden. Nevertheless, equivocal speech is permitted when there is a need recognized by Islamic law. It may also be called lying, because a speaker intends a meaning by his words and wants the listener to understand that meaning. If his words do not accord with what he means, that is an outright lie. If they accord with what he means, but not with what the listener understands, that is equivocal speech. It is lying from the standpoint of what is understood, though not from the standpoint of the legitimate purpose intended.

An example is the saying of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

“Abraham told only three lies, all for Allah’s sake: his words concerning Sarah, ‘My sister’; his saying, ‘Rather, this largest one of them did it’; and his saying, ‘I am ill.’”

All three are instances of equivocal speech. Scholars have cited them as evidence that a person suffering injustice may use equivocation: that is, intend by his words a meaning that the wording can bear, even if the listener does not understand it. This is why some of the

---

## Page 13815

scholars have said that the concessions granted by the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, concern only this kind of speech, as in the hadith of Umm Kulthūm bint ʿUqba, who reported that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“The person who reconciles people, saying good things or intending good, is not a liar.”

He permitted what people call lying only in three situations: reconciling people, warfare, and a man’s conversation with his wife. The scholar holding this view said: “All of this consists exclusively of equivocal speech.” Thus, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, denied that it was lying in view of its intention and purpose. It is authentically reported that he said:

“War is deception.”

When he intended to undertake a military expedition, he would conceal his intention by indicating another destination. Another example is al-Siddīq’s statement about the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, during the migration journey: “This man guides me along the way.” There is also the Prophet’s reply, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, to the unbeliever who questioned him during the expedition to Badr: “We are from water.”

Another example is his statement to the man who swore, concerning a Muslim whom the unbelievers intended to capture, “He is my brother.” He meant brotherhood in religion, whereas they understood brotherhood by descent. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“You were indeed the most upright and truthful of them. A Muslim is the brother of a Muslim.”

The point here is that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, distinguished backbiting from slander. He explained that someone who truthfully reports something about his believing brother that the latter dislikes is engaging in backbiting. In his words, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, “Mentioning your brother in a way that

---

## Page 13816

he dislikes,” he echoes the words of Allah Most High:

“And do not backbite one another. Would any of you like to eat the flesh of his dead brother? You would detest it.”

Thus, the basis for the prohibition is brotherhood in faith. Accordingly, the gravity of backbiting varies with the believer’s standing: the greater his faith, the graver it is to backbite him. Reviling and fault-finding are akin to backbiting, since both involve criticizing people and attacking them, as backbiting does. Reviling, however, involves harsh and vehement attacks, whereas fault-finding may lack such harshness and vehemence. Allah Most High says:

“Among them are those who find fault with you concerning the alms.”

That is, they criticize and attack you. Allah Most High also says:

“Do not find fault with yourselves.”

That is, do not find fault with one another. He also says:

“A habitual reviler, going about spreading malicious gossip.”

And He says:

“Woe to every reviler and fault-finder.”

With this established, we say: mentioning people in ways they dislike takes two basic forms: first, mentioning a category of people; and second, mentioning a particular individual, living or dead.

As for the first, every category condemned by Allah and His Messenger must be condemned; this is not backbiting. Likewise, every category praised by Allah and His Messenger must be praised. Those cursed by Allah and His Messenger are to be cursed, just as blessings are to be invoked upon those whom Allah and His angels bless. Thus, Allah Most High has condemned the unbeliever, the wicked, the defiantly disobedient, the wrongdoer, the wayward, the misguided,

---

## Page 13817

the envious, the miserly, the sorcerer, the one who takes interest and the one who pays it, the thief, the adulterer, the conceited, the boastful, the arrogant tyrant, and others like them. Likewise, He has praised the pious believer, the truthful, the dutiful, the just, the rightly guided, the upright, the generous, the charitable, the merciful, and others like them.

“The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, cursed the one who takes interest, the one who pays it, its two witnesses and its scribe.”

He also cursed the man who marries a woman to make her lawful again for her former husband, and the former husband for whose sake this is done. He cursed whoever does what the people of Lot did. He cursed whoever commits an offense or shelters an offender. He cursed wine, the one who presses it, the one who has it pressed, the one who carries it, the one to whom it is carried, its seller, its buyer, the one who serves it, the one who drinks it, and the one who consumes its proceeds. He cursed the Jews and Christians because, when animal fats were forbidden to them, they rendered them, sold them, and consumed their proceeds. Allah cursed those who conceal the clear proofs He revealed after He had made them clear to people, and He mentioned the curse upon the wrongdoers.

Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet and upon those who believe. The patient person who says, “To Allah we belong and to Him we shall return,” receives blessings and mercy from his Lord. Allah and His angels send blessings upon the one who teaches people good, and everything seeks forgiveness for him, even the fish and the birds. Allah commanded His Prophet to seek forgiveness for his own sin and for believing men and women.

Thus, when the purpose is to enjoin good and encourage it, and to forbid evil and warn against it, these things must be mentioned. For this reason, whenever the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, learned that someone had done something he forbade, he would say: “Why is it that some men stipulate

---

## Page 13818

conditions that are not in the Book of Allah? Whoever stipulates a condition that is not in the Book of Allah, it is invalid, even if there are a hundred such conditions.”

“Why is it that some men scrupulously avoid things I allow myself to do? By Allah, I am the most mindful of Allah among you and know His limits best.”

“Why is it that some men say, ‘As for me, I fast and never break my fast,’ while another says, ‘As for me, I pray at night and never sleep,’ another says, ‘I do not marry women,’ and another says, ‘I do not eat meat’? Yet I fast and break my fast, pray at night and sleep, marry women, and eat meat. Whoever turns away from my sunnah is not of me.”

No one may base praise and blame, love and hatred, allegiance and enmity, or blessings and curses on designations other than those on which Allah has made them depend. Such other designations include the names of tribes and cities, schools and paths associated with imams and shaykhs, and similar labels intended for identification. As Allah Most High said:

“O mankind, We created you from a male and a female and made you peoples and tribes so that you may know one another. Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most pious of you.”

Allah Most High also said:

“Indeed, the allies of Allah shall have no fear, nor shall they grieve.”

“Those who believe and are mindful of Him.”

And He said:

“That is Paradise, which We grant as an inheritance to those of Our servants who are pious.”

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“The family of Abū So-and-so are not my allies; my only allies are Allah and the righteous believers.”

He also said:

“Indeed, my allies are the pious, wherever they may be and whoever they may be.”

And he said:

“Allah has removed from you the arrogance of the pre-Islamic age of ignorance and its boasting of ancestry. People are of two kinds: a pious believer and a wretched evildoer.

---

## Page 13819

People are descended from Adam, and Adam was made from dust.” He also said:

“An Arab has no superiority over a non-Arab, nor a non-Arab over an Arab; a white person has no superiority over a black person, nor a black person over a white person, except through piety.”

Thus, mentioning times and justice through designations of preference, allegiance, locality, or affiliation with a scholar or shaykh is intended only to identify a person and distinguish him from others. Praise and blame, love and hatred, allegiance and enmity, however, must be based only on matters for which Allah has revealed His authority—and His authority is His Book. Whoever is a believer must be accorded allegiance, whatever group he belongs to; whoever is a disbeliever must be opposed, whatever group he belongs to. Allah Most High said:

“Your only allies are Allah, His Messenger, and those who believe—those who establish prayer, give zakah, and bow down in worship.”

“And whoever takes Allah, His Messenger, and the believers as allies—indeed, it is the party of Allah that will prevail.”

Allah Most High also said:

“O you who believe, do not take the Jews and Christians as allies; they are allies of one another.”

Allah Most High also said:

“The believing men and believing women are allies of one another.”

Allah Most High also said:

“Do not take My enemies and your enemies as allies.”

Allah Most High also said:

“Will you then take him and his offspring as allies instead of Me, though they are your enemies? What an evil exchange for the wrongdoers!”

Allah Most High also said:

“You will not find a people who believe in Allah and the Last Day loving those who oppose Allah and His Messenger, even if they are their fathers, their sons, their brothers, or their kin. Those are the ones in whose hearts He has inscribed faith and whom He has strengthened with a spirit from Him.”

Whoever possesses both faith and wickedness is to be accorded allegiance in proportion to his faith

---

## Page 13820

and hatred in proportion to his wickedness. Merely committing sins and acts of disobedience does not remove him from faith altogether, contrary to what the Khawārij and Mu‘tazilah maintain. Nor are the prophets, the steadfastly truthful, the martyrs, and the righteous to be placed on the same footing as the wicked with respect to faith, religion, love, hatred, allegiance, and enmity. Allah Most High said:

“If two groups of believers fight, make peace between them. But if one transgresses against the other, fight the transgressing group until it returns to Allah’s command. If it returns, reconcile them with justice and be equitable. Indeed, Allah loves those who act equitably.”

“The believers are but brothers.”

Thus, He declared them brothers despite their fighting and aggression. Allah Most High also said:

“Or should We treat those who believe and do righteous deeds like those who spread corruption on earth? Or should We treat the righteous like the wicked?”

Allah Most High also said:

“Do not let pity for them keep you from carrying out Allah’s prescribed punishment, if you believe in Allah and the Last Day.”

This discussion, then, concerns categories of people.

As for a particular individual, the evil in him may be mentioned in certain circumstances. Among these is that a person who has been wronged may mention his wrongdoer’s faults—either to ward off his wrongdoing and obtain his due, as when Hind said: “O Messenger of Allah, Abū Sufyān is a miserly man, and he does not give me enough maintenance for myself and my children.” The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said to her: “Take what is sufficient for you and your children, according to what is reasonable.”

Likewise, he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “A debtor’s delay in payment when he has the means makes it lawful to censure and punish him.” Wakī‘ said: “Censuring him means complaining about him, and punishing him means imprisoning him.” Allah Most High said:

“Allah does not like evil to be voiced openly

---

## Page 13821

in speech, except by one who has been wronged.” It has been reported that this verse was revealed concerning a man who stayed with some people, but they offered him no hospitality. If this applies to someone wronged by being denied hospitality—whose obligatory nature people have disputed, although the correct view is that it is obligatory—then how much more does it apply to someone wronged by being denied a right to which the Muslims unanimously agree he is entitled? Or he may mention his wrongdoer’s faults in retaliation, without overstepping the bounds, resorting to falsehood, or wronging anyone else; refraining from this, however, is better.

Another circumstance is when this is done to offer Muslims sincere advice concerning their religious and worldly affairs, as in the authentic hadith concerning Fātimah bint Qays:

“When she consulted the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, about whom she should marry, she said, ‘Mu‘āwiyah and Abū Jahm have proposed to me.’ He replied, ‘As for Mu‘āwiyah, he is penniless and has no wealth. As for Abū Jahm, he frequently beats women.’”

Another narration states:

“He never puts his staff down from his shoulder.”

He thus explained to her that one was poor and might be unable to fulfil her rights, while the other would harm her by beating her. This was sincere advice to her, even though it involved mentioning a suitor’s fault. The same applies to advising a man about someone with whom he deals, whom he appoints as his agent or executor, whom he calls as a witness, or even to whom he submits a dispute for judgment, and similar matters.

If this applies to a private interest, then how much more important is giving advice where the rights of Muslims at large are at stake—concerning rulers, judges, witnesses, and officials, including those serving in the administrative bureaus and others? There is no doubt that sincere advice in such matters is of greater importance, as the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

---

## Page 13822

“Religion is sincere advice. Religion is sincere advice.” They asked, “To whom, O Messenger of Allah?” He replied, “To Allah, His Book, His Messenger, the leaders of the Muslims, and their common people.”

People said to ‘Umar ibn al-Khattāb concerning the members of the consultative council, “Appoint so-and-so and so-and-so.” He then mentioned something about each of the six—who were the finest members of the Muslim community—that prevented him from appointing that man.

If sincere advice is obligatory in matters concerning private and public religious interests, this applies, for example, to hadith transmitters who make mistakes or lie. As Yahyā ibn Sa‘īd said:

“I asked Mālik, al-Thawrī, al-Layth ibn Sa‘d—I think—and al-Awzā‘ī about a man whose hadith transmission is suspect or whose memory is unreliable. They said, ‘Make his condition clear.’”

Someone said to Ahmad ibn Hanbal, “I find it burdensome to say that so-and-so is like this and so-and-so is like that.” He replied, “If you remain silent and I remain silent, when will an uninformed person distinguish the sound from the unsound?”

The same applies to the leading proponents of religious innovation who espouse doctrines contrary to the Book and the Sunnah or practise forms of worship contrary to the Book and the Sunnah. Explaining their condition and warning the Muslim community against them is obligatory by the agreement of the Muslims. Indeed, Ahmad ibn Hanbal was asked:

“Which do you prefer: a man who fasts, prays, and observes spiritual retreat, or one who speaks out against the people of religious innovation?”

He replied, “If he stands in prayer, offers prayers, and observes spiritual retreat, he benefits only himself. But if he speaks out against the people of religious innovation, he benefits the Muslims. This is better.”

He thus explained that the benefit of this extends to the Muslims generally in their religion and is a form of jihad

---

## Page 13823

in the path of Allah; for purifying Allah’s path, His religion, His way, and His law, and repelling these people’s oppression and aggression against them, is a collective obligation by the agreement of the Muslims. Were it not for those whom Allah raises up to repel the harm these people cause, religion would be corrupted. This corruption would be worse than the damage caused when an enemy at war with the Muslims takes control. For when such enemies take control, they corrupt hearts and the religion within them only as a secondary consequence, whereas those others corrupt hearts directly. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said:

“Allah does not look at your appearance or your wealth; rather, He looks at your hearts and your deeds.”

This is because Allah says in His Book:

“We have certainly sent Our messengers with clear proofs and sent down with them the Scripture and the balance so that people may uphold justice. And We sent down iron, wherein is great might and benefits for people, and so that Allah may make evident those who support Him and His messengers without having seen Him.”

He thus states that He sent down the Book and the balance so that people may uphold justice, and that He sent down iron as He described. Religion is therefore upheld by the Book that guides and the sword that supports:

“And sufficient is your Lord as a guide and helper.”

The Book is the foundation. Thus, when Allah first sent His Messenger, He sent down the Book to him. He remained in Mecca, and Allah did not command him to take up the sword until he had emigrated and had supporters to assist him in jihad.

The enemies of religion are of two kinds: the disbelievers and the hypocrites. Allah has indeed commanded His Prophet

---

## Page 13824

to strive against both groups, saying in two verses of the Quran:

“Strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and be stern with them.”

If hypocrites introduce innovations that contradict the Book and mislead people about them, and these innovations are not explained to people, the authority of the Book is undermined and the religion is altered—just as the religion of the People of the Book before us was corrupted through alterations whose perpetrators went unchallenged.

There may also be people who are not hypocrites but readily listen to the hypocrites. They have become so confused about them that they suppose their statements to be true, even though they contradict the Book, and become advocates of the hypocrites’ innovations. As Allah Most High says:

“Had they gone forth with you, they would only have added to your confusion and would have hurried about in your midst, seeking to sow discord among you. And among you are those who listen to them.”

The condition of these people must therefore also be explained. Indeed, the confusion caused by such people is greater, for they possess faith that requires loyalty toward them, yet they have embraced some of the hypocrites’ innovations that corrupt the religion. It is therefore essential to warn against those innovations, even if this requires mentioning these people and identifying them by name. Indeed, even if they had not received that innovation from a hypocrite, but had propounded it thinking it to be guidance, goodness, and part of the religion, when it was not, its true nature would still have to be explained.

For this reason, it is obligatory to explain the condition of those who err in hadith and its transmission, and those who

---

## Page 13825

err in scholarly judgment and the issuing of fatwas, and those who err in asceticism and worship—even though one who errs while exercising independent judgment is forgiven his error and rewarded for his effort. It is obligatory to explain the words and deeds prescribed by the Book and the Sunnah, even if this means contradicting his words and deeds. Anyone known to have exercised legitimate independent judgment must not be spoken of in a manner that disparages him or imputes sin to him, for Allah has forgiven his error. Rather, his faith and piety require that he be shown loyalty and love, and accorded the rights Allah has prescribed for him, including praise, supplication, and other such things.

If, however, his hypocrisy is known—as the hypocrisy of certain people was known during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, such as Abd Allāh ibn Ubayy and his associates, and as the Muslims have known the hypocrisy of the Rāfidah (Rejectionists) at large: Abd Allāh ibn Saba’ and others like him, such as Abd al-Quddūs ibn al-Hajjāj and Muhammad ibn Sa‘īd al-Maslūb—then he is to be identified as a hypocrite. If he openly professes an innovation, but it is not known whether he is a hypocrite or a mistaken believer, he should be described according to what is known of him. It is not lawful for anyone to pursue that of which he has no knowledge, nor may he speak on this subject unless he intends thereby to seek the Face of Allah Most High, to make Allah’s word supreme, and to make religion wholly devoted to Allah. Whoever speaks on this subject without knowledge, or says what he knows to be contrary to the truth, is sinful.

The same applies to judges, witnesses, and those who issue fatwas. As the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Judges are of three kinds: two are in the Fire and one is in Paradise. A man who knows the truth and judges accordingly is in Paradise, and a man who judges people’s cases in ignorance is in the Fire,

---

## Page 13826

and a man who knows the truth but judges contrary to it is in the Fire.” Allah Most High has said:

“O you who believe, stand firmly for justice as witnesses for Allah, even against yourselves, your parents, or your close relatives. Whether someone is rich or poor, Allah is best able to care for both. So do not follow your desires, lest you depart from justice. If you distort your testimony or refuse to give it, Allah is indeed fully aware of what you do.”

“Distortion” means lying, and “refusal” means concealing the truth. A similar meaning appears in the two Sahīh collections, where the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“The buyer and seller have the right to withdraw from the sale until they part. If they are truthful and make matters clear, their transaction will be blessed; but if they lie and conceal, the blessing of their transaction will be erased.”

Moreover, anyone who speaks about this matter with knowledge must have a good intention. If he speaks the truth with the aim of gaining supremacy in the land or spreading corruption, he is like someone who fights out of partisan zeal or to show off. But if he speaks for the sake of Allah Most High, devoting his religion sincerely to Him, he is among those who strive in Allah’s cause, the heirs of the prophets and successors to the messengers.

This does not contradict his saying:

“Backbiting is mentioning about your brother what he dislikes.”

For the brother meant here is a believer. If a believing brother is sincere in his faith, he will not dislike your speaking this truth, which Allah and His Messenger love, even if it constitutes testimony against him and his family. Rather, he must uphold justice and bear witness for Allah, even against himself, his parents, or his close relatives. Whenever he dislikes this truth, his faith is deficient, and his bond of brotherhood diminishes in proportion to that deficiency. His dislike is therefore not taken into account insofar as it stems from the deficiency in his faith; for his dislike of what

---

## Page 13827

Allah and His Messenger do not love requires giving precedence to what Allah and His Messenger love, as Allah Most High says:

“Allah and His Messenger are more deserving that they should please Him.”

It may then be said that this falls outside both the wording and the meaning of the hadith concerning backbiting. Alternatively, it may be said that those specifically exempted from it were included within its scope, just as generality in wording and generality in meaning may be qualified. Whether the ruling ceases to apply because its cause is absent or because an impediment is present, the result is the same. The disagreement over this ultimately comes down to terminology, since “cause” may mean either a complete cause or merely a factor conducive to the ruling. Allah knows best and is most wise. May Allah bless our Prophet Muhammad, his family, and his Companions, and grant them peace.

He also said—may Allah Most High have mercy on him:

Some people engage in backbiting to go along with those in their company, their friends, and their clansmen, even though they know that the person being discussed is innocent of what they say, or that only some of it is true of him. Yet such a person thinks that, if he objects, he will disrupt the gathering and those present will find him tiresome and turn away from him. He therefore regards going along with them as good manners and pleasant companionship. They may become angry, and he grows angry because they are angry, joining them in their talk.

---

## Page 13828

And some dress up backbiting in various guises. Sometimes they present it as piety and righteousness, saying: “It is not my habit to speak of anyone except favourably. I dislike backbiting and lying; I am merely telling you about his circumstances.” Or they say: “By Allah, he is a poor fellow—or a good man—but he has such-and-such faults.” They may also say: “Let us leave him alone. May Allah forgive us and him,” when their sole intention is to belittle him and diminish his standing. They dress up backbiting as righteousness and piety, seeking thereby to deceive Allah as they would deceive a created being. We have seen many forms of this and similar behaviour among them.

Some ostentatiously elevate others, thereby elevating themselves. One says: “Had I prayed for so-and-so in my prayer last night, I would not have heard such-and-such about him,” intending to elevate himself and lower the other man in the eyes of those who hold him in esteem. Or he says: “So-and-so is dull-witted and understands little,” intending to praise himself, establish his own knowledge, and show that he is superior to him.

Some are driven by envy to backbite, thus combining two reprehensible things: backbiting and envy. When someone is praised, they do whatever they can to strip him of that praise by disparaging him, whether under the guise of religious devotion and righteousness or through envy, wickedness, and slander, seeking to deprive him of that esteem. Some present backbiting as mockery and joking to make others laugh

---

## Page 13829

by mocking and mimicking someone and belittling the object of their ridicule.

Some dress up backbiting as astonishment, saying: “I am astonished at so-and-so! How can he fail to do such-and-such? And so-and-so—how could such-and-such have come from him? How could he have done such-and-such?” Thus they bring up his name under the guise of expressing astonishment.

Some make a show of sorrow, saying: “Poor so-and-so! What has happened to him and how things have turned out for him have saddened me.” Those listening suppose that he is grieving for the man and feels sorry for him, while inwardly he gloats over his misfortune. If he could, he would add to his suffering. He may even mention him in the presence of his enemies so that they too can gloat over him. This and similar behaviour are among the gravest diseases of the heart and attempts to deceive Allah and His creation.

Some dress up backbiting as anger and denunciation of wrongdoing, employing various forms of embellished speech, while their intention is other than what they outwardly profess. Allah is the One whose help is sought.

---

## Page 13830

He—may Allah have mercy on him—was asked:

About a man whose word is accepted by judges, who goes out to enjoy the blossoms during the seasons for recreation, when people gather. He sees wrongdoing but is unable to put a stop to it, and his wife also accompanies him. Is this permissible? Does it impugn his uprightness?

He replied:

A person may not attend places where he witnesses wrongdoing that he cannot oppose, unless there is a reason sanctioned by Islamic law—for example, something necessary for his religious or worldly welfare that requires his presence there, or his being compelled to attend.

As for attending merely for recreation and taking his wife along to witness such things, this impugns his uprightness and sense of propriety if he persists in doing so. Allah knows best.

---

## Page 13831

He—may Allah have mercy on him—was also asked:

Concerning the town of “Mardin”: Is it a land of war or a land of peace? Must a Muslim residing there emigrate to the lands of Islam? If emigration is obligatory for him, but he does not emigrate and assists the enemies of the Muslims personally or financially, does he thereby incur sin? Does someone who accuses him of hypocrisy and insults him on that account incur sin?

He replied:

Praise be to Allah. The lives and property of Muslims are inviolable wherever they may be, whether in “Mardin” or elsewhere. Assisting those who depart from the law of Islam is forbidden, whether they are inhabitants of Mardin or others. Anyone residing there who is unable to practise his religion must emigrate. Otherwise, emigration is recommended, not obligatory.

It is forbidden for them to assist the enemy of the Muslims with their persons or wealth. They must refrain from doing so by whatever means are available to them, whether by absenting themselves, speaking indirectly, or adopting conciliatory measures. If they can avoid it only by emigrating, emigration becomes obligatory.

It is not permissible to insult them indiscriminately or accuse them all of hypocrisy. Rather, censure and accusations of hypocrisy apply to those who display the characteristics mentioned in the Quran and Sunnah; this includes some of

---

## Page 13832

the inhabitants of Mardin and others.

As for whether it is a land of war or a land of peace, it has a mixed character, combining features of both. It is neither like a land of peace, where the rulings of Islam apply because its troops are Muslims, nor like a land of war, whose inhabitants are unbelievers. Rather, it belongs to a third category: Muslims there are treated as they deserve, while those who depart from the law of Islam are fought as they deserve.

He—may Allah Most High have mercy on him—also said:

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Bestower of Mercy.

From Ahmad ibn Taymiyyah to the Sultan of the Muslims and the ruler of the believers, the deputy of the Messenger of Allah—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—among his community, charged with upholding the obligations of the religion and its Sunnah.

May Allah grant him such support as will set right the affairs of this world and the Hereafter for him and for the Muslims, and enable him to put all inward and outward affairs in order, so that he may be included among those described in the words of Allah Most High:

“Those who, if We establish them in the land, establish prayer, give zakah, enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong. And to Allah belongs the outcome of all matters.”

And in the words of the Prophet—may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

“Seven are those whom Allah will shade in His shade on the Day when there is no shade but His: a just ruler”—to the end of the hadith.

And in his words—may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

---

## Page 13833

“Whoever calls others to guidance will have a reward equal to the rewards of those who follow him, without diminishing their rewards in the least.”

Allah has indeed answered the prayers for the Sultan, placing within him goodness to which the hearts of the community bear witness, and thereby favouring him over others. We ask Allah to help him, for none of Allah’s creation is more in need of His help and support than he. Allah Most High says:

“Allah has promised those among you who believe and do righteous deeds that He will surely grant them succession on earth, just as He granted it to those before them; that He will surely establish for them their religion which He has approved for them; and that He will surely replace their fear with security. They worship Me, associating nothing with Me”—to the end of the verse.

The soundness of the Sultan’s affairs depends on exclusive adherence to the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger and Prophet, and on requiring the people to do likewise. For Allah, glorified is He, has made the soundness of those granted authority depend on four things: establishing prayer, giving zakah, enjoining what is right, and forbidding what is wrong.

If he establishes prayer at its appointed times in congregation—together with his entourage and those under his authority—commands all his subjects to do likewise, and punishes anyone negligent in this with the punishment Allah has prescribed, then this foundation will have been fully established.

Moreover, he is utterly dependent on Allah Most High. If he communes privately with his Lord before dawn, seeks His help, and says, “O Ever-Living, O Sustainer of all, there is none worthy of worship but You; by Your mercy I seek help,” Allah will grant him strength and authority to an extent known only to Allah. Allah Most High says:

“If they had done what they were instructed to do, it would have been better for them and a firmer

---

## Page 13834

foundation.”

“And then We would surely have granted them a great reward from Us.”

“And We would surely have guided them to a straight path.”

Moreover, every benefit and good he brings to others is of the same nature as zakah.

Among the greatest acts of worship are relieving poverty, meeting people’s needs, supporting the oppressed, helping those in distress, and enjoining what is right—that is, enjoining the justice and goodness commanded by Allah and His Messenger. This includes instructing the land’s nawāʾib and those in authority to follow the rulings of the Book and the Sunnah and to refrain from what Allah has forbidden. It also includes forbidding what is wrong—that is, forbidding whatever Allah and His Messenger have prohibited.

If the Sultan—may Allah support him—issues directives to this effect throughout the lands of Islam, the resulting good for him and the Muslims in this world and the Hereafter will be known only to Allah. May Allah guide him to what He loves and is pleased with.

## Page 13835

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

He sent down iron, containing mighty force and benefits for people, so that Allah may know who supports Him and His messengers without having seen Him. Indeed, Allah is Powerful, Almighty.

(To proceed: this is a concise treatise containing comprehensive principles of governance

---

## Page 13836

as ordained by Allah, and prophetic signs, which neither ruler nor ruled can do without. It was requested by one of those in authority whom Allah has commanded us to counsel sincerely. As the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said in a report authentically transmitted through several routes in Sahīh Muslim and elsewhere:

“Allah is pleased with three things for you: that you worship Him without associating anything with Him; that you hold firmly, all together, to the rope of Allah and do not become divided; and that you offer sincere counsel to those whom Allah has placed in authority over you.”

This treatise is based on two verses in the Book of Allah, namely His words, Exalted is He:

“Indeed, Allah commands you to render trusts to those to whom they are due and, when you judge between people, to judge with justice. Excellent indeed is what Allah admonishes you to do. Indeed, Allah is All-Hearing, All-Seeing.”

“O you who believe, obey Allah and obey the Messenger and those in authority among you. If you disagree over anything, refer it to Allah and the Messenger, if you believe in Allah and the Last Day. That is better and best in outcome.”

The scholars said:

The first verse was revealed concerning those in authority: they must render trusts to those to whom they are due and judge justly when judging between people. The second was revealed concerning their subjects, soldiers and others: they must obey those in authority who fulfill these duties in their distributions, judgments, military campaigns, and other affairs, unless they command disobedience to Allah. If they command disobedience to Allah, no created being may be obeyed in disobedience to the Creator. If they disagree over anything, they must refer it to the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Even if those in authority fail to fulfill these duties, they are to be obeyed in whatever they command that constitutes obedience to Allah and His Messenger, for that is part of obedience to Allah

---

## Page 13837

and His Messenger, and their rights are to be rendered to them as Allah and His Messenger have commanded.

Allah, Exalted is He, says:

“Cooperate in righteousness and piety, but do not cooperate in sin and aggression.”

Since the verse requires rendering trusts to those to whom they are due and judging with justice, these two duties together encompass just governance and sound administration.

Section

Rendering trusts to those to whom they are due is of two kinds.

The first concerns public offices. This was the occasion for the revelation of the verse. When the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, conquered Mecca and received the keys of the Kaaba from Banū Shaybah, al-ʿAbbās asked him for them, so that he might hold both the responsibility for providing water to the pilgrims and the custodianship of the Sacred House. Allah then revealed this verse, and the Prophet handed the keys of the Kaaba to Banū Shaybah.

Those in authority must therefore appoint to every position in the Muslims’ affairs the most suitable person they can find for that position. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Whoever is entrusted with any of the Muslims’ affairs and appoints a man when he can find someone more suitable to serve the Muslims has betrayed Allah and His Messenger.”

Another version states:

“Whoever appoints a man over a group when he can find within that group someone more pleasing to Allah than him has indeed

---

## Page 13838

betrayed Allah and His Messenger, and betrayed the believers.” Al-Hākim related it in his Sahīh.

Some have transmitted it as a statement made by ʿUmar to Ibn ʿUmar, as reported from him. ʿUmar ibn al-Khattāb, may Allah be pleased with him, said:

“Whoever is entrusted with any of the Muslims’ affairs and appoints a man because of affection or kinship between them has betrayed Allah, His Messenger, and the Muslims.”

This is his duty. He must therefore seek out those qualified for public office to serve as his deputies throughout the provinces: governors acting on behalf of the ruler, judges, and others in similar positions; commanders of troops and military leaders of all ranks; and officials responsible for public funds, including ministers, secretaries, financial supervisors, and collectors of land tax, zakat, and other funds belonging to the Muslims.

Each of these must appoint as deputies and officials the most suitable people he can find. This extends to prayer leaders, muezzins, instructors in Quran recitation, teachers, leaders of the pilgrimage, postal couriers, intelligence agents—who are emissaries—treasury custodians, fortress guards, and the haddādīn, who are the gatekeepers of fortresses and cities; senior and junior army officers; overseers of tribes and markets; and village headmen, known as “dahāqīn.”

Thus, everyone entrusted with any of the Muslims’ affairs, whether among those mentioned or others, must appoint to every position under his authority the most suitable person available to him. He must not give a man preference merely because he has requested the office or was the first to request it;

---

## Page 13839

rather, that should be grounds for refusing him; for it is reported in the Sahīh that some people came to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and asked him for public office. He said:

“We do not entrust this authority of ours to anyone who asks for it.”

He also said to ‘Abd al-Rahmān ibn Samurah:

“O ‘Abd al-Rahmān, do not ask for authority. If you are given it without asking, you will be helped in discharging it; but if you are given it after asking, you will be left to manage it on your own.”

Both compilers recorded it in the two Sahīhs. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, also said:

“Whoever seeks judicial office and enlists help to obtain it will be left to manage it on his own. But whoever neither seeks judicial office nor enlists help to obtain it, Allah will send down an angel to guide him aright.”

It was reported by the compilers of the Sunan.

If he passes over the most deserving and suitable candidate in favor of another because of kinship, a bond arising from manumission, friendship, or shared ties of locality, school of thought, religious path, or ethnic origin—such as Arab, Persian, Turkish, or Roman—or because of a bribe he receives from him, whether money or some benefit, or for any other such reason; or because he harbors resentment toward the more deserving candidate, or because of enmity between them, then he has betrayed Allah, His Messenger, and the believers. He has committed what Allah Most High forbade in His words:

“O you who believe, do not betray Allah and the Messenger, or knowingly betray your trusts.”

Then He said:

“And know that your wealth and your children are but a trial, and that with Allah is a great reward.”

For a man’s love for his child or his freed slave may lead him to favor that person in certain appointments or give him what he does not deserve, thereby betraying his trust. Likewise, he may favor him for the sake of an increase in

---

## Page 13840

his wealth or its preservation, by taking what he is not entitled to or favoring someone who flatters him in certain appointments. He thereby betrays Allah and His Messenger and betrays his trust. But whoever fulfills his trust despite his own desires, Allah makes him steadfast and safeguards his family and wealth after his death. Whoever follows his desires, Allah punishes him with the opposite of what he intended, bringing humiliation upon his family and causing his wealth to vanish. There is a well-known account illustrating this:

One of the Abbasid caliphs asked a scholar to tell him about what he had witnessed. He replied:

“I lived in the time of ‘Umar ibn ‘Abd al-‘Azīz. During his final illness, he was told, ‘Commander of the Faithful, you have deprived your sons of this wealth and left them poor, with nothing.’

“He said, ‘Bring them to me.’ They brought them in—ten-odd sons, none of whom had reached puberty. When he saw them, his eyes filled with tears. Then he said to them:

“‘My sons, by Allah, I have not withheld anything that was rightfully yours, nor would I take other people’s wealth and give it to you. Each of you can only be one of two kinds of men: either righteous—and Allah takes care of the righteous—or unrighteous, in which case I will not leave him anything that would help him disobey Allah. Now leave me.’”

The scholar said, “I later saw one of his sons provide a hundred horses for the cause of Allah”—meaning that he gave them to men who would ride them into battle.

I say: This was despite his having been caliph of the Muslims from the farthest east, the lands of the Turks, to the farthest west, al-Andalus and beyond; and from the islands of Cyprus, the Syrian frontier districts, and fortified regions such as Tarsus and its surroundings, to the farthest reaches of Yemen. Yet each of his children received only a small amount from his estate—reportedly less than

---

## Page 13841

twenty dirhams.

The scholar said, “I also witnessed the case of a caliph whose sons divided his estate, each receiving six hundred thousand dinars. Yet I later saw some of them begging from people”—that is, asking them for charity with outstretched hands. Accounts and events of this kind, witnessed in our own time or reported from earlier times, offer a lesson to everyone endowed with understanding.

The Sunnah of Allah’s Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, establishes in several places that authority is a trust whose duties must be fulfilled. These include what has already been mentioned, as well as his words to Abū Dharr, may Allah be pleased with him, concerning leadership:

“It is a trust, and on the Day of Resurrection it will be a source of disgrace and regret, except for one who assumes it rightfully and fulfills its duties.”

Narrated by Muslim.

Al-Bukhārī narrated in his Sahīh from Abū Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“When the trust is neglected, await the Hour.”

He was asked, “Messenger of Allah, how is it neglected?”

He replied, “When authority is entrusted to those unfit for it, await the Hour.”

The Muslims unanimously agree on the substance of this: an orphan’s guardian, the administrator of an endowment, and a man’s agent in managing his wealth must act in the interests of those they represent, giving priority to the most beneficial course available. As Allah Most High says:

“And do not approach the orphan’s property except in a way that is best.”

He did not say, “except in a way that is good.” This is because a ruler is a shepherd over the people, just like a shepherd tending sheep. As the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Each of you is a shepherd, and each of you is responsible for his flock;

---

## Page 13842

the ruler who governs the people is a shepherd and is responsible for his flock; a woman is a shepherd in her husband’s home and is responsible for her flock; a son is a shepherd over his father’s wealth and is responsible for his flock; and a slave is a shepherd over his master’s wealth and is responsible for his flock. Indeed, each of you is a shepherd, and each of you is responsible for his flock.”

Al-Bukhārī and Muslim narrated it in their Sahīhs. He, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, also said:

“There is no shepherd whom Allah entrusts with a flock who dies while betraying them but that Allah forbids him the fragrance of Paradise.”

Narrated by Muslim.
