## Page 13963

Allah’s witnesses on earth.” Yet “there was a woman in his time who openly engaged in immorality, and he said: ‘If I were to stone anyone without evidence, I would stone this woman.’”

Thus, prescribed punishments are not carried out without evidence. As for exercising caution regarding a man’s testimony, trustworthiness, and similar matters, this does not require eyewitness knowledge. Widespread reports suffice, as does information falling short of that. Indeed, a person’s character may be inferred from his associates, as Ibn Masʿūd said:

“Judge people by their close companions.”

This is to ward off his harm, just as one takes precautions against an enemy. ʿUmar ibn al-Khattāb, may Allah be pleased with him, said:

“Guard yourselves against people by being suspicious.”

This was ʿUmar’s instruction, even though it is impermissible to punish a Muslim on the basis of suspicion.

Section

As for penalties and rights pertaining to a specific individual, these include matters concerning human life. Allah Most High says:

“Say, ‘Come, I will recite what your Lord has forbidden to you: do not associate anything with Him; be good to your parents; do not kill your children out of poverty—We provide for you and for them; do not approach shameful deeds, whether open or secret; and do not take a life which Allah has made sacred, except by right. This is what He has commanded you, so that you may understand.’”

“And do not approach

---

## Page 13964

an orphan’s property except in the best manner, until he reaches maturity. Give full measure and weight with justice. We do not burden any soul beyond its capacity. When you speak, be just, even concerning a close relative. And fulfil Allah’s covenant. This is what He has commanded you, so that you may take heed.”

“And this is My path, perfectly straight, so follow it. Do not follow other paths, lest they lead you away from His path. This is what He has commanded you, so that you may be mindful of Him.”

Allah Most High also says:

“It is not for a believer to kill another believer except by mistake,”

up to His words:

“Whoever kills a believer deliberately, his recompense is Hell, where he will remain forever. Allah is angry with him, has cursed him, and has prepared for him a tremendous punishment.”

Allah Most High also says:

“Because of that, We decreed for the Children of Israel that whoever kills a soul, unless in retaliation for a life or for spreading corruption in the land, it is as though he has killed all mankind; and whoever saves a life, it is as though he has saved all mankind.”

In the two Sahīh collections, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, is reported to have said:

“The first matters to be adjudicated between people on the Day of Resurrection will be cases of bloodshed.”

Killing is of three types:

The first is intentional killing in the strict sense: deliberately targeting someone whose life one knows to be inviolable, using a means that ordinarily kills. This applies whether it kills by its sharp edge, such as a sword or the like; by its weight, such as an anvil or a fuller’s mallet; or by some other means, such as burning, drowning, throwing someone from a great height, strangling, gripping the testicles until death ensues, smothering the face until the person dies, administering poisons, or similar acts.

If someone does this, retaliatory execution becomes due. This means that the slain person’s heirs are given authority over the killer: if they wish, they may put him to death

---

## Page 13965

or, if they wish, pardon him; or, if they wish, accept blood money.

They may not kill anyone other than his killer. Allah Most High says:

“Do not take the life which Allah has made inviolable, except by right. Whoever is killed unjustly, We have given his heir authority, but let him not exceed the limits in killing, for he has been granted support.”

It has been explained in Quranic commentary as meaning: no one other than his killer may be killed.

Abū Shurayh al-Khuzā‘ī, may Allah be pleased with him, reported that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Whoever suffers a loss through bloodshed or khabal—meaning wounds—has a choice of one of three courses. If he seeks a fourth, restrain him: he may put the offender to death, pardon him, or accept blood money. Whoever takes one of these courses and then goes back on it shall have Hell, where he will abide forever and ever.”

This was reported by the compilers of the Sunan collections. Al-Tirmidhī said: “A good and authentic hadith.”

Whoever kills after granting a pardon or accepting blood money commits a graver crime than the original killer. Some scholars have even said that he must be executed as a prescribed punishment, and that his fate is not left to the slain person’s heirs. Allah Most High says:

“Retaliation is prescribed for you in cases of killing: the free for the free, the slave for the slave, and the female for the female. But if the killer is granted any pardon by his brother, then let the claim be pursued fairly and payment be made to him graciously. This is a concession and a mercy from your Lord. Whoever transgresses after that shall have a painful punishment.”

“In retaliation there is life for you, O people of understanding, so that you may be mindful of Allah.”

The scholars have said: The hearts of the slain person’s heirs boil with rage, to the point that they wish to kill both the killer and his relatives. Sometimes they are not content to kill the killer, but instead kill

---

## Page 13966

many of the killer’s associates, such as the chief of the tribe or the leader of the group. Thus, the killer commits the initial transgression, and these people transgress when exacting retribution. Such is the practice of those who follow the ways of pre-Islamic ignorance and depart from the Sharia in these times, whether Bedouins, townspeople, or others.

They may consider killing the killer too grave a matter because he is a person of standing, nobler than the victim. This leads the victim’s heirs to kill whichever of the killer’s relatives they can seize. Sometimes one side opposes a group and seeks its help, while the other does likewise with another group, leading to strife and bitter enmities. This happens because they depart from the path of justice, which is retaliation in cases of killing. Allah therefore prescribed retaliation for us—equality and equivalence in cases of killing—and declared that in it there is life. It spares the blood of everyone among the relatives of both men other than the killer. Moreover, when someone contemplating murder knows that he will be put to death, he refrains from killing.

It has been related from ‘Alī ibn Abī Tālib, may Allah be pleased with him, and from ‘Amr ibn Shu‘ayb, from his father, from his grandfather, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“The blood of all believers is of equal worth. They stand united against others, and a guarantee of protection granted by even the least of them is binding upon them all. Indeed, no Muslim shall be killed for a disbeliever, nor shall anyone under a covenant be killed while his covenant remains in force.”

This was reported by Ahmad, Abū Dāwūd, and others among the compilers of the Sunan collections. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, thus ruled that the blood of all Muslims is of equal worth—that is, equal and equivalent. No Arab is given precedence over a non-Arab, nor any Qurashī or Hāshimī over other members of

---

## Page 13967

the Muslim community. Nor is a freeborn man given precedence over a freedman, or a scholar or ruler over an unlettered person or a subordinate. This is agreed upon among Muslims.

This contrasts with the practice of the people of pre-Islamic ignorance and the Jewish rulers. Near the city of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, there were two Jewish tribes: Qurayzah and al-Nadīr. Al-Nadīr were accorded precedence over Qurayzah in matters of bloodshed. They sought the judgment of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, concerning this and the prescribed punishment for unlawful sexual intercourse, which they had changed from stoning to blackening the face. They said, “If he judges between you on that basis, you will have an argument in your favour; otherwise, you have already abandoned the ruling of the Torah.” So Allah Most High revealed:

“O Messenger, do not let those who hasten into disbelief grieve you, among those who say with their mouths, ‘We believe,’ while their hearts do not believe.”

Down to His words:

“If they come to you, judge between them or turn away from them. If you turn away from them, they cannot harm you at all. But if you judge, judge between them with justice. Indeed, Allah loves those who act justly.”

And down to His words:

“So do not fear people, but fear Me, and do not sell My verses for a small price. Whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed—it is they who are the disbelievers.”

“And We prescribed for them therein: a life for a life, an eye for an eye, a nose for a nose, an ear for an ear, a tooth for a tooth, and equal retaliation for wounds.”

Thus He, glorified and exalted, made clear that He had made their lives equal, giving no life precedence over another, as they used to do. The passage continues down to His words:

“And We have sent down to you the Book in truth

---

## Page 13968

confirming the Scripture that came before it and as a guardian over it. So judge between them by what Allah has revealed, and do not follow their desires, turning away from the truth that has come to you. To each of you We have prescribed a law and a clear way.”

Down to His words:

“Is it the judgment of pre-Islamic ignorance they seek? And who is better than Allah in judgment for people who are certain?”

Thus Allah’s ruling, glorified is He, concerning the lives of Muslims is that they are all equal, contrary to the practice of the people of pre-Islamic ignorance. Most of the partisan passions that arise among people, in the countryside and in towns, stem from oppression and the abandonment of justice. Some members of one group may wrong members of another in matters of blood or property, or one group may unjustly dominate the other and deny it fair treatment, while the other does not confine itself to obtaining its due.

Allah’s Book therefore requires that disputes between people concerning bloodshed, property, and other matters be judged with the justice Allah has commanded, and that the judgments of pre-Islamic ignorance still practised by many people be abolished. Whoever seeks to reconcile the two groups must do so justly, as Allah Most High says:

“If two groups of believers fight one another, make peace between them. But if one of them transgresses against the other, fight the transgressing group until it returns to Allah’s command. If it returns, reconcile them with justice and act equitably. Indeed, Allah loves those who act justly.”

“The believers are but brothers, so make peace between your two brothers.”

The slain person’s heirs should be asked to pardon, for that is better for them, as Allah Most High says:

“And wounds are subject to equal retaliation. But whoever forgoes it as an act of charity, it will be an expiation for him.”

Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, said: “Nothing was ever brought before the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace,

---

## Page 13969

that called for legal retaliation without his urging pardon.” Reported by Abū Dāwūd and others.

Muslim narrated in his Sahīh from Abū Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Charity does not diminish wealth. Allah only increases a servant in honour through his pardoning others, and no one humbles himself before Allah but Allah raises him.”

The equality we have mentioned applies between one free Muslim and another. As for a dhimmī (a non-Muslim subject under Muslim protection), the majority of scholars hold that he is not equal to a Muslim in this respect, just as they unanimously agree that someone granted safe-conduct who comes from the lands of the unbelievers as an envoy, merchant, or the like is not his equal. Some scholars, however, maintain that he is his equal. There is likewise disagreement over putting a free person to death for killing a slave.

The second category is unintentional killing that resembles intentional killing. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Indeed, the blood money for unintentional killing resembling intentional killing—killing with a whip or stick—is one hundred camels, including forty pregnant she-camels carrying their young.”

He called it quasi-intentional because the perpetrator intended to assault the victim by striking him, but with something that does not ordinarily kill. Thus, he intended the assault but did not intend to use a lethal means.

The third category is purely accidental killing and cases treated similarly: for example, someone shoots at game or a target but hits a person without knowing or intending it. Such a case does not entail execution in retaliation, but only blood money and expiation. There are many questions concerning these matters that are well known among scholars and discussed in their books.

---

## Page 13970

Section

Retaliation in kind for bodily injuries is also established by the Quran, the Sunnah, and scholarly consensus, provided that equivalence can be maintained. If someone severs another person’s right hand at a joint, the victim is entitled to have the offender’s hand severed in the same manner. If he knocks out his tooth, the victim is entitled to have the offender’s tooth knocked out. If he wounds his head or face, exposing the bone, the victim is entitled to have an equivalent wound inflicted upon him.

If equivalence cannot be maintained—for example, where someone fractures an internal bone or inflicts a head wound that falls short of exposing the bone—retaliation is not prescribed. Instead, the prescribed indemnity or compensation for the injury is due.

As for retaliation for blows inflicted with the hand, a stick, or a whip—such as slapping someone, punching him, or striking him with a stick and the like—a group of scholars maintain that retaliation does not apply. Rather, discretionary punishment is imposed, because equivalence cannot be maintained in such cases.

What is transmitted from the Rightly Guided Caliphs and other Companions and Successors, however, is that retaliation is prescribed in these cases. This is also the explicit position of Ahmad and other jurists, and it is established by the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. This is the correct view.

Abū Firās related that Umar ibn al-Khattāb, may Allah be pleased with him, delivered a sermon, and reported among his words:

“Take heed! By Allah, I do not send my officials to you to beat you, nor

---

## Page 13971

to take your wealth; rather, I send them to you to teach you your religion and the Sunnah of your Prophet. Whoever is treated otherwise should report it to me. By Him in Whose hand is my soul, I shall certainly exact retaliation against the offender on his behalf.”

Amr ibn al-Ās sprang up and said, “O Commander of the Faithful, if a Muslim is appointed to govern a people and disciplines them, would you really exact retaliation against him?”

He replied, “Yes, by Him in Whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, I shall certainly exact retaliation against him. I have seen the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, allow retaliation against himself. Take heed! Do not beat the Muslims and thereby humiliate them, nor withhold their rights and thereby drive them to disbelief.”

Reported by Imam Ahmad and others. This refers to a governor striking his subjects unlawfully. As for lawful striking, scholarly consensus holds that no retaliation applies, since it is obligatory, recommended, or permissible.

Section

Retaliation for affronts to honor is also prescribed. If a man curses another or supplicates against him, the latter may respond in kind. Likewise, if someone insults him, he may respond with an insult containing no falsehood. Forgiveness, however, is better.

Allah Most High says:

“The recompense for an evil deed is an evil deed like it. But whoever pardons and makes reconciliation—his reward is with Allah. Indeed, He does not love the wrongdoers.”

“And whoever defends himself after being wronged—there is no blame upon such people.”

And the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

---

## Page 13972

“When two people exchange insults, the blame for what they say rests upon the one who began, so long as the wronged party does not overstep the bounds.”

This is called defending oneself. Insults containing no falsehood include mentioning a person’s actual faults, calling him a dog or a donkey, and the like. If, however, someone fabricates a lie against another, the latter may not fabricate a lie against him in return. If someone unjustly declares him a disbeliever or an evildoer, he may not unjustly declare the other a disbeliever or an evildoer in return. Likewise, if the offender curses his father, tribe, fellow townspeople, or the like, he may not retaliate against such people, for they have not wronged him.

Allah Most High says:

“O you who believe, stand firm for Allah as witnesses in justice, and do not let hatred of a people lead you to be unjust. Be just; that is nearer to righteousness.”

Thus, Allah commands Muslims not to let their hatred of the disbelievers lead them to act unjustly. He says:

“Be just; that is nearer to righteousness.”

If an affront to someone’s honor is forbidden because it violates his right, owing to the hurt it causes him, retaliation in kind is permissible—for example, supplicating against the offender as he supplicated against him. But if it is forbidden because it violates Allah Most High’s right, as with lying, it is never permissible.

Many jurists have likewise said: If someone kills another by burning, drowning, strangling, or the like, the same is to be done to him, unless the act is forbidden in itself, such as forcing him to drink wine or committing sodomy against him.

Others have said: He may be executed in retaliation only by the sword. The former view accords more closely with the Quran, the Sunnah, and justice.

---

## Page 13973

Section

Where false accusations and similar offenses do not admit of retaliation in kind, they are subject to punishment by other means.

Among these is the prescribed punishment for accusing someone of unlawful sexual intercourse, established by the Quran, the Sunnah, and scholarly consensus. Allah Most High says:

“Those who accuse chaste women and then fail to produce four witnesses—lash them eighty times, and never accept their testimony thereafter. They are the defiantly disobedient, except those who repent afterward and reform; surely Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.”

If a free person accuses a chaste person of unlawful sexual intercourse or sodomy, he incurs the prescribed punishment for such an accusation: eighty lashes. If he accuses him of something else, he is subject to discretionary punishment. This prescribed punishment is a right belonging to the accused and, by agreement of the jurists, may be carried out only at his request. If he pardons the accuser, the punishment lapses according to the majority of scholars, because the individual’s right predominates, as with retaliation and property claims.

Another view holds that it does not lapse, giving precedence to Allah’s right because the punishment is not equivalent in kind to the offense, as with the other prescribed punishments.

The prescribed punishment for such an accusation is required only when the accused is chaste—that is, a free, chaste Muslim. As for someone notorious for sexual immorality, his accuser is not subject to this prescribed punishment. The same applies to someone who accuses a disbeliever or a slave;

---

## Page 13974

but the accuser is subject to discretionary punishment. An exception is the husband: he may accuse his wife of adultery if she has committed it without becoming pregnant as a result. If she becomes pregnant through adultery and gives birth, he must accuse her and disavow paternity of her child, lest someone who is not his offspring be attributed to him. If he accuses her, she either admits to adultery or undergoes the prescribed mutual imprecation with him, as Allah has set out in the Quran and the Sunnah.

If the accuser is a slave, he receives half the prescribed punishment imposed on a free person. The same applies to flogging for unlawful sexual intercourse and drinking wine, for Allah Most High says concerning slave women:

“If they commit sexual immorality, their punishment is half that of free women.”

However, when the required punishment is execution or amputation of the hand, it cannot be halved.

Section

Marital rights are also among these rights. Disputes between spouses must therefore be judged according to what Allah Most High has commanded: retaining the marriage on equitable terms or releasing the wife with kindness. Each spouse must willingly and wholeheartedly fulfil the other’s rights.

A wife has a financial right over her husband: her bridal payment and reasonable maintenance. She also has a right over his person: marital companionship and sexual enjoyment. Thus, if he swears to abstain from intercourse with her, she is entitled to separation, by the consensus of the Muslims. Likewise, if his penis has been amputated or he is impotent and unable to have intercourse with her, she is entitled to separation. According to most scholars, having intercourse with her is an obligation upon him.

---

## Page 13975

And it has been said that it is not obligatory, since natural desire provides sufficient motivation. The correct view, however, is that it is obligatory, as indicated by the Quran, the Sunnah, and fundamental legal principles. When the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, saw that ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr, may Allah be pleased with him, was fasting and praying extensively, he told him:

“Your wife has a right over you.”

It has been said that he must have intercourse with her once every four months. Another view is that he must have intercourse with her on reasonable terms, according to his capacity and her need, just as maintenance must likewise be provided on reasonable terms. This is the more fitting view.

The husband, in turn, has the right to sexual enjoyment with her whenever he wishes, provided that this neither harms her nor keeps her from fulfilling an obligation. She must therefore make herself available to him under these conditions. She may not leave his home without his permission or the permission of the Lawgiver.

The jurists have differed over whether she is obliged to perform household tasks, such as making the beds, sweeping, cooking, and the like. Some have said that she is obliged to do so; others have said that she is not; and others have said that only light household tasks are obligatory upon her.

Section

As for financial matters, disputes between people must be judged with justice, as Allah and His Messenger have commanded. This includes distributing inheritances among the heirs according to what is set out in

---

## Page 13976

the Quran and the Sunnah. Muslims have differed over some questions concerning this. The same applies to transactions such as sales, leases, agency agreements, partnerships, gifts, endowments, bequests, and other dealings involving contracts and transfers of possession. Justice in these matters is the mainstay of human life; well-being in this world and the Hereafter depends upon it.

Some requirements of justice in these matters are obvious and recognizable to everyone through reason: the buyer’s obligation to pay the price; the seller’s obligation to deliver the purchased goods to the buyer; the prohibition against giving short measure or weight; the obligation to be truthful and disclose relevant information; the prohibition of lying, betrayal, and deception; and the principle that a loan calls for repayment and gratitude. Other requirements are less apparent and have been laid down in the revealed laws, or in our own law as Muslims.

The transactions prohibited by the Quran and the Sunnah generally fall under securing justice and forbidding injustice, whether minor or major. These include consuming wealth wrongfully, with usury and gambling among its forms, and the kinds of usury and gambling prohibited by the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: sales involving uncertainty; habal al-habalah sales; selling birds in the air or fish in the water; sales with an unspecified payment deadline; selling livestock whose milk has been retained in their udders; sales involving concealment; mulāmasah (sales by touching); munābadhah (sales by tossing); muzābanah; muhāqalah; sham bidding; selling fruit before its soundness becomes apparent; and the forms of partnership that he prohibited

---

## Page 13977

—invalid partnerships such as sharecropping based on the crop of a specified plot of land.

Some of these matters have been disputed among Muslims because they are obscure and ambiguous. One person may regard a particular contract and transfer of possession as valid and just, while another sees in it an injustice that renders it invalid. Allah Most High says:

“Obey Allah and obey the Messenger and those in authority among you. If you disagree over anything, refer it to Allah and the Messenger, if you believe in Allah and the Last Day. That is better and best in outcome.”

The basic principle here is that no transaction people need is to be prohibited unless the Quran and the Sunnah establish its prohibition. Likewise, no act of worship through which they seek nearness to Allah is to be prescribed unless the Quran and the Sunnah establish its legitimacy. Religion is what Allah has prescribed, and what is forbidden is what Allah has forbidden. This stands in contrast to those whom Allah condemned for declaring forbidden in His religion what He had not forbidden, associating with Him that for which He had sent down no authority, and instituting for themselves religious practices for which He had given no permission. O Allah, guide us to regard as lawful what You have made lawful, as forbidden what You have forbidden, and as religion what You have prescribed.

Section

The ruler cannot dispense with consultation, for Allah Most High commanded His Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, to consult others. He Most High said:

“So pardon them and ask forgiveness for them

---

## Page 13978

and consult them in the matter. Then, when you have decided, put your trust in Allah. Indeed, Allah loves those who put their trust in Him.”

It has been reported that Abū Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, said: “No one consulted his companions more than the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.”

It has been said that Allah commanded His Prophet to consult them to foster harmony among his Companions, to provide an example for those who came after him, and to elicit their views on matters concerning which no revelation had come down, such as warfare, particular circumstances, and other matters. Others therefore have all the more reason to consult than he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

Allah praised the believers for this in His words:

“But what is with Allah is better and more lasting for those who believe and put their trust in their Lord,”

“and who avoid major sins and indecencies, and when they are angry, forgive,”

“and who respond to their Lord, establish prayer, conduct their affairs through mutual consultation, and spend out of what We have provided for them.”

When the ruler consults them, if any of them makes clear to him what must be followed from the Book of Allah, the Sunnah of His Messenger, or the consensus of the Muslims, he must follow it. No one is to be obeyed in contravention of that, however eminent he may be in religious or worldly affairs. Allah Most High says:

“O you who believe, obey Allah and obey the Messenger and those in authority among you.”

If, however, it is a matter over which the Muslims disagree, he should elicit from each of them his view and the reasoning behind it, then act upon whichever view most closely accords with the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger, as He Most High says:

“If you disagree over anything, refer it

---

## Page 13979

to Allah and the Messenger, if you believe in Allah and the Last Day. That is better and yields the best outcome.”

Those in authority fall into two categories: rulers and scholars. When they are upright, the people are upright. Each must therefore strive, in word and deed, to obey Allah and His Messenger and follow the Book of Allah. Whenever it is possible to ascertain what the Book and Sunnah indicate concerning difficult cases, that is what must be followed. If this is not possible because time is short, the person seeking the ruling lacks the ability, the evidence appears equally balanced to him, or for some other reason, he may follow someone whose knowledge and religious commitment he trusts. This is the strongest view.

It has also been said that he may not follow another scholar’s judgment under any circumstances; and it has been said that he may do so under all circumstances. All three views are found within the school of Ahmad and those of others.

Likewise, the qualifications required of judges and governors must be fulfilled as far as possible. Indeed, the same applies to all acts of worship, including prayer, jihad, and others: all are obligatory when one is able. As for inability, Allah does not burden any soul beyond its capacity. Thus, Allah has commanded the person praying to purify himself with water. If he cannot find it, or fears harm from using it because of severe cold, a wound, or some other reason, he should perform dry purification with clean earth, wiping his face and hands with it.

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said to ‘Imrān ibn Husayn:

“Pray standing; if you cannot, then sitting; and if you cannot, then lying on your side.”

Allah has thus made it obligatory to perform prayer at its prescribed time in whatever manner is possible, as He Most High says:

“Maintain

---

## Page 13980

the prayers, especially the middle prayer, and stand before Allah in devout obedience.”

“If you fear danger, then pray on foot or riding. But when you are safe, remember Allah as He has taught you what you did not know.”

Allah has thus made prayer obligatory upon those who are safe and those who are afraid, the healthy and the sick, the rich and the poor, residents and travellers. He has eased its requirements for travellers, those in fear, and the sick, as explained in the Book and Sunnah.

Likewise, He has prescribed requirements for prayer, including purification, covering oneself, and facing the direction of prayer, while waiving whatever a person is unable to fulfil. Thus, if people are shipwrecked or robbers strip them of their clothes, they should pray naked as their circumstances allow, with their imam standing among them so that the others do not see his private parts. If they are uncertain of the direction of prayer, they should do their utmost to determine it from the available signs. If no signs can be discerned, they should pray in whatever direction they can, as it is reported that people did during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

The same applies to jihad, positions of authority, and all other religious matters. All of this is encompassed by the words of Allah Most High:

“So fear Allah as much as you are able.”

And by the words of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

“When I command you to do something, do as much of it as you are able.”

Likewise, when Allah Most High prohibited unwholesome foods, He said:

“But whoever is compelled by necessity, neither desiring it nor exceeding the limit, incurs no sin.”

Allah Most High also says:

“He has placed no hardship upon you in religion.”

And Allah Most High says:

“Allah does not intend to place upon you any

---

## Page 13981

hardship.” Thus, He has not made obligatory what is beyond one’s ability, nor prohibited what necessity compels one to use, provided that the necessity does not arise from disobedience on the servant’s part.

Section

It must be understood that governing people’s affairs is among the greatest religious obligations. Indeed, neither religion nor worldly life can be maintained without it. Human beings can only secure their well-being by living together, because they need one another; and whenever they come together, they must have a leader. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, even said:

“When three people set out on a journey, let them appoint one of themselves as their leader.”

Abū Dāwūd narrated this from Abū Saʿīd and Abū Hurayrah.

Imam Ahmad narrated in al-Musnad, from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr, that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“It is not lawful for three people to be in a deserted stretch of land without appointing one of themselves as their leader.”

By making it obligatory to appoint a single leader over even a small, temporary gathering during a journey, he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, indicated that this applies to all other forms of gathering. Moreover, Allah Most High has made enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong obligatory, and this cannot be fully accomplished without power and leadership. Likewise, the other duties He has prescribed—jihad, upholding justice, organizing Hajj, Friday prayers and Eid prayers, supporting the oppressed, and enforcing the prescribed punishments—cannot be fully accomplished without power and leadership.

For this reason, it is reported:

“The ruler is Allah’s shade on earth.”

---

## Page 13982

And it is said:

“Sixty years under an unjust ruler are better than a single night without a ruler.”

Experience bears this out. For this reason, the early generations—such as al-Fudayl ibn ʿIyād, Ahmad ibn Hanbal, and others—used to say: “If we had one supplication guaranteed to be answered, we would offer it for the ruler.”

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Allah is pleased with three things for you: that you worship Him without associating anything with Him, that you hold firmly together to the rope of Allah and do not become divided, and that you offer sincere counsel to those whom Allah has placed in charge of your affairs.”

Narrated by Muslim.

He also said:

“Three things keep a Muslim’s heart free of treachery: doing deeds sincerely for Allah, offering sincere counsel to those in authority, and remaining with the Muslim community, for their call encompasses them from behind.”

Narrated by the compilers of the Sunan.

It is also authentically reported that he said:

“Religion is sincerity. Religion is sincerity. Religion is sincerity.”

They asked, “Towards whom, O Messenger of Allah?”

He replied, “Towards Allah, His Book, His Messenger, the leaders of the Muslims, and their common people.”

It is therefore obligatory to regard holding authority as a religious responsibility and a means of drawing near to Allah. Drawing near to Him in this role through obedience to Him and His Messenger is among the finest acts of devotion. Most people become corrupt in this role only because they use it to pursue power or wealth.

Kaʿb ibn Mālik narrated that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Two hungry wolves let loose in a sheepfold are no more destructive to it than a person’s eagerness for wealth and prestige is to his religion.”

Al-Tirmidhī said: “A good and authentic hadith.” He thus explained that a person’s eagerness for wealth and power

---

## Page 13983

corrupts his religion as much as, or more than, two hungry wolves ravage a sheepfold.

Allah Most High has told us that the one given his record in his left hand will say:

“My wealth has been of no avail to me.”

“My authority has vanished from me.”

The ultimate ambition of one who seeks power is to be like Pharaoh, and of one who amasses wealth, to be like Qārūn. Allah Most High has explained the fate of Pharaoh and Qārūn in His Book, saying:

“Have they not travelled through the land and seen how those before them met their end? They were mightier than them and left greater marks upon the earth, yet Allah seized them for their sins, and they had no one to protect them from Allah.”

He also says:

“That home of the Hereafter We reserve for those who seek neither supremacy on earth nor corruption. The best outcome is for those mindful of Allah.”

People fall into four categories:

The first category consists of those who seek supremacy over others and corruption on earth—that is, disobedience to Allah. These are corrupt kings and leaders, such as Pharaoh and his followers. They are the worst of creation. Allah Most High says:

“Indeed, Pharaoh exalted himself in the land and divided its people into factions, oppressing one group among them, slaughtering their sons and sparing their women. He was truly one of those who spread corruption.”

Muslim narrated in his Sahīh that Ibn Masʿūd, may Allah be pleased with him, reported that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“No one with an atom’s weight of arrogance in his heart will enter Paradise, nor will anyone enter the Fire who

---

## Page 13984

has an atom’s weight of faith in his heart.” A man said, “O Messenger of Allah, I like my clothes and shoes to look fine. Is that arrogance?” He replied, “No. Allah is beautiful and loves beauty. Arrogance is rejecting the truth and looking down on people.” Rejecting the truth means repudiating and denying it; looking down on people means despising and belittling them. This is the condition of those who seek supremacy and corruption.

The second category consists of those who seek corruption without supremacy, such as thieves and criminals among the basest of people.

The third category consists of those who seek supremacy without corruption, such as people with religious devotion who seek thereby to rise above others.

As for the fourth category, they are the people of Paradise, who seek neither supremacy on earth nor corruption, even though they may be above others. As Allah Most High says:

“Do not lose heart or grieve, for you will have the upper hand if you are believers.”

He also says:

“So do not lose heart and call for peace while you have the upper hand. Allah is with you and will never deprive you of the reward of your deeds.”

And He says:

“To Allah belongs all honour, and to His Messenger and the believers.”

How many seek supremacy, only to sink ever lower! And how many are raised above others without seeking supremacy or corruption! This is because the desire for supremacy

---

## Page 13985

over others is an injustice, for all people share the same humanity. A person’s desire to stand above his equal and place him beneath himself is therefore unjust. Besides being unjust, such a person is hated and opposed by others: the just among them do not wish to be subjugated by their equals, while the unjust prefer to be the ones who subjugate others. Nevertheless, both reason and religion require that some people be above others, as we have already explained, just as a body cannot function properly without a head.

Allah Most High says:

“It is He who has made you successors upon the earth and raised some of you above others in rank, to test you through what He has given you.”

And He says:

“We have apportioned among them their livelihood in the life of this world and raised some of them above others in rank, so that some may employ others in their service.”

Thus, the Sharia directs that authority and wealth be devoted to Allah’s cause. When the purpose of authority and wealth is to draw closer to Allah and devote them to His cause, both religious and worldly affairs are set right. But when authority is separated from religion, or religion from authority, people’s affairs become corrupt. Those who obey Allah are distinguished from those who disobey Him only by their intentions and righteous deeds, as reported in the two Sahīh collections from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

“Allah does not look at your appearance or your wealth; rather, He looks at your hearts and your deeds.”

When the desire for wealth and prestige came to dominate many rulers [and] (1) they became estranged from the reality of faith in their exercise of authority, many people came to believe that rulership

## Page 13986

was incompatible with faith and the perfection of religion. Some therefore gave priority to religion and turned away from those means without which it cannot be fully established. Others recognized their need for such means and embraced them while turning away from religion, believing it incompatible with them. Religion thus became, in their eyes, a matter of compassion and lowliness, rather than ascendancy and honor.

Likewise, when many religious people became unable to establish religion fully and were overcome by distress at the trials they might suffer in upholding it, those who saw that neither their own interests nor those of others could be served by this approach regarded it as weak and abject.

These two corrupt paths—the path of those who profess religion but fail to complete it with the authority, jihad, and wealth it requires, and the path of those who pursue authority, wealth, and warfare without intending thereby to establish religion—are the paths of those who have incurred Allah’s anger and those who have gone astray. The first is that of the Christians who have gone astray; the second is that of the Jews who have incurred His anger.

The straight path, however—the path of those upon whom Allah has bestowed His favor: the prophets, the steadfastly truthful, the martyrs, and the righteous—is the way of our Prophet Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, his caliphs, his Companions, and those who follow their way. They are those described in the verse:

“And the first forerunners among the Emigrants and the Helpers and those who followed them in goodness—Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him. He has prepared for them gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide forever. That is

---

## Page 13987

the great triumph.”

The Muslim must therefore strive toward this to the best of his ability. Whoever assumes a position of authority intending thereby to obey Allah, uphold as much of His religion as he can, and serve the interests of the Muslims, and fulfills whatever duties he can while avoiding whatever prohibitions he can, will not be held accountable for what lies beyond his ability. Appointing the righteous is better for the Muslim community than appointing the wicked.

Whoever is unable to uphold religion through authority and jihad, but does what he can through sincere concern in his heart, supplication for the Muslim community, love of goodness, and whatever good deeds he can perform, is not charged with what lies beyond his ability. Religion is sustained by the guiding Book and the supporting iron, as Allah Most High has mentioned. Everyone must therefore strive to bring the Quran and iron together for the sake of Allah Most High, seeking what is with Him and asking His help in doing so. Worldly affairs will then serve religion, as Muʿādh ibn Jabal, may Allah be pleased with him, said:

“O son of Adam, you need your share of this world, but you need your share of the Hereafter even more. If you begin with your share of the Hereafter, your share of this world will follow and fall fully into place. But if you begin with your share of this world, you will miss your share of the Hereafter, while your worldly share remains uncertain.”

The evidence for this is what al-Tirmidhī narrated from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

“Whoever begins the day with the Hereafter as his greatest concern, Allah will set his affairs in order, place richness in his heart, and make this world come to him despite itself. But whoever begins the day with this world as his greatest concern, Allah will throw his affairs into disarray

---

## Page 13988

and place poverty before his eyes, and nothing of this world will come to him except what He has decreed for him.”

The foundation of this is His saying, Most High:

“I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me.”

“I seek no provision from them, nor do I ask that they feed Me.”

“Indeed, Allah alone is the Provider, the Possessor of Power, the Strong.”

We therefore ask Allah the Magnificent to guide us, all our brethren, and all Muslims to the words and deeds He loves and approves for us. There is no power nor strength except through Allah, the Most High, the Magnificent. All praise is due to Allah, Lord of all worlds. May Allah grant our master Muhammad, his family, and his Companions blessings and abundant peace, enduring until the Day of Judgment.

## Page 13989

Shaykh al-Islām wrote to al-Malik al-Nāsir after the battle of Mount Keserwan, concerning the conquest of the mountain:

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Ever Merciful.

From Ahmad ibn Taymiyyah, who prays for you, to the Sultan of the Muslims, in whose reign Allah has strengthened the religion, honored His believing servants, and subdued the disbelievers, the hypocrites, and the renegade Khawārij. May Allah grant him victory and grant Islam victory through him; set right, for him and through him, the affairs of the elite and the common people; revive through him the signs of faith; establish through him the ordinances of the Quran; and humble through him the people of disbelief, wickedness, and disobedience.

Peace be upon you, and Allah’s mercy and blessings. In addressing you, we praise Allah, besides whom there is no god. He is worthy of all praise and has power over all things. We ask Him to bestow blessings upon the Seal of the Prophets and leader of the God-fearing, Muhammad, His servant and Messenger—may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace.

To proceed: Allah has indeed fulfilled His promise, granted victory to His servant, honored His army, and alone defeated the confederates. Allah has bestowed upon the Sultan and the believers during his reign blessings unprecedented in past centuries. He has brought about such a renewal of Islam during his reign

---

## Page 13990

that it has clearly surpassed what was achieved under earlier dynasties. During his rule, the report of the truthful and trustworthy one, the best of all generations, has been fulfilled: he foretold the renewal of the religion at the turn of every century. May Allah Most High inspire him and the Muslims to give thanks for these immense blessings in worldly and religious affairs, and complete them by granting complete victory over all the remaining renegade enemies.

To explain: under the Sultan—may Allah perfect His blessing upon him—the Muslim community has attained achievements resembling those witnessed in the days of the Rightly Guided Caliphs and sought by the greatest just rulers. This has come through the blessings of his rule, his good intentions, the soundness of his Islam and creed, the blessing of his faith and knowledge, his lofty resolve and courage, his reverence for the religion and its law, and his adherence to Allah’s Book and wisdom.

These achievements include waging jihad against Allah’s enemies who have broken away from the religion. They fall into two categories. The first consists of people of wickedness and tyranny, error and aggression, who depart from the laws of faith in pursuit of supremacy and corruption on earth, abandoning the path of guidance and righteousness. These are the Tatars and others like them who depart from the laws of Islam, even if they hold fast to the two testimonies of faith or to some aspects of Islamic governance.

The second category consists of renegade adherents of religious innovation and hypocritical followers of misguidance who depart from the Sunnah and the Muslim community, abandoning divine law and obedience, such as these people

---

## Page 13991

who campaigned at the Sultan’s command, from among the people of al-Jabal, al-Jurd, and Kisrawān. The conquest and victory Allah has granted over these wretches are among the momentous blessings He has bestowed upon the Sultan and the Muslims.

This is because these people and their like are among the greatest perpetrators of corruption in worldly and religious affairs.

Their belief is that Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, ʿUthmān, those who fought at Badr and those who took the Pledge of Divine Pleasure, the great majority of the Emigrants and Helpers and those who followed them in righteousness, the imams and scholars of Islam belonging to the four schools and others, the religious masters and devout worshippers of Islam, Muslim rulers and their soldiers, ordinary Muslims and individual members of the community—all these, in their view, are unbelievers and apostates, more unbelieving than the Jews and Christians. This is because they regard them as apostates, and an apostate is worse than someone who was an unbeliever from the outset. For this reason, they favor the Franks and Tatars over the people of the Quran and faith.

Thus, when the Tatars came to the land, they inflicted untold devastation upon the Muslim army and sent word to the people of Cyprus, who seized part of the coast. They raised the banner of the cross and transported to Cyprus Muslim horses, weapons, and captives in numbers known only to Allah. Their market was held on the coast for twenty days, during which they sold Muslims, horses, and weapons to the people of Cyprus. They rejoiced at the Tatars’ arrival, as did all the other adherents of this accursed doctrine, such as the people of Jazzīn and its surroundings, and Jabal ʿĀmil and its neighboring districts.

---

## Page 13992

And when the Muslim armies set out from Egypt, the disgrace and chastisement that became apparent among these people were plain for others to see. When Allah granted Islam its great victory upon the Sultan’s arrival, they were in something like mourning. All this and worse is found among this sect, which was among the foremost causes of Genghis Khan’s invasion of the lands of Islam, Hulagu’s seizure of Baghdad and advance upon Aleppo, the plundering of al-Sālihiyya, and other acts of hostility towards Islam and its people.

For they hold that anyone who does not agree with their misguidance is an unbeliever and an apostate. Whoever regards fuqqāʿ (a foaming barley drink) as lawful is an unbeliever. Whoever wipes over his leather socks is, in their view, an unbeliever. Whoever holds temporary marriage to be forbidden is, in their view, an unbeliever.

Whoever loves Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, or ʿUthmān, or invokes Allah’s pleasure upon them or upon the great majority of the Companions, is, in their view, an unbeliever. Whoever does not believe in their awaited one is, in their view, an unbeliever. This awaited one is a child aged two, three, or five. They claim that he entered the cellar in Samarra more than four hundred years ago, that he knows everything, and that he is Allah’s proof to the people of the earth. Whoever does not believe in him is, in their view, an unbeliever. Yet he has no reality; no such person has ever existed.

They also hold that whoever says that Allah will be seen in the Hereafter is an unbeliever. And whoever says:

---

## Page 13993

“Allah truly spoke the Quran” is an unbeliever. Whoever says, “Allah is above the heavens,” is an unbeliever. Whoever believes in divine decree and predestination and says that Allah guides whom He wills and leads astray whom He wills, that Allah turns the hearts of His servants, and that Allah is the Creator of all things is, in their view, an unbeliever. They also regard anyone who believes in the reality of Allah’s names and attributes, which He has made known in His Book and through His Messenger, as an unbeliever.

This is the doctrine their leaders teach them, such as the Banū al-ʿŪd, who are the religious leaders of the people of this mountain. They were the ones who ordered them to fight the Muslims and issued religious rulings endorsing these matters. A number of their books, written by Ibn al-ʿŪd and others, have come into Muslim hands. They contain these things and worse. They themselves admitted to us that they were the ones who had taught and commanded these people. Yet despite this, they engage in dissimulation and hypocrisy, and seek favor by giving money to anyone willing to accept it from them.

Such has been the customary practice of these mountain people. They were only able to remain in their mountain because of the hypocrisy they displayed and the bribes they paid to those who came against them. Their stronghold is exceedingly difficult to reach. Those familiar with such terrain stated that they had never seen anything like it. Thus their wrongdoing multiplied: they killed so many people and seized so much wealth that Allah alone knows its extent.

---

## Page 13994

Indeed, their neighbors in the Beqaa and elsewhere suffered immeasurable harm at their hands. Every night, a band of them would descend upon their neighbors and commit acts of wrongdoing whose extent none but the Lord of all servants could reckon. In their highway robbery and terrorizing of people in their homes, they followed the most atrocious practices known among criminals. Christians from Cyprus would come to them, and they would offer them hospitality and give them the Muslims’ weapons. Yet they would attack a righteous Muslim, either killing him or robbing him. Few escaped them, and then only through ingenuity.

Allah granted assistance and made it possible—through the sultan’s sincere intention, his resolve to uphold the laws of Islam, and his concern to wage jihad against those who had departed from Islam—for a lawful military expedition to be undertaken against them, as Allah and His Messenger commanded. This came after their circumstances had been exposed, their excuses removed, and their misconceptions dispelled; after they had been offered justice and fairness beyond anything they could have hoped for; and after it had been explained to them that the expedition against them followed the example of the Commander of the Faithful, ʿAlī ibn Abī Tālib, may Allah be pleased with him, in fighting the Harūriyya who had departed from Islam. The Prophet’s command to fight them, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, is established by mass transmission, and his descriptions of them have been reported through numerous channels.

The compilers of the authentic hadith collections recorded ten such routes of transmission, through reports from ʿAlī ibn Abī Tālib, Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, Sahl ibn Hunayf, Abū Dharr al-Ghifārī, Rāfiʿ ibn ʿAmr, and other Companions of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

He said of them:

“One of you will consider his own prayer insignificant compared with theirs, and his own fasting compared with theirs

## Page 13995

and his own recitation compared with theirs. They recite the Quran, but it does not pass beyond their throats. They pass out of Islam as an arrow passes through its quarry. If those who fight them knew what reward awaits them, as declared by Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, they would cease striving. They kill the people of Islam and leave the idolaters alone. They recite the Quran, thinking that it supports them, whereas it stands against them. Yet they had departed from the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and from the Muslim community. They killed a Muslim named ʿAbdullāh ibn Khabbāb and raided the Muslims’ livestock.

These people, by contrast, prayed and fasted less. We found neither a copy of the Quran on their mountain nor anyone among them who recited it. All they had were their doctrines, through which they contradicted the Book and the Sunnah and deemed the Muslims’ blood lawful to shed. Moreover, they shed blood and seized wealth in quantities known only to Allah Most High.

If, then, ʿAlī ibn Abī Tālib permitted his army to plunder what was in the camp of the Khawārij, even though he killed them all, these people were all the more deserving of having their property seized. These people are not

## Page 13996

on the same footing as those acting on an interpretation, concerning whom ʿAlī ibn Abī Tālib proclaimed on the Day of the Camel that he would not kill those who fled, finish off their wounded, take their wealth as booty, or enslave their offspring. Those people had an admissible interpretation, whereas these people have no admissible interpretation. People like the former merely rebel against the ruler’s authority, whereas these people have departed from the law and Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

They are worse than the Tatars in numerous respects, but the Tatars are more numerous and more powerful, so the extent of their evil is more apparent. Much of the Tatars’ corruption results from these people’s association with them, as happened in the time of Ghāzān, Hūlākū, and others. For they took from the Muslims’ wealth many times what was taken from their own. Their land is fay’ (property accruing to the public treasury).

Many of the early generations stated that the Rāfidah have no share in fay’, because Allah assigned it only to the Emigrants, the Helpers, and:

“Those who came after them, saying, ‘Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith, and do not place in our hearts any resentment toward those who believe. Our Lord, You are indeed Most Kind, Most Merciful.’”

Anyone whose heart is not free of ill will toward them and whose tongue does not seek forgiveness for them is not among these people.

Their trees were cut down “because when the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, besieged Banū al-Nadīr, his Companions cut down their date palms and burned them. The Jews said, ‘This is corruption, yet you

---

## Page 13997

O Muhammad, forbid corruption.’ Then Allah revealed:

‘Whatever palm trees you cut down or left standing on their roots was by Allah’s permission, so that He might disgrace the defiantly disobedient.’”

The scholars have agreed that cutting down trees and destroying developed property is permissible when necessary. This is no graver than taking lives, and no other course was possible. It was only when the trees were cut down that all these people came out from their hiding places and abandoned hope of remaining on the mountain. Otherwise, they would hide where they could not be found. Nor was it possible for others to settle on the mountain: the Turkomans sought only pasture, which had now become available to them, while the other farmers would not abandon the cultivation of their own lands and come there. Praise be to Allah, who facilitated this victory during the Sultan’s reign, through his zeal, determination and command, as well as the clearing of the mountain of these people and their expulsion from their homes.

They resemble those whom Allah described in His words:

“He is the One who expelled those who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture from their homes at the first gathering. They destroyed their houses with their own hands and the hands of the believers. So take heed, O people of insight.”

“Had Allah not decreed exile for them, He would have punished them in this world; and in the Hereafter they will suffer the punishment of the Fire.”

“That is because they opposed Allah and His Messenger. And whoever opposes

## Page 13998

Allah—Allah is indeed severe in punishment.”

“Whatever palm trees you cut down or left standing on their roots was by Allah’s permission, so that He might disgrace the defiantly disobedient.”

Moreover, this has dealt the people of innovation and hypocrisy in Syria, Egypt, the Hijaz, Yemen and Iraq a blow through which Allah will raise the Sultan’s rank and strengthen the believers.

Section

The completion of this victory and its blessings lie in the issuance of the Sultan’s decrees to cut off what sustains those who spread corruption and to establish the Sharia throughout the lands. These people have shaykhs and brethren in many villages whom they follow and whose cause they champion. They harbour deep resentment and intense, concealed hostility, such that they cannot be trusted to refrain from whatever harm lies within their power, even if it amounts only to covert collaboration with the enemy. If their leaders who misguide them—such as the Banū al-‘Ūd—are apprehended, this will eliminate an extent of evil known only to Allah.

Orders should be sent to their villages, which are scattered throughout the districts of Damascus, Safad, Tripoli, Hama, Homs and Aleppo, that the observances of Islam be established among them: Friday prayers, congregational prayers and recitation of the Quran. They should have preachers and muezzins

---

## Page 13999

as in other Muslim villages. The prophetic hadiths should be read among them, the teachings of Islam disseminated among them, and those among them known for innovation and hypocrisy punished as prescribed by Islamic law.

These combatants and others like them have said: “We are ignorant people. These men used to teach us and tell us: ‘If you fight these people, you will be fighting in Allah’s cause, and whoever among you is killed will be a martyr.’”

Among these people are many who acknowledge neither prayer, fasting, Hajj nor ‘umrah (the lesser pilgrimage); who do not regard carrion, blood or pork as forbidden; and who do not believe in Paradise or Hell. They are of the same kind as the Ismā‘īliyyah, Nusayriyyah, Hākimiyyah and Bātiniyyah. By the consensus of the Muslims, they are disbelievers whose disbelief is more extreme than that of the Jews and Christians.

The issuance of the Sultan’s decrees establishing the observances of Islam—Friday prayers, congregational prayers, recitation of the Quran and transmission of the hadiths of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace—in these people’s villages is therefore among the greatest measures serving the interests of Islam and the most effective forms of jihad in Allah’s cause. This will help restrain those among them who secretly collaborate with the enemy and bring them into obedience to Allah and His Messenger and to those in authority among the Muslims. It is also among the means through which Allah helps subdue the enemies. What they did to the Muslims in the land of “Sīs” is an instance of their treachery through which Allah grants the Muslims victory over them. In this there is wisdom from Allah

that is profound, and mighty support for Islam.

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

to him, a guardian over the Scriptures that preceded it and a confirmation of them. in a number of false claimants to prophethood, such as Musaylima the Liar, Tulayha al-Asadī, and others. Their army comprises four groups:

Disbelievers who remain in their disbelief, from among the Georgians, Armenians, and Mongols.

A group who were Muslims but apostatized from Islam and turned back on their heels, from among the Arabs, Persians, Byzantines, and others. These people bear greater guilt in the sight of Allah

---

## Page 14005

and of His Messenger and the believers, than those who have always been disbelievers, in many respects. They must be put to death unless they return to what they abandoned. So long as they remain apostates, it is impermissible, by consensus, to grant them a covenant of protection, a truce, or safe-conduct; their captives may neither be released nor exchanged for money or men; their slaughtered animals may not be eaten, their women may not be married, and they may not be enslaved. Those among them who fight and those who do not—including the decrepit elderly, the blind, and the infirm—are to be put to death, by agreement of the scholars. The same applies to their women according to the majority.

By contrast, someone who has always been a disbeliever may be granted safe-conduct or a truce. According to the majority, if taken captive, he may be released without ransom or exchanged for ransom. If he belongs to the People of the Book, he may be granted a covenant of protection; their food may be eaten and their women married. Their women are not to be killed unless they participate in fighting through words or deeds, by agreement of the scholars. Likewise, according to the majority of scholars, only those among them who are counted among combatants may be killed, as the Sunnah indicates.

Thus, an apostate disbeliever is in a worse position, in both religious and worldly terms, than a disbeliever who has remained in his disbelief. Among these people are apostates whose numbers only Allah can reckon. These, then, are two groups.

There are also among them people who were disbelievers and then professed affiliation with Islam without committing themselves to its laws, such as establishing prayer, giving zakat, performing pilgrimage to the House, and refraining from shedding the blood of

Muslims or seizing their property, undertaking jihad in Allah’s cause, levying the jizya on Jews and Christians, and so forth. ## Page 14007

Islam while continuing to cling to their affiliation with it.

This is if they remain in their own territory. How much more so if they seize Muslim lands—Iraq, Khurāsān, al-Jazīra, and Rūm? And how much more so if they advance against you and assault you unjustly and aggressively?

“Will you not fight a people who broke their oaths and intended to expel the Messenger, and who attacked you first? Do you fear them? Allah is more worthy of your fear, if you are believers.”

“Fight them: Allah will punish them at your hands, disgrace them, grant you victory over them, and heal the hearts of a believing people.”

“And He will remove the rage from their hearts. Allah turns in mercy to whomever He wills. Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.”

Know—may Allah set you right—that it is authentically established through numerous routes that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“A group of my community will continue to uphold the truth victoriously, unharmed by those who abandon them or oppose them, until the Hour comes.”

It is also established that they are in Syria.

In this turmoil, people have divided into three factions: the victorious faction, consisting of those who wage jihad against these people who spread corruption; and the opposing faction, consisting of these

---

## Page 14008

people and the corrupt elements among those affiliated with Islam who have sided with them; and the faction that withholds support, consisting of those who refrain from waging jihad against them, even if their Islam is sound. Let each man consider whether he belongs to the victorious faction, the faction that withholds support, or the opposing faction. There is no fourth category.

Know that jihad brings the good of this world and the Hereafter, while abandoning it brings loss in this world and the Hereafter. Allah Most High says in His Book:

“Say, ‘Are you waiting for anything to befall us except one of the two best outcomes?’”

This means either victory and triumph, or martyrdom and Paradise. Those who survive among those who wage jihad live in honour, receiving the reward of this world and the excellent reward of the Hereafter. Those who die or are killed go to Paradise. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“The martyr is granted six privileges: he is forgiven with the first drop of his blood; he is shown his place in Paradise; he is clothed in a garment of faith; he is married to seventy-two wide-eyed maidens of Paradise; he is protected from the trial of the grave; and he is kept safe from the greatest terror.”

This was narrated by the compilers of the Sunan. He also said, may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

“In Paradise there are one hundred ranks, with a distance between each rank and the next like that between heaven and earth. Allah, glorified and exalted is He, has prepared them for those who wage jihad in His cause.”

Thus, those who wage jihad have an elevation in Paradise spanning fifty thousand years. He also said, may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

“The one who wages jihad in Allah’s cause is like someone who fasts and stands in devout prayer, never ceasing to pray or fast.”

“A man said, ‘Tell me of a deed that equals jihad in Allah’s cause?’

He replied, ‘You cannot do it.’

The man said:

---

## Page 14009

‘Tell me what it is.’

He replied, ‘When the one who wages jihad sets out, can you fast without breaking your fast and stand in prayer without resting?’

The man replied, ‘No.’

He said, ‘That is what equals jihad in Allah’s cause.’”

These hadiths are found in the two Sahīh collections and elsewhere. Likewise, the scholars have agreed—as far as I know—that no voluntary act of worship is superior to jihad. It is superior to voluntary pilgrimage, fasting, and prayer. Standing guard in Allah’s cause is superior to residing for worship in Mecca, Medina, or Jerusalem. Indeed, Abū Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, said: “To spend one night standing guard in Allah’s cause is dearer to me than to be present on the Night of Decree beside the Black Stone.” Thus, he preferred one night of guard duty to worship on the best of nights in the best of places.

For this reason, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and his Companions resided in Medina rather than Mecca, for several reasons, including that they were standing guard in Medina. Guard duty means remaining in a place that is threatened by the enemy and itself poses a threat to the enemy. Whoever stays there with the intention of repelling the enemy is standing guard, and deeds are judged by intentions. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“One day of guard duty in Allah’s cause is better than a thousand days spent in other places.”

This was narrated by the compilers of the Sunan, who graded it authentic. In Sahīh Muslim, Salmān reported that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“One day and night of guard duty in Allah’s cause is better than a month of fasting and standing in prayer. Whoever dies while standing guard will continue to receive the reward for his deeds, will continue to receive his provision from Paradise, and will be safe from the interrogators.”

That is, Munkar and Nakīr. Such is the merit of guard duty; how much greater, then, is that of jihad!

---

## Page 14010

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Dust encountered in Allah’s cause and the smoke of Hell will never come together on a servant’s face.”

He also said:

“Whoever’s feet become dusty in Allah’s cause, Allah will forbid the Fire to touch them.”

This concerns merely the dust that reaches one’s face and feet. What, then, of greater hardships, such as snow, cold, and mud? For this reason, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, condemned the hypocrites who make excuses on account of obstacles such as heat and cold. He, Glorified and Exalted, said:

“Those who were left behind rejoiced at staying behind the Messenger of Allah. They were unwilling to strive with their wealth and their lives in Allah’s cause, and said, ‘Do not go forth in the heat.’ Say, ‘The Fire of Hell is fiercer in heat’—if only they understood.”

Likewise, those who say, “Do not go forth in the cold,” should be told, “The Fire of Hell is more intensely cold.” For al-Bukhārī and Muslim both narrated in their Sahīh collections that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“The Fire complained to its Lord, saying, ‘My Lord, parts of me have consumed other parts.’ So He permitted it two breaths: one in winter and one in summer. Thus, the most intense heat and cold you experience comes from the bitter cold of Hell.”

By patiently enduring heat and cold in Allah’s cause, the believer wards off the heat and cold of Hell. The hypocrite, however, flees the heat and cold of this world, only to fall into the heat and bitter cold of Hell.

Know—may Allah set you right—that victory belongs to the believers, that the final outcome belongs to the God-fearing, and that Allah is with those who fear Him and those who do good. These people are subdued and crushed. Allah, Glorified and Exalted, supports us against them and takes vengeance on them for us. There is no power and no strength except through Allah, the Most High, the Almighty. So rejoice in Allah Most High’s help and in the good

---

## Page 14011

outcome.

“Do not lose heart or grieve, for you will have the upper hand, if you are believers.”

This is something of which we have become certain and which we have verified. All praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds.

“O you who believe, shall I direct you to a trade that will save you from a painful punishment?”

“Believe in Allah and His Messenger and strive in Allah’s cause with your wealth and your lives. That is better for you, if only you knew.”

“He will forgive your sins and admit you into gardens beneath which rivers flow, and into pleasant dwellings in Gardens of Eternity. That is the supreme triumph.”

“And another blessing that you love: help from Allah and a victory near at hand. And give glad tidings to the believers.”

“O you who believe, be supporters of Allah, as Jesus, son of Mary, said to the disciples, ‘Who will support me in Allah’s cause?’ The disciples said, ‘We are Allah’s supporters.’ Then a group of the Children of Israel believed, while another group disbelieved. So We supported those who believed against their enemy, and they prevailed.”

Know—may Allah set you right—that one of the greatest blessings for someone for whom Allah intends good is that He has kept him alive until this time, when Allah renews the religion and revives the distinctive practices of the Muslims and the ways of the believers and those who fight in His cause, so that he may resemble the earliest forerunners among the Emigrants and the Helpers. Whoever rises to this task at this time will be among those who follow them in righteousness, with whom Allah is pleased and who are pleased with Him. He has prepared for them gardens beneath which rivers flow, where they will abide forever. That is the supreme triumph. Thus, the believers should thank Allah Most High for this ordeal, which

---

## Page 14012

is in reality a generous gift from Allah, and for this trial that conceals an immense blessing. Indeed, by Allah, were the earliest forerunners among the Emigrants and the Helpers—such as Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, ʿUthmān, ʿAlī and others—present in this age, fighting these criminal people would be among their finest deeds. Only someone whose trade has brought him loss, who has shown himself a fool and been deprived of a great share of good in this world and the Hereafter would miss a campaign such as this—unless he is among those whom Allah Most High has excused, such as the sick, the poor, the blind and others. Anyone who possesses wealth but is physically unable to fight should support the campaign with his wealth.

It is reported in the two Sahīh collections that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Whoever equips a fighter has himself taken part in the fighting, and whoever takes good care of the fighter’s family in his absence has himself taken part in the fighting.”

Anyone who is physically able but poor should obtain enough of the Muslims’ wealth to equip himself, whether it comes from zakat, a gift, the public treasury or another source. Even if a man has come into possession of unlawfully acquired wealth and cannot return it to its owners because he does not know who they are or for a similar reason, or if he holds deposits, pledged items or borrowed articles whose owners cannot be identified, he should spend them in Allah’s cause, for that is their proper destination.

For someone burdened with many sins, the greatest remedy is fighting in Allah’s cause, for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will forgive his sins, as He has declared in His Book, saying—glorified and exalted is He:

“He will forgive your sins.”

Anyone who wishes to rid himself of unlawfully acquired wealth and repent, but cannot return it to its owners, should spend it in Allah’s cause on their behalf, for that is a sound path to

---

## Page 14013

freeing himself of it, besides the reward he earns for fighting in Allah’s cause. Likewise, anyone who wishes Allah to expiate his sins of invoking the rallying cries of pre-Islamic ignorance and displaying its partisan zeal should fight in Allah’s cause. Those who take sides out of loyalty to tribes or other groupings—such as Qays, Yaman, Hilāl, Asad and the like—when any of them is killed, both the killer and the slain are in the Fire. It is authentically reported that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“When two Muslims confront one another with their swords, both the killer and the slain are in the Fire.” He was asked, “Messenger of Allah, we understand about the killer, but why the slain?” He replied, “He was intent on killing his brother.”

Both al-Bukhārī and Muslim recorded it in their Sahīh collections. He also said, may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

“Whoever is killed under a banner of blind allegiance, becoming angry out of partisanship and calling others to partisanship, is in the Fire.”

Muslim narrated it. He also said, may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

“Whoever invokes the rallying cries of the people of pre-Islamic ignorance, tell him to bite his father’s private part, and do not use euphemisms.”

Ubayy ibn Kaʿb heard a man say, “Rally, people of so-and-so!” He told him, “Bite your father’s penis!” The man said, “Abū al-Mundhir, you have never used foul language.” He replied, “This is what the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, commanded us to do.” Ahmad narrated it in his Musnad.

The meaning of his words, “Whoever invokes the rallying cries of pre-Islamic ignorance,” is that he calls upon people using their cries of affiliation, identifying himself with them when rallying support—for example, saying, “Rally, Qays! Rally, Yaman! Rally, Hilāl! Rally, Asad!” Anyone who is partisan toward the people of his town, his school of thought, his path, his relatives or his friends, to the exclusion of others, has a trait of pre-Islamic ignorance in him, until the believers hold fast—as Allah Most High has commanded them—to His rope, His Book and the Sunnah of His Messenger. For

---

their Book is one, their religion is one, their Prophet is one, and their Lord is one God. There is no god but He. To Him belongs all praise in this world and the Hereafter; His is the judgment, and to Him you will be returned.

May He make us and you among those with whom Allah is pleased and for whom He has prepared Gardens of Bliss. He has power over all things. He is sufficient for us, and He is the best Guardian.
