## Page 14015

He also said—may Allah sanctify his soul:

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

To all believers and Muslims whom this reaches:

Peace be upon you, and Allah’s mercy and blessings. We praise Allah, besides whom there is no god. He is worthy of all praise and has power over all things. We ask Him to bless His chosen one, the best of His creation, Muhammad, His servant and Messenger—may Allah bless him and his family and grant them abundant peace.

To proceed:

Allah has fulfilled His promise, granted victory to His servant, honored His army, and defeated the confederates alone.

“Allah turned back those who disbelieved in their rage, having gained no good. Allah spared the believers from fighting. Allah is Strong, Almighty.”

Allah Most High brings this to completion for us through His words:

“And He brought down from their fortresses those of the People of the Book who supported them, and cast terror into their hearts. Some you killed, and others you took captive.”

“And He caused you to inherit their land, their homes, their wealth, and land you had not trodden. Allah has power over all things.”

---

## Page 14016

Indeed, in this trial that has afflicted the Muslims through their confrontation with this enemy who spreads corruption and has departed from Islamic law, events have unfolded resembling those experienced by the Muslims against their enemies during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—in the military campaigns concerning which Allah revealed His Books and through which He tested His Prophet and the believers. These events provide an example, until the Day of Resurrection, for whoever hopes in Allah and the Last Day and remembers Allah often.

The texts of the Book and the Sunnah—which constitute the call of Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace—apply to all people through the general scope of both their wording and their meaning, or through the general scope of their meaning. Allah’s pledges in His Book and the Sunnah of His Messenger extend to the later generations of this nation just as they extended to its earliest generations.

Allah has related to us the accounts of earlier nations only so that they may serve as lessons for us. We therefore compare our circumstances with theirs and draw analogies between the later generations of nations and their earliest generations. Thus, what befalls a believer in later generations resembles what befell a believer in earlier generations; and what befalls a disbeliever or hypocrite in later generations resembles what befell a disbeliever or hypocrite in earlier generations.

Thus, after recounting the story of Joseph in detail and summarizing the accounts of the prophets, Allah Most High said:

“There was certainly in their stories a lesson for those of understanding. It was not a narration invented.”

That is, these accounts related in the Book are not like fabricated stories, such as the fictitious accounts of military exploits that are circulated.

And after recounting the story of Pharaoh, Allah Most High said:

“So Allah seized him in exemplary punishment for the last

---

## Page 14017

and the first.”

“Indeed, in that is a lesson for whoever fears Allah.”

Concerning the encounters of our Prophet Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, with his enemies at Badr and elsewhere, He said:

“There has already been a sign for you in the two forces that met: one fighting in the cause of Allah and the other disbelieving. They saw them with their own eyes as twice their number. Allah strengthens with His help whomever He wills. Indeed, in that is a lesson for those with insight.”

Concerning the Prophet’s siege of Banū al-Nadīr, Allah Most High said:

“He is the One who expelled those who disbelieved among the People of the Book from their homes at the first gathering. You did not think they would leave, and they thought their fortresses would protect them from Allah. But Allah came upon them from where they had not expected and cast terror into their hearts. They destroyed their houses with their own hands and the hands of the believers. So take heed, O people of insight.”

He thus commanded us to draw lessons from the circumstances of those who preceded us, both within this nation and among the nations before it.

In several places, He states that His way in this regard follows a consistent pattern and that His manner of dealing with people remains unchanged. Allah Most High said:

“If the hypocrites, those in whose hearts is disease, and those who spread alarming rumors in Medina do not desist, We will surely incite you against them. Then they will remain your neighbors there only a little while. Accursed, wherever they are found, they will be seized and killed mercilessly. Such was Allah’s established way with those who passed before, and you will find no change in Allah’s established way.”

Allah Most High also said:

“If those who disbelieve were to fight you, they would turn their backs in flight; then they would find neither protector nor helper. Such is Allah’s established way, which has prevailed before, and you will find no change in Allah’s established way.”

He, glorified be He, has also stated that the conduct of later disbelievers is like that of earlier disbelievers.

---

## Page 14018

Thus, people of understanding should draw lessons from Allah’s established way and His momentous dealings with His servants, and from the conduct and customs of nations—especially in a tremendous calamity such as this, news of which reached East and West, and whose sparks spread throughout the lands of Islam. In it, hypocrisy raised its head and disbelief bared its fangs and molars. The pillar of Scripture was almost uprooted and destroyed, the rope of faith severed and torn away, and the heartland of the believers laid waste. This religion itself nearly vanished under the domination of the wicked Tatars.

The hypocrites and those in whose hearts was disease thought that Allah and His Messenger had promised them nothing but delusion, and that the party of Allah and His Messenger would never return to their families. That notion was made appealing in their hearts; they entertained evil thoughts and were a people doomed to ruin.

A trial descended that left even the forbearing bewildered, reduced the sober man to the state of one intoxicated, and left the discerning man, beset by anxious thoughts, neither asleep nor awake. The hearts of acquaintances and brothers became estranged, until each man was too preoccupied with himself to help those in distress.

Through it, Allah distinguished those endowed with insight and certainty from those whose hearts harbored disease, or hypocrisy and weakness of faith. Through it, He raised some people to lofty ranks, brought others down to abysmal depths, and expiated the sinful deeds of still others. So many kinds of affliction arose that it became a miniature of the Great Resurrection. For people were divided during it into the wretched and the blessed, just as they will likewise be divided

---

## Page 14019

on the promised Day. In this trial, a man fled from his brother, his mother, and his father, for each had concerns enough to occupy him. Some people’s utmost concern was to save themselves, without looking back to their wealth, children, or wives. Others had the strength to rescue their families and possessions. Others could offer further assistance to those they cared about, while still others held the standing of an intercessor whose plea was heeded. They occupied differing ranks before Allah in the benefit they brought and the harm they warded off. Only faith, righteous deeds, goodness, and mindfulness of Allah brought benefit untainted by complaint.

In this trial, innermost secrets were tested, and what lay concealed within hearts came to light. It became clear that counterfeit words and deeds betray their owner when, in the end, he needs them most. Those who had obeyed their leaders and great men condemned them for leading them astray, while those sincere in their faith praised their Lord, having taken a path alongside the Messenger.

The predictions conveyed in the prophetic reports proved true. The hearts of those in this community granted inspired insight concurred with them, as did the glad tidings shown to the believers. Through this trial, the victorious group became clearly known: those who prevail in upholding the religion and whom neither their opponents nor those who abandon them will harm until the Day of Resurrection.

For the people had divided into three parties: one striving to support the religion, another abandoning it, and a third departing from the law of Islam. People were divided into those deserving reward, those who were excused, and others whom the deceiver had deluded concerning Allah. Through this ordeal, Allah distinguished people and separated them into their respective groups:

“So that Allah may reward the truthful

---

## Page 14020

for their truthfulness and punish the hypocrites if He wills, or turn to them in mercy. Indeed, Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.”

The lesson to be drawn from this momentous event is this:

Allah Most High sent Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, with guidance and the religion of truth, to make it prevail over all religion. He prescribed jihad for him, first permitting it and then making it obligatory after he emigrated to Medina and gained supporters there who aided Allah and His Messenger. During his residence in the city of emigration—a period of about ten years—he personally led twenty-some expeditions, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

The first was the expedition of Badr, and the last was the expedition of Tabūk. Allah revealed Surah al-Anfāl concerning his first expedition and Surah Barā’ah concerning his last. He placed the two together in the written Quran because of the similarity between the beginning and the end of the matter, as the Commander of the Faithful, ‘Uthmān, explained when asked why the two surahs were placed together without the basmalah—the opening invocation—separating them. Fighting took place in nine of these expeditions.

The first expedition involving combat was Badr, and the last were Hunayn and al-Tā’if. Allah sent down His angels during them, as the Quran relates. For this reason, people came to mention the two together, despite the great distance in time and place between the two battles. Badr took place in Ramadan in the second year after the Hijrah, between Medina and Mecca, to the north of Mecca. The battle of Hunayn took place in late Shawwāl of the eighth year. Hunayn is a valley near al-Tā’if, east of Mecca. Then the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, distributed

---

## Page 14021

the spoils of that battle at al-Ji‘rānah and set out from al-Ji‘rānah to perform ‘umrah. He then besieged al-Tā’if. Its people did not fight him in open battle with their ranks drawn up; rather, they fought him from behind a wall.

Thus, the last expedition involving open battle between forces drawn up in ranks was the expedition of Hunayn. Badr was the first expedition in which the Muslims prevailed over the leading warriors of the unbelievers. Allah killed their nobles and took their leaders captive, despite the Muslims’ small numbers and weakness. They numbered three hundred and a little over ten, with only two horses, while two or three men took turns riding a single camel. Their enemy numbered more than three times as many and came with strength, equipment, an imposing appearance, and arrogance.

The following year, the unbelievers attacked Medina, where the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and his Companions were residing. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and his Companions marched out to meet them, numbering about a quarter as many as the unbelievers. They left their families in Medina, then moved them elsewhere. At first, the Muslims had the upper hand, but then the advantage passed to the unbelievers. Most of the Muslim army fled, except for a few men around the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, some of whom were killed and others wounded. The unbelievers were intent on killing the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, to the point that they broke one of his lateral incisors, gashed his forehead, and smashed the helmet on his head.

Allah revealed a portion of Surah Āl ‘Imrān concerning this battle, beginning with His words:

“And remember when you left your family in the morning to assign the believers their positions for battle.”

He also said concerning it:

“Indeed, those of you who turned away on the day the two armies met—it was Satan who caused them to slip

---

## Page 14022

because of some of what they had earned. But Allah has pardoned them. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Forbearing.” He also said concerning it:

“Allah certainly fulfilled His promise to you when you were killing them by His permission, until you lost courage, disputed the command, and disobeyed after He had shown you what you loved. Among you are those who desire this world, and among you are those who desire the Hereafter. Then He turned you away from them to test you. But He has pardoned you, and Allah is gracious to the believers.”

He also said concerning it:

“When a calamity befell you, although you had inflicted twice as much, did you say, ‘How has this happened?’ Say, ‘It is from yourselves.’ Indeed, Allah has power over all things.”

Satan had cried out among the people that Muhammad had been killed. Some were shaken by this and fled, while others stood firm and fought. Allah Most High said:

“Muhammad is no more than a messenger; other messengers have passed away before him. If he dies or is killed, will you turn back on your heels? Whoever turns back on his heels will not harm Allah at all, and Allah will reward the grateful.”

This resembled the Muslims’ situation when they were defeated last year. Their defeat last year was due to manifest sins and evident transgressions: corrupt intentions, boasting, arrogance, oppression, indecencies, turning away from the judgment of the Book and the Sunnah and from observing Allah’s obligations, and aggression against many Muslims in the lands of al-Jazīrah and Rūm. Their enemy had initially been content with a truce and peaceful relations with them and was beginning to embrace Islam.

---

## Page 14023

and was only just embracing faith and peaceful relations, while they themselves had turned away from many of the requirements of faith. In His wisdom and mercy toward the believers, Allah therefore subjected them to these trials so that He might purify those who believed, that they might turn back to their Lord, and that their enemy’s aggression, scheming, breach of pledges, and departure from the laws of Islam would be exposed. Thus, grounds would arise for granting them victory and for exacting retribution upon their enemy.

There was such grave evil within many of the Muslim fighters and their subjects that, had it been accompanied by victory over their enemy—whose condition was as described—it would have brought them indescribable corruption in both their religious and worldly affairs. Just as Allah’s granting the Muslims victory at Badr was a mercy and a blessing, their defeat at Uhud was also a blessing and a mercy for the believers. For the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Allah decrees nothing for the believer except what is good for him. This is true of no one but the believer: if prosperity comes to him and he thanks Allah, it is good for him; and if adversity befalls him and he remains patient, it is good for him.”

Since the ordeal that befell the Muslims last year resembled Uhud, and since the Muslims were tried in the year of the Trench more than a year after Uhud—or, according to another account, two years later—so too, this year, the believers were tried by their enemy much as the Muslims had been tried

---

## Page 14024

alongside the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, in the year of the Trench. This was the Battle of the Confederates, concerning which Allah revealed Surah al-Ahzāb. This surah recounts that campaign, in which Allah granted victory to His servant, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, strengthened His believing army, and single-handedly defeated the confederates who had allied against him, without fighting; rather, the believers stood firm against their enemy. In it, Allah mentioned the distinctive privileges of His Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, his rights, the inviolability of his person, and that of his household, for he was the central figure whom Allah granted victory in that campaign without fighting. Exactly the same happened in this campaign of ours. The secret of the support granted to the religion became clear in it, just as it had in the Battle of the Trench. People also divided into groups just as they had in the year of the Trench.

For since Allah Most High sent Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and strengthened him through the emigration and the support he received, people have fallen into three groups:

Believers: those who believed in him both outwardly and inwardly.

Disbelievers: those who openly declared their disbelief in him.

Hypocrites: those who believed outwardly but not inwardly.

For this reason, Allah opened Surah al-Baqarah with four verses describing the believers, two verses describing the disbelievers, and thirteen verses describing the hypocrites. Faith, disbelief, and hypocrisy each have pillars and branches, as

---

## Page 14025

the evidence of the Quran and Sunnah shows, and as the Commander of the Faithful, ‘Alī ibn Abī Tālib, may Allah be pleased with him, explained in the report transmitted from him concerning faith, its pillars, and its branches.

Some hypocrisy is major, placing the person guilty of it in the lowest depths of the Fire, like the hypocrisy of ‘Abd Allah ibn Ubayy and others. This includes openly rejecting the Messenger, denying some of what he brought, hating him, not believing that following him is obligatory, rejoicing at the decline of his religion, grieving at its ascendancy, and similar attitudes that necessarily make a person an enemy of Allah and His Messenger.

This kind of hypocrisy existed in the time of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and has persisted ever since. Indeed, it has been more prevalent since his time than during his lifetime, because the grounds for faith were stronger in his time. If hypocrisy existed alongside them despite their strength, it is all the more likely to exist when they are weaker.

Just as he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, knew some hypocrites but did not know others—as Allah’s words make clear:

“Among the Bedouins around you are hypocrites, and among the people of Medina are those entrenched in hypocrisy. You do not know them; We know them.”

So too, his successors and heirs may know some hypocrites but not others. Among those who affiliate themselves with Islam, across the various groups, are many hypocrites, both among the elite and among ordinary people. They are called “zindīqs” (concealed unbelievers). Scholars have differed over whether their repentance should be accepted outwardly, because this is not

---

## Page 14026

known, since they always profess Islam outwardly.

Such people are numerous among adherents of philosophy, including astrologers and the like, then among physicians, and to a lesser extent among scribes. They are also found among Sufis, those engaged in jurisprudence, soldiers, rulers, and ordinary people. However, they are especially numerous among the sects of the innovators, particularly the Rāfidah. Among them are more concealed unbelievers and hypocrites than among any other sect.

For this reason, the Khurramiyyah, Bātiniyyah, Qarāmitah, Ismā‘īliyyah, Nusayriyyah, and similar groups of hypocrites and concealed unbelievers have affiliated themselves with the Rāfidah. In these times, many of these hypocrites are inclined toward the rule of these Tatars, because the Tatars do not oblige them to observe Islamic law, but leave them to their existing ways. Some of them are averse to the Tatars only because of their corrupt worldly conduct, their seizure of wealth, and their brazen bloodshed and taking of captives—not for the sake of religion. This is the major form of hypocrisy.

As for minor hypocrisy, it is hypocrisy in deeds and the like: lying when speaking, breaking promises, betraying trusts, or acting wickedly in disputes. In the two Sahīhs, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, is reported to have said:

“The signs of a hypocrite are three: when he speaks, he lies; when he promises, he breaks his promise; and when entrusted with something, he betrays that trust.”

An authentic version adds:

“Even if he prays, fasts, and claims to be a Muslim.”

And in the two Sahīhs,

---

## Page 14027

‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Amr reports that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Whoever possesses four traits is a complete hypocrite, and whoever possesses one of them has a trait of hypocrisy until he abandons it: when he speaks, he lies; when he promises, he breaks his promise; when he makes a covenant, he betrays it; and when he disputes, he acts wickedly.”

Turning away from jihad also falls into this category, for it is among the traits of the hypocrites. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Whoever dies without having fought or even contemplated fighting dies with a trait of hypocrisy.”

Narrated by Muslim.

Allah revealed Sūrat Barā’ah (“Disavowal”), which is called al-Fādihah (“the Exposer”) because it exposed the hypocrites. Both compilers report in their Sahīhs that Ibn ‘Abbās said:

“It is the Exposer. Revelation kept coming down with ‘Among them …’ and ‘Among them …’ until they thought that no one would be left unmentioned in it.”

Al-Miqdād ibn al-Aswad said:

“It is Sūrat al-Buhūth (‘the Surah of Searching’), because it searched out the hypocrites’ secrets.”

Qatādah said:

“It is al-Muthīrah (‘the Uncoverer’), because it uncovered the hypocrites’ shameful deeds.”

Ibn ‘Abbās said:

“It is al-Muba‘thirah (‘the Unearther’).”

Unearthing and uncovering are close in meaning.

Ibn ‘Umar said that it is al-Muqashqishah (“the Healer”), because it cures the disease of hypocrisy. The expression taqashqasha al-marīd means “the sick person recovered.” Al-Asma‘ī said: “The two surahs of sincerity used to be called al-Muqashqishatān (‘the Two Healers’), because they cure hypocrisy.”

---

## Page 14028

This surah was revealed during the Prophet’s last military campaign, the expedition to Tabūk, in 9 AH, when Islam had grown strong and prevailed. In it, Allah exposed the condition of the hypocrites, describing their cowardice and abandonment of jihad, their reluctance to spend in Allah’s cause, and their avaricious attachment to wealth.

These are two grave maladies: cowardice and miserliness. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“The worst traits in a person are avarice that fills him with anguish and cowardice that makes his heart quake.”

This is an authentic hadith. Hence, these two traits may constitute major sins that incur Hellfire, as indicated by His words:

“Let not those who greedily withhold what Allah has granted them of His bounty think that it is good for them. Rather, it is bad for them. What they withheld will be hung around their necks on the Day of Resurrection.”

Allah Most High also said:

“Whoever turns his back on them that day, unless manoeuvring for battle or joining another company, has incurred Allah’s wrath. His refuge is Hell—what an evil destination!”

As for His description of their cowardice and fear, Allah Most High said:

“They swear by Allah that they are indeed of you, but they are not of you; rather, they are a people who are afraid.”

“If they could find a refuge, caves, or a place to enter, they would turn towards it, rushing headlong.”

Thus, He, glorified be He, states that although they swear they are among the believers, they are not among them; rather, they are terrified of the enemy. So, “if they could find a refuge”—some stronghold or fortress in which to seek shelter, of the kind to which those who abandon jihad flee—or “caves”—maghārāt, the plural of maghārah (“cave”). Caves are so called because whoever enters them sinks out of sight, becoming hidden, just as water sinks into the ground. Or “a place to enter”

---

## Page 14029

—a place that can be entered only with effort, whether because its entrance is narrow or for some other reason. In other words, somewhere they could enter, even with difficulty and hardship. “They would turn”—away from jihad—“towards it, rushing headlong.” That is, they would rush so swiftly that nothing could hold them back, like a runaway horse whose bridle cannot restrain it once it bolts. This description applies to many people in the events we are experiencing, as well as in events before and after them.

Likewise, He said in Surah Muhammad—may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

“But when a decisive surah is revealed and fighting is mentioned in it, you see those in whose hearts is a disease looking at you like someone overcome by the throes of death. So woe to them!”

That is, may they be cast far away!

“Obedience and proper speech would be better. Then, when the matter is decided, if they were true to Allah, it would be better for them.”

Allah Most High also said:

“The believers are only those who believe in Allah and His Messenger, then never doubt, and strive with their wealth and their lives in Allah’s cause. It is they who are truthful.”

Thus, He identifies believers exclusively as those who believe and strive in jihad.

Allah Most High said:

“Those who believe in Allah and the Last Day do not ask your permission to be excused from striving with their wealth and their lives. And Allah knows those who fear Him.”

“Only those who do not believe in Allah and the Last Day ask your permission. Their hearts are filled with doubt, and in their doubt they waver.”

Here Allah declares that a believer does not ask the Messenger’s permission to refrain from jihad; only someone who does not believe asks his permission. What, then, of someone who refrains without even asking permission? Whoever reflects upon the Quran will find many similar passages that reinforce this meaning.

## Page 14030

And, describing their stinginess, He said:

“Nothing prevents their contributions from being accepted except that they disbelieve in Allah and His Messenger, come to prayer only sluggishly, and spend only reluctantly.”

Such is the condition of someone who spends reluctantly; what, then, of someone who does not spend at all? He also said:

“Among them are those who criticize you concerning the distribution of charity. If they are given some of it, they are pleased; but if they are given none, they become resentful.”

And He said:

“Among them are those who pledged to Allah, ‘If He gives us of His bounty, we will surely give charity and be among the righteous.’ But when He gave them of His bounty, they were stingy with it and turned away in aversion.”

He also said in the surah:

“O you who believe, many rabbis and monks wrongfully consume people’s wealth and bar others from Allah’s path. Those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend it in Allah’s cause—give them tidings of a painful punishment.”

“On the Day when it is heated in the Fire of Hell and their foreheads, sides, and backs are branded with it: ‘This is what you hoarded for yourselves, so taste what you used to hoard!’”

Thus, this verse encompasses everyone who takes wealth without any right to it or withholds it from those entitled to it. The rabbis are the scholars, and the monks are the devout worshippers. Allah states that many of them wrongfully consume people’s wealth and turn away—that is, they turn away themselves and prevent others from following the truth. One says, *sadda ‘an al-haqq sudūdan* (he turned away from the truth), and *sadda ghayrahu saddan* (he prevented someone else).

This includes wealth wrongfully consumed from an endowment or a gift granted on the basis of

---

## Page 14031

religious service, such as prayer, or vows made for the benefit of religious people, as well as communal funds, such as those of the public treasury and the like. This concerns those who wrongfully consume wealth on ostensibly religious grounds.

Then He said:

“Those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend it in Allah’s cause.”

This includes anyone who hoards wealth instead of meeting obligatory expenditure in Allah’s cause—whether a king, a commander, a wealthy person, or anyone else. Jihad is the activity most deserving of the designation “Allah’s cause.” If this includes hoarded wealth acquired through inheritance or earnings, then it applies even more strongly to hoarded communal wealth, to which the entire community is entitled and which should serve its welfare.

Section

Now that some of the meaning of “believer” and “hypocrite” has become clear, if a person reads Surah al-Ahzāb and learns from the accounts transmitted in hadith, Quranic commentary, jurisprudence, and narratives of the Prophet’s military campaigns what the event concerning which the Quran was revealed was like, then compares the present event with that one, he will find confirmation of what we have said: people divided into the same three categories in this event as they did in that one. Many matters that seemed ambiguous will also become clear to him.

Thus, patience and certainty—the two foundations of trust in Allah—bring about leadership in religion, as indicated by His words, Exalted is He:

Jihad also embodies true detachment from the life of this world and from this worldly abode. It also embodies true sincerity, for the discussion here concerns those who strive in Allah’s cause, not for leadership, wealth, or partisan zeal. The account, in brief, is as follows: most of the polytheists surrounding the Muslims formed a coalition against them and brought their forces to Medina to eradicate the believers. Quraysh gathered with their allies from Banū Asad, Ashjaʿ, Fazārah, and other tribes of Najd.

The Jews of Qurayzah and al-Nadīr also joined together. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had previously expelled Banū al-Nadīr, as Allah, Exalted is He, mentioned in Surah al-Hashr. They came with the confederates to Qurayzah, who had a treaty with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and lived nearby, close to

---

## Page 14035

Medina—and they kept pressing them until Qurayzah broke the treaty and joined the confederates. These mighty confederate forces assembled, outnumbering the Muslims several times over. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, placed the women and children in Medina’s fortified towers, which resemble castles, and did not move them elsewhere. He positioned the Muslims with their backs to Salʿ—the mountain near Medina to the west and north—and placed a trench between himself and the enemy. The enemy had surrounded them from the upper and lower approaches. Such was their bitter hostility that, had they gained power over the believers, they would have inflicted the most devastating harm upon them.

In the present incident, this enemy formed a coalition of Mongols, other Turkic peoples, Persians, Arabized peoples, and others from the various groups of apostates, as well as Armenian and other Christians. This enemy encamped beside the Muslims’ lands, wavering between advancing and holding back, despite the small number of Muslims confronting them. Their aim was to seize the land and annihilate its inhabitants, just as those earlier forces had encamped around Medina facing the Muslims.

The siege of the Muslims in the year of the Trench lasted, according to one account, twenty-odd nights; according to another, twenty nights. This enemy crossed the Euphrates on the seventeenth of Rabīʿ al-Ākhir, and the beginning of

---

## Page 14036

their withdrawal from Aleppo—when their senior commander Ghāzān returned with his men—was on Monday, the eleventh or twelfth of Jumādā al-Ūlā, the day the army—the Muslim army—entered well-guarded Egypt. The supplicant met with them and addressed them concerning this matter.

When Allah, glorified and exalted is He, instilled such concern and determination in the believers’ hearts, He instilled terror and the desire to withdraw in their enemies’ hearts.

In the year of the Trench, there was intense cold and a fierce, dreadful wind through which Allah drove the confederates away from Medina, as He, exalted is He, said:

“So We sent against them a wind and armies you did not see.”

Likewise, this year Allah sent unusually abundant snow, rain, and cold, until most people came to resent it. We would tell them: “Do not resent it, for Allah has wisdom and mercy in it.” This was among the greatest means by which Allah drove the enemy away. Snow, rain, and cold descended upon them so heavily that as many of their horses perished as Allah willed, and as many of their men also perished as Allah willed. Cold and hunger brought such weakness and incapacity upon them and their remaining horses that they realized they could no longer fight.

I even received word that one of the senior commanders in Syria had said: “May Allah not brighten our faces! Is our enemy up to their hair in snow while we sit idle and do not seize them?” They even realized that they were prey for the Muslims, if only the Muslims would hunt them down. Yet there was great wisdom in Allah’s postponement of their capture.

## Page 14037

And Allah said concerning the confederates:

“There the believers were tested and shaken severely.”

So it was this year. The enemy came from the two directions of Upper Syria—north of the Euphrates and south of it. Eyes grew terribly wild and hearts reached the throats because of the severity of the ordeal, especially when news spread that the army had withdrawn to Egypt and that the enemy was drawing near and advancing toward Damascus. People harbored all manner of thoughts about Allah.

One thought that none of Syria’s soldiers would stand against them, and that they would annihilate the people of Syria. Another thought that even if the soldiers stood their ground, the enemy would crush them and surround them as a halo encircles the moon. Another thought that Syria was no longer fit to inhabit and would no longer remain under Muslim rule. Another thought that they would seize it, then advance upon Egypt and conquer it, with no one able to stand against them; he therefore contemplated fleeing to Yemen or somewhere similar.

Another, at his most optimistic, said: “They will occupy it this year, just as they occupied it in Hūlākū’s time, in the year fifty-seven. Then perhaps the army will march out of Egypt and rescue it from them, just as it marched out that year.” Such was the thinking of the best of them.

Another thought that what he had been told by those versed in prophetic reports and those who received inspirations and glad tidings was nothing but false hopes and idle fables. Another was so overcome by terror and alarm that thoughts passed through his heart like passing clouds; he has no mind

---

with which to understand, nor a tongue with which to speak. He might then fail to discern their subtler implications or to resolve what, at first consideration, he imagined contradicted them. ## Page 14039

As for those in whose hearts is disease, they are mentioned repeatedly in this surah. They are mentioned here, and in His words:

“If the hypocrites, those in whose hearts is disease, and those who spread rumours in Medina do not desist…”

And in His words:

“Lest one in whose heart is disease should be moved to desire.”

Allah mentions disease of the heart in several places. He Most High says:

“When the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is disease said, ‘Their religion has deluded these people.’”

Disease in the heart is like disease in the body. Just as bodily disease is a departure from health and balance without death, so too the heart may suffer a disease that takes it away from health and balance without causing it to die, whether it impairs the heart’s perception and understanding or its actions and impulses. As they have explained, this stems from weakness of faith: either weakness in the heart’s knowledge and conviction, or weakness in its actions and impulses. This includes those whose belief is weak and those overcome by cowardice and fear. The heart’s ailments—unlawful desire, envy, cowardice, miserliness, and the like—are all diseases, as are the ignorance, doubts, and misconceptions within it.

Accordingly, the statement:

“Lest one in whose heart is disease should be moved to desire”

refers to the desire for sexual immorality and the lust for illicit intercourse, as they have explained it. Another example is the saying of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

“What disease is worse than miserliness?”

Thus this verse—namely, His words, Most High, “When the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is disease said”—shows that disease and hypocrisy in the heart cause doubt concerning truthful reports that should reassure a person and dispel his fear, until they imagine that those reports were merely a deception, exactly as happened in this incident of ours.

The basic meaning of ʿawrah is an unprotected place that needs guarding and covering. One says, “Your meeting place has become exposed,” when its screen is gone or its wall has fallen. From this comes the expression “the enemy’s vulnerable point.”

for Allah protects them.

Their aim was to flee from jihad, using their families as a pretext. The same happened to many people during this campaign. They began fleeing from the frontier to strongholds and fortresses, and to distant places such as Egypt. They would say: “Our only aim is to protect our families, and we cannot send them away with anyone else.” They were lying about this. He thus states that if Medina had been invaded from its outskirts and they had then been asked to yield to temptation—meaning being led away from religion through disbelief or hypocrisy—they would have yielded and embraced it without hesitation. Such is the condition of some people: if this hypocritical, criminal enemy invaded their land and then asked them to join him in departing from the law of Islam—which is a tremendous trial—they would join him in doing so. Indeed, last year some people helped them through various forms of wrongdoing in religious and worldly affairs, ranging from neglecting obligations to committing forbidden acts, whether concerning the rights of Allah or the rights of His servants, such as abandoning prayer and drinking

---

## Page 14044

intoxicating drinks, reviling the righteous predecessors and the Muslim troops, spying on the Muslims for them, directing them to the Muslims’ wealth and womenfolk, seizing people’s property and torturing them, strengthening their accursed state, and filling the Muslims’ hearts with fear of them, along with other forms of turmoil.

Then Allah Most High says:

Such is the condition of people who made pledges and then broke them, both in the past and recently during this campaign. Both last year and this year, there were people from various groups who initially pledged to fight and not flee, but then fled in defeat when the situation became grave.

Then Allah Most High says:

“Say: ‘Fleeing will never benefit you if you flee from death or killing, and then you would be allowed to enjoy life only for a little while.’”

Allah thus states that fleeing avails nothing, whether from death or from being killed. Fleeing from death is like fleeing from the plague. Hence the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“If it breaks out in a land while you are there, do not leave to flee from it.”

Fleeing from being killed is like fleeing from jihad. The particle “lan” (“will not”) negates an action in the future. The verb is indefinite, and an indefinite expression in a negative context encompasses all its instances. It therefore follows that fleeing from death or from being killed brings no benefit whatsoever. This is Allah’s truthful statement. Whoever believes that such flight will benefit him has accused Allah of lying in what He has stated.

---

## Page 14045

Experience also confirms what the Quran teaches. Those who fled this year gained nothing from their flight; rather, they suffered loss in both their religion and their worldly affairs, and calamities befell them in varying degrees. Those who remained steadfast at their posts benefited in both their religion and their worldly affairs. Even death itself, which the fugitives had fled, was more common among them and less common among those who stayed. Flight did not save those whose death Allah had willed. Not one of those who pursued the enemy and inflicted punishment upon them died or was killed. Indeed, deaths in the city declined after the fugitives departed. Such has always been Allah’s way, in the past and the present.

Then Allah Most High says:

“And then you would be allowed to enjoy life only for a little while.”

That is, even if fleeing benefited you, it would give you only a little more life before you died, for death is inevitable.

One fool is reported to have said: “Well, we want that little while!” This betrays his ignorance of the verse’s meaning. Allah did not say that fleeing would allow them a little enjoyment. Rather, He stated that it brings no benefit whatsoever. He then gave a second answer: even if it did bring benefit, it would afford only a little enjoyment. He then gave a third answer: whatever harm has been decreed for the fugitive will reach him, and whatever happiness has been decreed for the steadfast person will reach him.

He says:

“Say: ‘Who can protect you from Allah if He intends harm for you or intends mercy for you?’ They will find no protector or helper besides Allah.”

A parallel is His statement among the verses concerning jihad:

“Wherever you may be, death will overtake you, even if you are in lofty, fortified towers”—and the rest of the verse—and His words:

“O you who believe,

---

## Page 14046

do not be like those who disbelieved and said of their brothers when they travelled through the land or went out to fight, ‘Had they stayed with us, they would not have died or been killed,’ so that Allah may make this a source of regret in their hearts. Allah gives life and causes death, and Allah sees all that you do.”

The point is this: death is inevitable. How many have stood in the battle lines and survived, and how many have fled death only to meet it! As Khālid ibn al-Walīd said when he was dying:

“I have stood in so many battle lines, and my body bears more than eighty wounds from sword blows, spear thrusts, and arrows. Yet here I am, dying in my bed as a camel dies. May the eyes of cowards never sleep!”

The scholars said:

Some of the hypocrites would return from the trench and enter Medina. Whenever someone came to them, they would say, “Woe to you! Stay here; do not go out.” They would also write to their brothers in the army: “Come to us in Medina; we are waiting for you,” discouraging them from fighting. They would only go to the army when they had no alternative, and then only so that people would see their faces. Once no one was watching them, they would return to Medina.

One man left the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and found his full brother with roast meat and nabīdh (an infused drink) before him. He said, “You are here while the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, is amid spears and swords?”

His brother replied, “Come here to me, for you and your companion have been surrounded.”

---

## Page 14047

Thus He described those who discourage others from jihad as belonging to two groups: those who are in the fighters’ town and those who are elsewhere. If they are there, they hinder them from jihad through words, deeds, or both. If they are elsewhere, they send messages or letters urging the fighters to leave their town and join them in fortresses or far away. This is what happened in this campaign: some people in the army, Medina, and elsewhere began hindering those who wished to fight, while others were sent from strongholds, fortresses, and elsewhere to their brothers with the message, “Come to us.” Allah Most High said of them:

“They seldom join the fighting, being miserly toward you.”

That is, they are unwilling to fight alongside you or spend in Allah’s cause. Mujāhid said: “They begrudge you good fortune, victory, and spoils.”

Such is the condition of those who withhold their own service and wealth from the believers, or begrudge them Allah’s bounty—the victory and provision He brings about through the actions of others. Some people are stingy with their own kindness, while others begrudge Allah’s kindness and bounty. These are the envious.

Then Allah Most High said:

“But when fear comes, you see them looking at you, their eyes rolling like someone fainting in the throes of death.”

So intense is the terror in their hearts that they resemble someone losing consciousness at the moment of death: he is afraid, his mind is bewildered, and his eyes stare fixedly without blinking. These people are just the same, because they fear being killed.

“But when fear has passed, they lash you with sharp tongues.”

In Arabic usage, one also says:

---

## Page 14048

“Salaqūkum” (“they assailed you”), meaning to raise one’s voice with hurtful words. From this comes sāliqa: a woman who raises her voice in lamentation over a calamity. One says salaqahu, with either sād or sīn, when someone addresses another harshly and forcefully. Some of the early generations recited it with sād, although this does not conform to the written text of the Quran.

An orator is described as mislāq when he is eloquent in his address. Here, however, this forcefulness is directed toward evil, not good, as Allah says:

“With sharp tongues, greedy for good things.”

This lashing out with sharp tongues takes various forms. Sometimes the hypocrites say to the believers: “What has befallen us is due to the ill fortune you bring! You are the ones who called people to this religion, fought for it, and opposed them.” Such were the words the hypocrites addressed to the believers among the Companions.

At other times they say: “You are the ones who advised us to remain here and hold firm at this frontier post until now. Had we left earlier instead, this would not have befallen us.”

Sometimes they say: “Despite your small numbers and weakness, you want to defeat the enemy! Your religion has deluded you.” As Allah Most High says:

“When the hypocrites and those with sickness in their hearts said, ‘These people have been deluded by their religion.’ But whoever puts his trust in Allah—surely Allah is Almighty, All-Wise.”

At other times they say: “You are madmen, devoid of reason! You want to destroy

---

## Page 14049

yourselves and everyone with you!”

At other times, they utter all manner of harsh, hurtful words. Yet they are also “greedy for good things”—that is, eager to obtain the spoils and wealth that have come into your possession.

Qatāda said:
“When the time comes to divide the spoils, they unleash their tongues against you, saying: ‘Give us our share! You have no greater right to it than we do.’ In battle, however, they are the most cowardly of people and the readiest to abandon the truth; but when it comes to spoils, they are the greediest.”

It has also been said that “greedy for good things” means that they are miserly with them, contributing neither their persons nor their wealth.

The root of avarice is an intense greed that gives rise to miserliness and injustice: withholding what is due and taking what one has no right to. As the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Beware of avarice, for avarice destroyed those who came before you. It commanded them to be miserly, and they were miserly; it commanded them to commit injustice, and they committed injustice; and it commanded them to sever ties, and they severed them.”

Thus, these people are miserly toward their brothers, yet greedy for good things—that is, eager to possess them—and so they do not spend them. As Allah says:

“And he is indeed intense in his love of wealth.”

Then Allah Most High says:

“They think the confederate forces have not withdrawn. If the confederate forces should come again, they would wish they were out in the desert among the Bedouins, asking for news of you. Even if they were among you, they would fight but little.”

He thus describes them as having three characteristics.

---

## Page 14050

The first characteristic is that their intense fear makes them think the confederate forces have not withdrawn from the city. Such is the condition of a coward whose heart is diseased: his heart readily believes frightening reports and rejects reassuring ones.

The second characteristic is that, if the confederate forces return, they wish they were not among you, but out in the desert among the Bedouins, asking for news of you: “What news is there from Medina? What has happened to the people?”

The third characteristic is that, if the confederate forces come while they are among you, they fight but little. These three characteristics apply to many people in this campaign, as they recognize in themselves and as those acquainted with them recognize in them.

Then Allah Most High says:

“Indeed, in the Messenger of Allah you have an excellent example for whoever hopes in Allah and the Last Day and remembers Allah often.”

Thus, He, glorified be He, tells us that those who are tried by the enemy, as the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was tried, have in him an excellent example, since they have suffered the like of what he suffered. Let them therefore follow his example in reliance upon Allah and patience. They should not suppose that these trials are punishments and a humiliation for those who suffer them. Were that so, the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace—the best of all creation—would not have been subjected to them. Rather, through them lofty ranks are attained, and through them Allah expiates the sins of those who hope in Allah and the Last Day and remember Allah often. Yet someone who is not of this description may also be subjected to such trials

---

## Page 14051

in which case they are a punishment for him, as with the disbelievers and hypocrites.

Then Allah Most High says:

“When the believers saw the confederate forces, they said, ‘This is what Allah and His Messenger promised us, and Allah and His Messenger spoke the truth.’ And it only increased them in faith and submission.”

The scholars said that Allah had already revealed in Sūrat al-Baqarah:

“Or do you think that you will enter Paradise without undergoing the like of what befell those who passed away before you? They were afflicted by poverty and hardship and were so shaken that the Messenger and those who believed with him said, ‘When will Allah’s help come?’ Indeed, Allah’s help is near.”

Thus Allah, glorified be He, made clear—rebuking anyone who supposed otherwise—that they would not enter Paradise until they had been tried like the nations before them: with “poverty,” meaning need and destitution; “hardship,” meaning pain and illness; and “being shaken,” meaning being shaken by the enemy. When the confederate forces came in the year of the Trench and the believers saw them, they said:

“This is what Allah and His Messenger promised us, and Allah and His Messenger spoke the truth.”

They knew that Allah had tried them by shaking them, and that the like of what had befallen those before them had now befallen them. This only increased them in faith and submission to Allah’s judgment and command. Such is the condition of some people in this campaign: they said these very words.

Likewise, His words:

“Among the believers are men who have been true to the covenant they made with Allah. Among them are those who have fulfilled their vow.”

That is, the covenant a man made with Allah: he fought until he was killed, or else survived. Nahb means a vow or covenant. It derives from nahīb (wailing), which is

---

## Page 14052

sound. From the same root comes intihāb (wailing in grief). The vow is the utterance spoken when making the covenant. Since their covenant was their vow to remain true in battle—and someone who remains true in battle may be killed—the words “fulfilled his vow” came to be understood as meaning that he had been martyred. This is especially so when the vow is to remain true in all circumstances, for he can only fulfil it completely through death. Fulfilling the vow means honouring the covenant, as Allah Most High says:

“Among the believers are men who have been true to the covenant they made with Allah. Among them are those who have fulfilled their vow.”

That is, they have fulfilled it completely. For someone whose covenant was unrestricted, this comes about through death or being killed.

“And among them are those who are still waiting.”

That is, waiting to fulfil it: having fulfilled part of it, they await the completion of the covenant. The basic meaning of fulfilment is bringing something to completion.

“So that Allah may reward the truthful for their truthfulness and punish the hypocrites if He wills, or turn to them in forgiveness. Indeed, Allah is Ever-Forgiving, Most Merciful.”

Allah, glorified be He, explains that He brought the confederate forces so that He might reward the truthful for their truthfulness, since they proved true in their faith. As Allah Most High says:

“The believers are only those who believe in Allah and His Messenger, then never doubt, and strive with their wealth and their lives in the cause of Allah. It is they who are the truthful.”

He thus confined faith to those believers who strive in His cause and declared that they are the ones who are truthful in saying, “We believe”—not those who said, as the Bedouins did, “We believe,” when faith had not entered their hearts; rather, they had yielded and submitted.

As for the hypocrites, they face one of two outcomes: either He will punish them, or He will turn to them in forgiveness. Such was the condition of the people at the Trench and in this campaign.

---

## Page 14053

Moreover, Allah Most High has tested people with this trial so that He may reward the truthful for their truthfulness—those who remain steadfast and patient in supporting Allah and His Messenger—and punish the hypocrites if He wills, or turn to them in forgiveness. We hope that Allah will turn in forgiveness to many of these blameworthy people, for some of them have felt remorse. Allah, glorified be He, accepts repentance from His servants and pardons their misdeeds. Allah has opened a gate for repentance in the west, forty years’ journey wide, which He will not close until the sun rises from the west.

The historians of the Prophet’s campaigns—including Ibn Ishāq—have related that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said at the Trench:

“Now we shall attack them, and they will not attack us.”

After that, neither Quraysh, Ghatafān nor the Jews attacked the Muslims. Rather, the Muslims attacked them, conquering Khaybar and then Mecca. The same will apply, if Allah wills, to these confederate forces of Mongols, various Turkic peoples, Persians, Arabized peoples, Christians and others who stand outside the law of Islam: now we shall attack them, and they will not attack us. Allah will turn in forgiveness to whomever He wills among the Muslims whose hearts have been touched by disease or hypocrisy, enabling them to return to their Lord, think more favourably of Islam, and strengthen their resolve to strive against their enemy.

Allah has indeed shown them signs containing a lesson for those with insight, as He says:

“Allah drove back those who disbelieved in their rage, having gained no good. Allah spared the believers from fighting. And Allah is All-Powerful, Almighty.”

---

## Page 14054

For Allah drove back the confederate forces in the year of the Trench by sending against them the east wind—a fierce, cold wind—and by sowing discord in their hearts until He scattered their ranks, leaving them with no good gained. Their aim had been to conquer Medina and seize control of it, capturing the Messenger and his Companions, just as this enemy’s aim was to conquer Syria and overpower its Muslim inhabitants. But Allah drove them back in their rage, afflicting them with heavy snow, bitter cold, a raging wind and agonizing hunger to an extent known to Him.

Some people disliked the heavy snow and rain that fell this year, even asking for the skies to clear on more than one occasion. We would tell them:

“There is great good in this. Allah has wisdom and a hidden purpose in it, so do not dislike it.”

Among His wise purposes was that, reportedly, this weather struck Ghāzān and his troops, bringing destruction upon them; it was also reportedly the reason for their departure. The Muslims, too, were tested by it, so that those who patiently uphold Allah’s command and decree might be distinguished from those who flee from obedience to Him and from striving against His enemy.

Ghāzān and those accompanying him began their withdrawal from Syria and the lands around Aleppo on Monday, the eleventh of Jumādā al-Ūlā—the day I entered Egypt, following the army, and met with the Sultan and the Muslim commanders. Allah instilled in their hearts a profound concern for striving in His cause. Once Allah had made the Muslims’ hearts steadfast, He drove the enemy away as a reward from Him, demonstrating that Allah grants victory through sincere intentions and true resolve, even when no action has yet taken place and the lands are far apart.

---

## Page 14055

It was also reported that Allah sowed discord in the hearts of these Mongols and Georgians, setting mutual hatred and hostility between them, just as He, glorified be He, had done between Quraysh and Ghatafān and the Jews in the year of the Confederates, as the historians of the Prophet’s campaigns relate. There is not enough space here to recount the events of the Trench. Anyone who studies that account will recognize the truth of this comparison, as recorded by such historians as ‘Urwa ibn al-Zubayr, al-Zuhrī, Mūsā ibn ‘Uqba, Sa‘īd ibn Yahyā al-Umawī, Muhammad ibn ‘Ā’idh, Muhammad ibn Ishāq, al-Wāqidī and others.

Some remnants of their forces remained in Syria. Most of the Damascus army marched against them, joined by the armies of Hama, Aleppo and the surrounding regions. The Muslims stood firm facing them. Although they greatly outnumbered the Muslims, they were severely weakened. They drew near Hama, but Allah Most High humbled them, and they never dared attack the Muslims. Some Muslims wished to advance against them, but the others would not agree. Small skirmishes ensued, much as they had during the campaign of the Trench, when ‘Alī ibn Abī Tālib, may Allah be pleased with him, killed ‘Amr ibn ‘Abd Wudd al-‘Āmirī after he and a small band of polytheists had forced their way across the trench.

Likewise, some enemy forces would draw near, only to be defeated by the Muslims, even though the approaching enemy numbered many times the Muslim force that had marched against them. On every occasion, the Muslims had the upper hand. The Muslims rode in pursuit of them on the last of

---

## Page 14056

the engagements, but did not catch up with them until they were crossing the Euphrates. Some of them were on an island in the river. When they saw the Muslim vanguard, they fled before them. The two forces clashed, and the Muslims struck some of them. It was said that some of them drowned.

Their crossing and the clearing of Syria of their presence took place in early Rajab. Between Ghāzān’s initial crossing and this crossing, there had been upheavals and minor engagements. More than once, we resolved to go to Hama for the fighting, upon learning that the Muslims intended to attack those who remained. The commander stationed at Hama, the troops with him, and those who had come to him from Damascus stood firm against them. They resolved to meet them in battle and earned a tremendous reward. It was said that the enemy numbered several kamānāt—three or four.

It was thus decreed that, when matters became decisive and the believers were true to Allah, He would cast terror into their enemies’ hearts, causing them to flee. Nevertheless, they attacked small northern towns, such as “Tīzīn,” “al-Fū‘a,” “Ma‘arrat Misrīn,” and others that they had not overrun the previous year.

It was said that many inhabitants of those places were sympathetic to them because of their Rāfidī beliefs, and that some possessed decrees issued by them. But these men are oppressors, and whoever helps an oppressor will suffer at his hands. Allah Most High says:

“Thus We make some wrongdoers allies of others because of what they used to earn.”

Those who disbelieved among the People of the Book also supported them against the Muslims, including

---

## Page 14057

the people of “Sīs” and the Franks. We therefore hope that Allah will bring them down from their strongholds—the meaning of sayāsī, a word also used for horns—and cast terror into their hearts. Allah has already granted the conquest of those lands. We shall campaign against them, if Allah Most High wills, and conquer Iraq and other lands, so that Allah’s word may reign supreme and His religion prevail.

This episode involved momentous events that defied all ordinary reckoning and departed from the customary course of events. Every discerning person could see Allah’s support for this religion, His care for this community, and His protection of the land He blessed for all peoples. Islam had nearly suffered a breach; the enemy had launched an assault without turning away from … (1) Those offering support were left helpless and did not turn back to … Those on the march were bewildered, not knowing who … or where to … All outward means had failed. The overpowering confederate forces rushed forward, the supporting force withdrew, and hearts once united in mutual support faltered.

Yet the supporting force stood firm, pure hearts became certain of victory, and the victorious band, granted divine aid, implored Allah to fulfil His promise. Allah opened the gates of His heavens to His overwhelming hosts and displayed His dazzling signs in support of the truth. He set upright the pillar of the Book after it had begun to lean, and through His power and might the banner of religion stood firm. He utterly humbled the people of disbelief and hypocrisy and made this a sign for the believers until the Day of Meeting.

May Allah perfect this blessing by uniting the hearts of the faithful in striving against the people of tyranny, and make this immense favour the beginning of every noble gift and a foundation
