## Page 14058

for establishing the upright prophetic call, and may He heal the believers’ hearts through the defeat of their enemies and grant them power over those near and far. All praise belongs to Allah, Lord of all worlds. May Allah bless our master Muhammad, his family and his Companions, and grant them peace.

The shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, said: “I wrote the beginning of this letter after the departure of Qāzān and his troops, upon my return from Egypt in Jumādā al-Ākhirah. They had spread word that not one of them remained. Then, when that band remained behind, we devoted our efforts to striving against them, intending to go to our brothers in Hama and urging the commanders to take action, until news reached us that those remaining had withdrawn. So I wrote it in Rajab. Allah knows best. All praise belongs to Allah alone. May Allah bless the noblest of creation, Muhammad, his family and his Companions, and grant them abundant peace until the Day of Judgment.”

---

## Page 14059

Shaykh al-Islām Taqī al-Dīn was asked:

Concerning those who claim to believe in Allah, Mighty and Majestic, His angels, His Books, His messengers and the Last Day, yet believe that the rightful imam after the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was ‘Alī ibn Abī Tālib; that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, explicitly designated him as imam; and that the Companions wronged him, denied him his right and thereby became disbelievers: is it obligatory to fight them? Does this belief make them disbelievers or not?

He replied:

All praise belongs to Allah, Lord of all worlds. Muslim scholars unanimously agree that any group that resists compliance with any of Islam’s manifest ordinances established through mass transmission must be fought until all worship is devoted to Allah alone.

Thus, if they were to say: “We pray but do not pay zakat”; or, “We perform the five daily prayers but do not perform the Friday prayer or pray in congregation”; or, “We uphold the five pillars of Islam but do not regard Muslims’ blood and property as inviolable”; or, “We will not give up usury, intoxicants or gambling”; or, “We follow the Quran but do not follow the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, or act upon the hadiths reliably established from him”; or, “We believe that Jews and Christians are better than the general body of Muslims, and that those who face the qiblah have disbelieved in Allah and His Messenger, with only a small group of believers remaining among them”

---

## Page 14060

or say: “We will not fight the disbelievers alongside the Muslims,” or profess anything else contrary to the law and Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and the way of the Muslim community—then it is obligatory to fight all these groups, just as the Muslims fought those who withheld zakat, the Khārijites and their various branches, the Khurramiyyah, the Qarmatians, the Bātiniyyah, and other adherents of deviant doctrines and religious innovations who depart from the law of Islam.

This is because Allah Most High says in His Book:

“Fight them until there is no more fitnah and all worship is devoted to Allah alone.”

Thus, if some worship is devoted to Allah and some to others, they must be fought until all worship is devoted to Allah alone.

Allah Most High also says:

“But if they repent, establish prayer and pay zakat, then let them go their way.”

He therefore commanded that they be allowed to go their way only after repenting of every form of disbelief, establishing prayer and paying zakat.

Allah Most High also says:

“O you who believe, fear Allah and give up what remains due to you of usury, if you are believers.”

“If you do not, then be warned of war from Allah and His Messenger.”

Allah Most High has thus declared that if a group resisting compliance does not desist from usury, it has waged war against Allah and His Messenger. Usury was the last thing Allah prohibited in the Quran; whatever He prohibited before it is therefore all the more emphatically prohibited.

Allah Most High also says:

“The recompense of those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger and strive to spread corruption in the land is only that they be killed or crucified, or have their hands and feet cut off on opposite sides, or be banished from the land.”

---

## Page 14061

Thus, anyone possessing the power to resist who refuses to submit in obedience to Allah and His Messenger has waged war against Allah and His Messenger. Whoever acts in the land contrary to Allah’s Book and His Messenger’s Sunnah has spread corruption in the land. For this reason, the early generations understood this verse to apply both to disbelievers and to those who pray toward the qiblah. Indeed, most leading scholars included within its scope highway robbers who brandish weapons merely to seize wealth. By taking people’s wealth through armed force, they regarded such robbers as waging war against Allah and His Messenger and spreading corruption in the land—even though the robbers believe their actions to be forbidden and profess faith in Allah and His Messenger. Someone who believes it lawful to shed Muslims’ blood, seize their wealth and fight them is therefore all the more rightly regarded as waging war against Allah and His Messenger and spreading corruption in the land.

Likewise, a belligerent disbeliever who considers Muslims’ blood and wealth lawful and believes it permissible to fight them is more deserving of being fought than an evildoer who believes such acts to be forbidden.

Similarly, an adherent of religious innovation who departs from part of the law and Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and considers it lawful to shed the blood and seize the wealth of Muslims who adhere to the Messenger’s Sunnah and law, is more deserving of being fought than an evildoer—even if he makes this a religious practice through which he seeks nearness to Allah. Likewise, Jews and Christians make waging war against Muslims a religious practice through which they seek nearness to Allah.

For this reason, the leading scholars of Islam agreed that these grave religious innovations are worse than sins whose perpetrators acknowledge them to be sins. Such, too, was the established practice of the Messenger of Allah

---

## Page 14062

may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who commanded that the Khawārij who depart from the Sunnah be fought, while commanding patience with the injustice and oppression of rulers and praying behind them despite their sins. He testified that one of his Companions who persisted in certain sins loved Allah and His Messenger, and forbade cursing him. Yet he said of Dhū al-Khuwaysirah and his followers—despite their worship and scrupulousness—that they would pass out of Islam as an arrow passes through its quarry.

Allah Most High says in His Book:

“But no, by your Lord, they will not believe until they make you judge in their disputes, then find within themselves no resistance to your judgment and submit completely.”

Thus, concerning everyone who departs from the Sunnah and law of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, Allah has sworn by His own holy Self that they do not believe until they accept the judgment of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, in all their religious and worldly disputes, and until no resistance to his judgment remains in their hearts. The Quran contains abundant evidence for this principle. This, too, is what the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and the practice of his rightly guided caliphs teach.

In the two Sahih collections, Abū Hurayrah reported:

“When the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, died, and those Arabs who apostatized had done so, ʿUmar ibn al-Khattāb said to Abū Bakr, ‘How can you fight the people when the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, “I have been commanded to fight the people until they testify that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. When they do so, they render inviolable to me their lives

---

## Page 14063

and their property, except by due right, and their reckoning rests with Allah”?’

Abū Bakr replied: ‘Did he not say, “except by due right”? Zakat is among those rights. By Allah, if they withheld from me even a young she-goat that they used to give to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, I would fight them for withholding it.’

ʿUmar said: ‘By Allah, as soon as I saw that Allah had opened Abū Bakr’s heart to fighting, I knew that it was right.’”

Thus, the Companions of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, agreed to fight people who prayed and fasted if they refused to fulfil some of what Allah had obligated them to pay as zakat on their wealth. This inference drawn by the truthful one of this community is also stated explicitly in hadith.

In the two Sahih collections, ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both, reported that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“I have been commanded to fight the people until they testify that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, establish prayer, and pay zakat. When they do so, they render inviolable to me their lives and their property, except by due right.”

He thus stated, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, that he had been commanded to fight them until they fulfilled these obligations. This accords with the Book of Allah.

Reports from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, have also been mass-transmitted through numerous chains. The compilers of the Sahih collections included ten of these chains: Muslim recorded them in his Sahih, and al-Bukhārī recorded several of them. Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, said: “The hadith concerning the Khawārij is authentically established through ten chains.”

He said, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: “Any one of you would consider his own prayer insignificant compared with theirs, and his fasting

---

## Page 14064

compared with theirs, and his recitation compared with theirs. They recite the Quran, but it does not pass beyond their throats. They pass out of Islam as an arrow passes through its quarry. If those who fight them knew what reward they have been promised through Muhammad, they would desist from further deeds.”

In another narration:
“If I live to encounter them, I will certainly kill them as ʿĀd were killed.”

In another narration:
“They are the worst of those slain beneath the sky; the best of those slain are those whom they kill.”

The first to fight them was the Commander of the Faithful, ʿAlī ibn Abī Tālib, together with the Companions of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who were with him. He fought them at Harūrā when they departed from the Sunnah and the Muslim community and deemed the blood and property of Muslims lawful. They had killed ʿAbd Allāh ibn Khabbāb and raided the Muslims’ livestock. The Commander of the Faithful, ʿAlī ibn Abī Tālib, then stood and addressed the people, mentioning the hadith and recounting how they had killed people and seized property. He therefore deemed it lawful to fight them and rejoiced greatly at their being killed. Of all the public undertakings of his caliphate, none was greater in his estimation than fighting the Khawārij.

They declared the majority of Muslims to be unbelievers, even declaring ʿUthmān and ʿAlī unbelievers. They claimed to act according to the Quran but would not follow the Sunnah of the Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, which they thought contradicted the Quran—as do the other adherents of religious innovation, despite their abundant worship and scrupulous piety.

It has been authentically reported from ʿAlī in Sahīh al-Bukhārī and elsewhere, through some eighty chains, that he said:
“The best of this community after its Prophet are Abū Bakr, then ʿUmar.”

It is also authentically reported from him

---

## Page 14065

that he burned to death the extremist Rāfidah who believed him to be divine.

It is reported from him through good chains of transmission that he said:
“If anyone is brought before me who ranks me above Abū Bakr and ʿUmar, I will flog him with the prescribed penalty for slander.”

It is also reported that, when he learned that ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sabaʾ had reviled Abū Bakr and ʿUmar, he sought him out to kill him, but he fled from him. ʿUmar ibn al-Khattāb, may Allah be pleased with him, ordered that a man who ranked him above Abū Bakr be flogged for doing so. When ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, suspected Sabīgh ibn ʿIsl of belonging to the Khawārij, he said to him:
“Had I found your head shaved, I would have struck off your head.”

Such was the practice of the Commander of the Faithful, ʿAlī. Others, too, ordered that the three categories of Shia be punished. The least extreme of them are those who rank ʿAlī above Abū Bakr and ʿUmar; both he and ʿUmar ordered that they be flogged.

The Muslims agree that the extremists are to be put to death. These are those who ascribe divinity and prophethood to ʿAlī and others, such as the Nusayriyyah and the Ismāʿīliyyah, who are called the House of Sād and the House of Sīn. They also include those deniers who have joined their ranks and deny the existence of the Creator, deny the Resurrection, or deny the outward prescriptions of the Sharia, such as the five daily prayers, fasting the month of Ramadan, and pilgrimage to the Sacred House. They interpret these as knowing their secrets, concealing their secrets, and visiting their shaykhs. They hold that wine is lawful for them and that they may marry women within the prohibited degrees.

All these unbelievers are greater in unbelief than the Jews and Christians. If any one of them does not openly manifest

---

## Page 14066

this, he is among the hypocrites who will be in the lowest depths of the Fire. Whoever openly manifests this is more extreme in unbelief than other unbelievers. He may not be allowed to remain among the Muslims, whether through payment of the jizyah (poll tax) or under a covenant of protection. Their women may not lawfully be married, nor may the animals they slaughter be eaten, for they are among the worst apostates. If they constitute a group offering resistance, they must be fought as apostates are fought, just as Abū Bakr al-Siddīq and the Companions fought the followers of Musaylimah the Liar. If they live in Muslim villages, they are to be dispersed and settled among the Muslims after repentance, and required to observe the prescriptions of Islam binding upon Muslims.

This is not limited to the extremist Rāfidah. Rather, it extends to anyone who goes to extremes concerning a shaykh and claims that the shaykh provides him with sustenance, exempts him from prayer, or is superior to the Prophet; or that he has no need of the law of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and has a path to Allah other than the Prophet’s law; or that a shaykh may stand in relation to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, as al-Khidr did to Moses.

All such people are unbelievers who, by the consensus of the Muslims, must be fought, and any individual among them who is apprehended must be put to death. As for an individual from among the Khawārij or the Rāfidah who is apprehended, it is also reported that the two of them—I mean ʿUmar and ʿAlī—put such individuals to death. Although the jurists have differed over putting to death an individual

---

## Page 14067

from among these groups who has been apprehended, they have not differed over the obligation to kill them if they offer resistance. For fighting has a broader scope than putting someone to death: attacking aggressors and transgressing rebels are fought, even though, once apprehended, an individual among them may be punished only as Allah and His Messenger have commanded.

The scholars have included within the scope of these mass-transmitted reports from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, concerning the Khawārij—whether by their wording or their meaning—those followers of deviant inclinations who resemble them in departing from the law of Allah’s Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and the Muslim community. Indeed, some of these are worse than the Harūrī Khawārij, such as the Khurramiyyah, the Qarāmitah, and the Nusayriyyah. Anyone who believes that a human being is a god, or that someone other than the prophets is a prophet, and fights the Muslims over that belief is worse than the Harūrī Khawārij.

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, specifically mentioned the Harūrī Khawārij only because they were the first group of religious innovators to emerge after him; indeed, the first of them emerged during his lifetime. He mentioned them because of their proximity to his time, just as Allah and His Messenger singled out certain matters for mention because they occurred at that time, as in His words:

“And do not kill your children for fear of poverty.”

And His words:

“Whoever among you turns back from his religion—Allah will bring forth a people whom He loves and who love Him.”

There are other examples of this, including the Prophet’s naming particular tribes of the Ansār, and his singling out Aslam, Ghifār, Juhaynah, Tamīm, Asad, Ghatafān, and others for particular rulings because of characteristics they possessed. Anyone who possesses those same characteristics is included with them, because

---

## Page 14068

their being singled out for mention did not mean that the ruling applied exclusively to them; rather, those being addressed at that time needed them to be identified specifically. This applies where his wording does not encompass them. As for these Rāfidah, if they are not worse than the Khawārij explicitly mentioned in the texts, they are no less evil. Those Khawārij declared only ‘Uthmān, ‘Alī, and their respective followers to be disbelievers—not those who refrained from fighting or died before those events. The Rāfidah, however, declared Abū Bakr, ‘Umar, ‘Uthmān, the general body of the Muhājirūn and Ansār, and those who followed them in righteousness to be disbelievers—those with whom Allah is pleased and who are pleased with Him. They also declared the vast majority of Muhammad’s community, both earlier and later generations, to be disbelievers, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

They thus declare anyone a disbeliever who considers Abū Bakr, ‘Umar, and the Muhājirūn and Ansār to have been upright, invokes Allah’s pleasure upon them as Allah Himself is pleased with them, or seeks forgiveness for them as Allah commanded. For this reason, they declare the leading figures of the faith to be disbelievers:

Such figures include Sa‘īd ibn al-Musayyib, Abū Muslim al-Khawlānī, Uways al-Qaranī, ‘Atā’ ibn Abī Rabāh, and Ibrāhīm al-Nakha‘ī; likewise Mālik, al-Awzā‘ī, Abū Hanīfah, Hammād ibn Zayd, Hammād ibn Salamah, al-Thawrī, al-Shāfi‘ī, Ahmad ibn Hanbal, Fudayl ibn ‘Iyād, Abū Sulaymān al-Dārānī, Ma‘rūf al-Karkhī, al-Junayd ibn Muhammad, Sahl ibn ‘Abd Allāh al-Tustarī, and others. They regard it as lawful to shed the blood of those outside their group and call the latter’s school “the school of the majority,” as do the philosophers and others like them,

## Page 14069

and just as the Mu‘tazilah call it “the school of the rabble, the common people, and the people of hadith.” They hold that it is unlawful to marry the people of Syria, Egypt, the Hijaz, the Maghreb, Yemen, Iraq, Upper Mesopotamia, and all other Muslim lands, or to eat animals slaughtered by them. They consider the liquids in their possession—water, oils, and so forth—to be ritually impure. They regard their disbelief as graver than that of the Jews and Christians, because they consider the latter to be disbelievers who have never embraced Islam, whereas these people are apostates; and, by consensus, apostasy is a graver form of disbelief than never having embraced Islam.

For this reason, they assist the disbelievers against the Muslim majority, helping the Tatars against them. Through their wickedness and scheming, they were among the principal causes of Genghis Khan, king of the disbelievers, invading Muslim lands, of Hulagu’s advance into Iraq, of the capture of Aleppo, of the plundering of al-Sālihiyyah, and of other events. Those among them who served as viziers to Muslim rulers became involved in this, as did others who held no such office.

For this same reason, they plundered the Muslim army when it passed by them while returning to Egypt on the first occasion. For this reason, too, they waylay Muslims on the roads. This also explains the manifest assistance they have given the Tatars and the Franks against the Muslims, and the profound distress they have shown at Islam’s victories. Likewise, when the Muslims conquered the coastal towns—Acre and others—their support for the Christians and their preference for them over the Muslims became manifest in what people heard from them.

Everything I have described represents only some of their deeds; the reality is far worse.

## Page 14070

Those acquainted with these affairs agree that the fiercest attacks against those who face the qiblah, and the gravest harm inflicted upon Muslims by people claiming to belong to that community, have come from factions affiliated with them. They have therefore been the most dishonest sects of the Muslim community. Among the groups claiming allegiance to the qiblah, none lie more, believe falsehood more readily, or reject truth more persistently than they do. Hypocrisy, in particular, is more evident among them than among other people. Concerning this, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“The signs of a hypocrite are three: when he speaks, he lies; when he promises, he breaks his promise; and when he is entrusted with something, he betrays that trust.”

Another narration states:

“Whoever possesses four traits is a thorough hypocrite, and whoever possesses one of them has a trait of hypocrisy until he abandons it: when he speaks, he lies; when he promises, he breaks his promise; when he makes a covenant, he betrays it; and when he disputes, he transgresses all bounds.”

Everyone who has dealt with them knows that they possess these traits. This is why they practise dissimulation, which is a hallmark of the hypocrites and the Jews, and employ it in their dealings with Muslims:

“They say with their tongues what is not in their hearts.”

They swear that they did not say it, although they did. They swear by Allah to please the believers, whereas Allah and His Messenger have a greater right that they should seek to please Him.

They resemble the Jews in many respects, especially the Samaritans among the Jews, whom they resemble more closely than the other groups. They resemble them in claiming that the imamate belongs to

---

## Page 14071

a particular individual or clan, and in rejecting anyone who brings a truth other than what they themselves claim. They also resemble them in following their desires or distorting words from their proper places, delaying the breaking of the fast and the sunset prayer, and other such practices, and declaring unlawful the meat of animals slaughtered by others. They resemble Christians in their excessive veneration of human beings, their innovated acts of worship, their association of partners with Allah, and other matters. They ally themselves with Jews, Christians, and polytheists against Muslims. These are the traits of hypocrites.

Allah Most High says:

“O you who believe, do not take the Jews and Christians as allies. They are allies of one another. Whoever among you takes them as allies is indeed one of them.”

He also says:

“You see many of them taking the disbelievers as allies. Evil indeed is what their souls have sent ahead for them: Allah is angry with them, and they will remain in punishment forever.”

“Had they believed in Allah, the Prophet, and what was revealed to him, they would not have taken them as allies. But many of them are defiantly disobedient.”

They have neither reason nor transmitted authority, neither a sound religion nor worldly success. They perform neither Friday prayers nor congregational prayers—whereas the Khawārij used to perform both. They do not consider it lawful to wage jihad against the disbelievers under the Muslim rulers, to pray behind them, to obey them in obedience to Allah, or to enforce any of their rulings, because they believe that these things are permissible only under an infallible imam.

They believe that this infallible imam entered the underground chamber more than four hundred and forty years ago. To this day, he has not emerged, nor has anyone seen him, nor has he taught anyone the religion, nor

## Page 14072

has any benefit come through him; rather, only harm.

Yet they maintain that faith is valid only through belief in him, that no one is a believer unless he believes in him, and that none will enter Paradise except his followers: such ignorant, misguided inhabitants of the mountains and deserts, or those who have gained sway over them through falsehood, such as Ibn al-ʿŪd and others like him. These have recorded in their own handwriting some of the disgraceful things we have related about them, explicitly affirming what we have reported and even more.

Despite this, they declare unbelievers all who believe in Allah’s names and attributes found in the Quran and Sunnah, and all who believe in Allah’s predestination and decree: His perfect power, His all-encompassing will, and that He is the Creator of everything. Most of those they regard as their foremost scholars hold that Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, most of the Emigrants and Helpers, the Prophet’s wives such as ʿĀ’isha and Hafsa, and the other Muslim leaders and the Muslims at large never believed in Allah for even the blink of an eye. This is because, according to them, faith followed by unbelief is invalid from its very inception—a view also held by some Sunni scholars.

Some of them hold that the sexual organ with which the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had intercourse with ʿĀ’isha and Hafsa must be touched by the Fire, so that it may thereby be purified of intercourse with women whom they claim were unbelievers; for they regard intercourse with unbelieving women as forbidden.

Furthermore, they reject the established, mass-transmitted hadiths of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, recognized as such by the scholars, such as the hadiths recorded by al-Bukhārī and Muslim. They consider the poetry of Rāfida poets such as al-Himyarī, Kūshyār al-Daylamī, and ʿUmāra al-Yamanī to be better

---

## Page 14073

than the hadiths recorded by al-Bukhārī and Muslim. We have seen more lies and fabrications against the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, his Companions, and his relatives in their books than we have seen falsehoods in the books of the People of the Book—the Torah and the Gospel. Moreover, they leave neglected the mosques that Allah has commanded to be raised and in which His name is to be mentioned, holding neither Friday prayers nor congregational prayers there. They build mosques over graves, both spurious and genuine, treating them as shrines. Yet the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, cursed those who built mosques over graves and forbade his community to do so.

Five days before his death, he said:

“Those who came before you used to take graves as places of worship. Beware! Do not take graves as places of worship, for I forbid you to do so.”

They regard pilgrimage to these shrines, both spurious and genuine, as one of the greatest acts of worship. Indeed, some of their shaykhs prefer it to the pilgrimage to the House commanded by Allah and His Messenger. A full account of their condition would be lengthy. This makes clear that they are worse than the generality of those who follow deviant doctrines, and more deserving of being fought than the Kharijites.

This explains the widespread popular identification of the people of religious innovation with the Rāfida. Ordinary people commonly understand the opposite of a Sunni to be a Rāfidi alone, because their defiance of the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and the ordinances of his religion is more conspicuous than that of all other followers of deviant doctrines.

## Page 14074

The scholars have stated that Rāfidi doctrine originated with the heretic ‘Abd Allāh ibn Saba’. Moreover, most of their imams are heretics who profess Rāfidi doctrine only because it offers a way to destroy Islam.

This was the course followed by the leaders of the heretics who rose in Azerbaijan during the reign of al-Mu‘tasim alongside Bābak al-Khurramī, and were known as the “Khurramiyya” and the “Muhammira”; by the “esoteric Qarmatians,” who subsequently rose in Iraq and elsewhere and seized the Black Stone, which remained in their possession for some time—such as Abū Sa‘īd al-Jannābī and his followers; and by those who rose in the Maghrib, then crossed into Egypt, built Cairo, and claimed to be Fatimids.

Yet scholars of genealogy agree that they have no connection to the lineage of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and that their ancestry goes back to Magians and Jews. ---

## Page 14075

the divinity of ‘Alī and the imams.

Among the followers of these heretics—the people of the missionary centres—were those in Khurāsān, Syria, Yemen, and elsewhere. Thus Hūlāgū, the king of the unbelievers, sanctioned their idols.

Furthermore, the Kharijites were among the most truthful people and the most faithful to their covenants, whereas these people are among the most deceitful and the most prone to breaking covenants. Sometimes they deny texts authentically transmitted from him; at other times they deny the meanings of the revelation. Everyone knows that their disgraceful practices, both those we have mentioned and those we have not, contradict the message with which Allah sent Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

In His Book, Allah has praised the Companions, declared His pleasure with them, and spoken of seeking forgiveness for them; yet they disbelieve in the reality of all this. In His Book, He has commanded Friday prayer, jihad, and obedience to those in authority, yet they depart from these commands. In His Book, He has enjoined allegiance, affection, and brotherhood among the believers, and reconciliation between them, yet they depart from these teachings. In His Book, He has forbidden allegiance and affection toward the unbelievers, yet they have departed
