Allah created all creatures by His power and manifested among them the effects of His will

---

## Page 14194

and His wisdom and mercy, and made worship of Him the purpose for which He created them, as expressed in His commands to them. The foundation of this is knowing Him and loving Him.

Whoever Allah guides to His straight path, He grants mercy, knowledge, and understanding of His most beautiful names and highest attributes. He blesses him with turning to Him, trembling at His remembrance, humbly submitting to Him, and worshipping Him with devotion.

He longs for Him as eagles long for their nests, and is devoted to Him in love as a child is to its mother. He worships none but Him, with hope, fear, and love, and devotes his religion sincerely to Him to whom this world and the Hereafter belong: the Lord of the first and the last, Master of the Day of Judgment, Creator of what you see and what you do not see, Knower of the unseen and the seen, whose command, when He wills something, is to say to it, “Be,” and it is.

He does not take rivals besides Him, like those who take rivals besides Allah, loving them as they love Allah, whereas those who believe are stronger in their love for Allah. He associates no one with his Lord and takes no protector or intercessor besides Him—neither king, prophet, nor friend. For:

“There is no one in the heavens and the earth but will come to the Most Merciful as a servant. He has enumerated them and counted them precisely. And each of them will come to Him on the Day of Resurrection alone.”

It is then that his Master chooses him, singles him out, grants him sound judgment, and guides him, by His permission, to the truth concerning which people differed. For He guides whom He wills to a straight path.

For after Adam, peace be upon him, and before Noah, peace be upon him, people adhered to monotheism and sincere devotion to Allah, as had their father Adam, the father of humankind—peace be upon him—until they introduced polytheism and idol worship—an innovation originating from

---

## Page 14195

themselves—for which Allah had neither revealed a scripture nor sent a messenger. They were prompted by specious arguments that Satan had embellished through unsound analogies and misguided philosophy. Some claimed that the statues were talismans of the heavenly bodies, the degrees of the celestial sphere, and the higher spirits. Others fashioned them in the likenesses of prophets and righteous people who had lived among them. Others made them for the sake of the lower spirits among the jinn and devils. Still others followed different doctrines. Most merely followed their leaders and turned away from the path of guidance.

Allah then sent His Prophet Noah, peace be upon him, to call them to worship Allah alone, without partners, and forbid them to worship anything besides Him—even if they claimed that they worshipped these beings to draw nearer to Allah through them and take them as intercessors. He remained among them for a thousand years less fifty. When Allah informed him that none of his people would believe except those who had already believed, he prayed against them. In answer to his supplication, Allah Most High drowned the inhabitants of the earth. Messengers came after him in succession, until the religion of the Sabians and polytheists spread throughout the earth, when Nimrods and Pharaohs ruled its eastern and western lands.

Allah Most High then sent the leader of those devoted to pure monotheism, the foundation of the pure faith and the enduring word: Abraham, the close friend of the Most Merciful. He called people away from polytheism to sincere devotion to Allah alone. He forbade them to worship heavenly bodies and idols, saying:

“I have turned my face toward Him who created the heavens and the earth, inclining to truth, and I am not of the polytheists.”

And he said to his people:

---

## Page 14196

“Have you considered what you have been worshipping—you and your ancient forefathers? They are enemies to me, except the Lord of the worlds, who created me and guides me; who feeds me and gives me drink; who heals me when I am ill; who will cause me to die and then bring me to life; and who, I hope, will forgive my sin on the Day of Judgment.”

Abraham, peace be upon him, and those with him said to their people:

“We are free of you and of whatever you worship besides Allah. We reject you, and enmity and hatred have arisen between us and you forever, until you believe in Allah alone.”

Allah thus appointed the prophets and messengers from Abraham’s family, gave each of them distinctive qualities, and raised some above others in rank. He granted each of them signs of the kind that would bring people to faith. He turned Moses’ staff into a serpent, which swallowed the great multitude of ropes and staffs fashioned by the magician-philosophers. He parted the sea for him, leaving dry ground, with the water standing as barriers between twelve paths corresponding to the number of the tribes. He sent with him lice, frogs, and blood. He shaded him and his people with white clouds that travelled with them, and sent down manna and quails upon them every morning. Whenever they grew thirsty, Moses struck the rock with his staff, and twelve springs gushed forth from it; each group knew its own drinking place.

After him, He sent prophets from among the Children of Israel. Through some, Allah brought the dead to life; through others, He healed the sick. To some He disclosed whatever He willed of His unseen knowledge; for others He subjected created beings; and some He sent

---

## Page 14197

with various kinds of miracles. This is agreed upon by all religious communities. In the books held by the Jews and Christians, the prophetic writings they possess, the accounts of the prophets—peace be upon them—such as Isaiah, Jeremiah, Daniel, Habakkuk, David, Solomon, and others, and in the Book of Kings and other books, there is much from which lessons may be drawn.

The Children of Israel were a hard-hearted, disobedient people. At times they worshipped idols and graven images, and at times they worshipped Allah. At times they killed the prophets unjustly, and at times they used the flimsiest stratagems to make lawful what Allah had forbidden. They were first cursed through the words of David, and Jerusalem suffered the destruction well known to all religious communities.

Then Allah sent the Messiah, son of Mary, as a messenger before whom other messengers had passed away. He made him and his mother a sign for humankind by creating him without a father, thereby demonstrating the perfection of His power and the all-encompassing reach of His word. He brought humankind into being in four ways: He made Adam without either a male or a female; He created his wife Eve from a male without a female; He created the Messiah, son of Mary, from a female without a male; and He created all other human beings from the pair, male and female.

He granted His servant, the Messiah, clear signs in accordance with His established way. The Messiah raised the dead, healed those born blind and those afflicted with leprosy, and told people what they ate and what they stored in their homes. He called people to Allah and to His worship, following the way of

---

## Page 14198

his fellow messengers, confirming those who had come before him and giving glad tidings of the one who would come after him. The Children of Israel had grown insolent and rebellious, while his approach was chiefly marked by gentleness, mercy, forgiveness, and pardon. Allah placed compassion and mercy in the hearts of those who followed him, and made some of them priests and monks.

People divided into three groups concerning the Messiah—peace be upon him—and the disciples who followed him:

One group rejected him and disbelieved in him. They claimed that he was the son of a prostitute, slandered his mother, and attributed his paternity to Joseph the carpenter. They maintained that none of the Torah’s law had been abrogated, and that Allah had not abrogated what He had prescribed following their treatment of the prophets, including the burdens imposed upon them concerning impurities and foods.

Another group went to excess concerning him, claiming that he was Allah or the son of Allah, that divinity had clothed itself in humanity, and that the Lord of all worlds had descended and sent down His son to be crucified and killed as a ransom for the sin of Adam—peace be upon him. They claimed that the One God, the Eternal Refuge, who neither begets nor is born, and to whom none is comparable, had begotten and taken a son. They also claimed that He is a living, knowing, powerful God: one substance, three hypostases; and that one of these is the hypostasis of the Word, which is knowledge, [and] (1) that it clothed itself in human nature—even though it is known that one of the two cannot be separated from the others unless they were to make Him three distinct gods. Yet this is something they do not profess.

## Page 14199

They became deeply divided and fragmented over the Trinity and union, in ways no rational person would accept. No scriptural evidence supports this apart from ambiguous expressions in the Gospel and earlier scriptures, which are explained by unambiguous passages in those same scriptures. These all affirm that the Messiah is Allah’s servant, worshipping Him alone, praying to Him, and humbly beseeching Him.

The foundation of religion is faith in Allah and His Messenger, as the Seal of the Prophets and Messengers said:

“I have been commanded to fight the people until they testify that none has the right to be worshipped except Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah.”

He also said:

“Do not praise me excessively as the Christians praised Jesus son of Mary. I am only a servant, so call me Allah’s servant and His Messenger.”

Religion thus consists in affirming Allah’s oneness and acknowledging His messengers. This is why the Sabians and polytheists, such as the Brahmins and other deniers of prophethood, associate partners with Allah in their beliefs and worship, and hold corrupt beliefs concerning His messengers.

Those who profess a Trinity in matters of divine oneness and union in matters of messengership have corruption within the very foundation of their religion. This corruption is evident both from the natural disposition with which Allah created humankind and from the scriptures He revealed. This is why the general pattern among their leaders—priests and monks, including patriarchs, metropolitans, and bishops—is that, when one of them becomes learned and discerning, he abandons his religion and becomes a hypocrite before the rulers and common people of his faith

---

## Page 14200

and is content with his authority over them and the worldly advantages he gains. Such were the man in Jerusalem known as “Ibn al-Būrī,” the man in Damascus known as “Ibn al-Quff,” the man in Constantinople whom they call “the pope,” and many leading popes, metropolitans, and bishops. When discerning men spoke with them, they acknowledged that they did not hold Christian beliefs. They remained as they were only out of habit and for the sake of leadership, just as kings and wealthy men retain their sovereignty and wealth.

Thus, you find that most of their learned men devote themselves only to some branch of the mathematical sciences, such as logic, astronomy, arithmetic, and astrology; or to natural science, such as medicine and knowledge of the elements; or to discussing metaphysics in the manner of the Sabian philosophers to whom Abraham, Allah’s intimate friend, peace be upon him, was sent. They have cast behind their backs the religion of the Messiah and the messengers before and after him, preserving only its outward forms for the sake of the rulers and the common people.

As for the monks, they have devised schemes and tricks to deceive the common people that are plain to every rational person. Indeed, learned men have written books about the monks’ tricks. One example is the fire that used to be manufactured at Qumāma. They coat a fine thread with sandarūs and quickly set it alight, so that the flame descends. The ignorant then believe that it has descended from heaven and carry it to the sea. Yet it is the handiwork of that monk, whom people see with their own eyes; he and others have admitted that they manufacture it.

Those who uphold the truth, from every group, have agreed that it is not permissible to worship Allah

---

## Page 14201

—exalted is He—by means of anything that has no basis in reality. Yet the hypocrites may imagine that the miracles reported of the Messiah and others are of the same kind as that manufactured fire.

The same applies to their tricks involving the suspension of the cross, the weeping of statues fashioned in the likeness of the Messiah, his mother, and others, and similar things. Every rational person knows that all this is fabricated falsehood, and that all Allah’s prophets and righteous servants are innocent of every deception, falsehood, and fabrication, just as they are innocent of the sorcery of Pharaoh’s magicians.

Furthermore, these people turned to the religious law by which they worship Allah and contradicted their Jewish predecessors, although they enjoin adherence to the Torah except where the Messiah abrogated it. The former fell short in their treatment of the prophets, even killing them; the latter went to extremes concerning them, even worshipping them and their statues.

The former said:
“It is not fitting for Allah to change and revoke what He has commanded, whether at another time or through another prophet.”

The latter said:
“Rather, rabbis and priests may change whatever they wish and forbid whatever they see fit. If someone commits a sin, they impose upon him whatever acts of worship they see fit and forgive him.”

Some among them claim to breathe something of the Holy Spirit into a woman, making incense an offering.

The former said:
“He has forbidden us many things.”

The latter said:
“Everything from a gnat to an elephant is lawful: eat whatever you wish and leave whatever you wish.”

The former said:
“Impurities are a grave matter: one must not even sit or eat with a menstruating woman.”

The latter say:
“Nothing on you is impure.”

Nor do they prescribe circumcision or ritual bathing after

---

## Page 14202

sexual impurity, nor do they require the removal of impurities, even though the Messiah and the disciples followed the law of the Torah.

Neither the Messiah nor the disciples commanded prayer facing east; it was introduced by Constantine or someone else. Likewise, the cross was introduced by Constantine on his own judgment and on the basis of a dream he claimed to have seen. Neither the Messiah nor the disciples commanded any of this. The religion by which Allah’s servants seek nearness to Him must be one that Allah has commanded and prescribed through His messengers and prophets. Otherwise, all religious innovations are misguidance, and idols came to be worshipped only through religious innovations. Likewise, neither the Messiah nor the disciples commanded the introduction of melodies into prayers.

In short, most of the forms of worship and festivals they observe were neither revealed by Allah in a scripture nor conveyed by a messenger He sent. Yet they have tenderness and mercy, and this is part of Allah’s religion, unlike the former, who have hardness of heart and hatred—things Allah Most High has forbidden. Nevertheless, the former possess discernment and reason, alongside obstinacy and arrogance, whereas the latter are astray from the truth and ignorant of Allah’s path.

---

## Page 14203

Moreover, these two communities split into numerous factions over the very foundations of their religion and their beliefs concerning the One they worship and their messenger.

One group says that the divine and human substances became one substance, one nature, and one hypostasis. These are the Jacobites. Another says: Rather, they are two substances, two natures, and two hypostases. These are the Nestorians. A third affirms union in one respect but not another. These are the Melkites.

Groups of scholars among the People of the Book, both in earlier and later times, have embraced faith and emigrated to Allah and His Messenger. They have written works on the evidence in Allah’s scriptures establishing the prophethood of the Prophet, the Seal of the Messengers, and on passages in the Torah, Psalms, and Gospel that they had not reflected upon. The same applies to the disciples.

When factions arose among them, Allah, by His permission, guided those who believed to the truth concerning their disagreements. He therefore sent the Prophet whose coming had been foretold by the Messiah and the prophets before him, calling people to the faith of Abraham and the religion of the messengers before and after him: worshipping Allah alone, without any partner, and devoting all religion sincerely to Allah. He cleansed the earth of idol worship and purified religion of every form of associating partners with Allah, great or small, after idols had been worshipped in Syria and elsewhere under the rule of the Children of Israel and of those who said, “We are Christians.” He commanded belief in all of Allah’s revealed scriptures, such as the Torah, Gospel, Psalms, and Criterion, and in all of Allah’s prophets, from Adam to Muhammad.

Allah Most High says:

“They say, ‘Be Jews or Christians, and you will be guided.’ Say,

---

## Page 14204

‘Rather, we follow the religion of Abraham, who inclined to the truth and was not one of the polytheists.’”

“Say, ‘We believe in Allah and in what has been revealed to us, and what was revealed to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and the tribes, and what Moses and Jesus were given, and what the prophets were given by their Lord. We make no distinction between any of them, and to Him we submit.’”

“So if they believe as you believe, then they are rightly guided. But if they turn away, they are only in opposition. Allah will suffice you against them, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.”

“Ours is the religion of Allah—and who is better than Allah in ordaining religion? And we worship Him alone.”

Allah commanded that Messenger to call people, with justice, to worship Him alone. He Most High said:

“Say, ‘O People of the Book, come to a word common to us and you: that we worship none but Allah, associate nothing with Him, and do not take one another as lords besides Allah.’ But if they turn away, say, ‘Bear witness that we submit to Allah.’”

He Most High also said:

“It is not for any human being that Allah should speak to him except by revelation or from behind a veil.”

He Most High also said:

“It is not for any human being whom Allah has given the Scripture, sound judgment, and prophethood to then say to people, ‘Be servants of mine rather than Allah.’ Rather, ‘Be devoted scholars of the Lord through your teaching of the Scripture and your study of it.’”

“Nor would he command you to take the angels and prophets as lords. Would he command you to disbelieve after you have submitted to Allah?”

He commanded him to direct his prayer and pilgrimage toward Allah’s Sacred House, built by His close friend Abraham, the father of the prophets and leader of those devoted to Allah alone. He made his community a community of moderation, so they did not go to excess concerning

---

## Page 14205

the prophets, as did those who equated them with Allah, ascribed to them a measure of divinity, worshipped them, and took them as intercessors. Nor did they mistreat them as did those who harmed them, disregarded their sanctity, and turned away from obeying them. Rather, they honoured the prophets—that is, revered and supported them—believed in what they brought, obeyed and followed them, took them as their guides, loved and esteemed them. They worshipped none but Allah, relied upon none but Him, and sought help from none but Him, devoting their religion sincerely to Him and turning away from all false worship.

The same was true of religious laws. They said: “Whatever Allah commands us to do, we obey, and whatever He forbids us, we refrain from. If He forbids us something He previously permitted—as He forbade the Children of Israel things He had permitted Jacob—or permits us something previously forbidden—as the Messiah permitted some of what Allah had forbidden the Children of Israel—we hear and obey.”

As for those other than Allah’s messengers and prophets, they have no right to alter Allah’s religion or introduce into it anything Allah has not authorized. The messengers spoke only to convey what came from Allah. For creation and command belong to Him, glorified is He: just as none but Him creates, none but Him commands.

“Judgment belongs to Allah alone. He has commanded that you worship none but Him. That is the upright religion, but most people do not know.”

This community also followed a middle course regarding ritual purity and impurity, the lawful and unlawful, and moral conduct. They did not practise severity alone, as the former did, nor did they practise compassion alone

---

## Page 14206

as the latter did. Rather, they treated Allah’s enemies with severity and His allies with compassion and mercy. Concerning the Messiah, they affirmed what Allah, glorified and exalted is He, said, and what the Messiah and the disciples said—not what was invented by those who went to extremes or those who failed to give him his due. The disciples foretold that the last of the messengers would be sent from the land of Yemen and would be sent with the rod of discipline, namely, the sword. The Messiah foretold that he would come with clear proofs and interpretation, whereas the Messiah himself had come with parables. This subject would require a lengthy explanation.

I offer this reminder, as one calling to the faith, to a leading figure among his co-religionists and his people only because I learned of his religious devotion, virtue, love of knowledge, and desire for scholarly discussion. I also saw that Shaykh Abū al-ʿAbbās al-Maqdisī was grateful to the king for his gentleness, kindness, and attentive reception, and was likewise grateful to the priests and others.

We are people who wish good for everyone, and we wish that Allah grant you the good of both this world and the Hereafter. The greatest act by which Allah is worshipped is offering sincere counsel to His creation; it was for this that Allah sent the prophets and messengers. No counsel is greater than that concerning a servant’s relationship with his Lord. For the servant must inevitably meet Allah, and Allah will surely call His servant to account, as He, exalted is He, says:

“We will surely question those to whom messengers were sent, and We will surely question the messengers.”

As for this world, its affairs are insignificant, and what seems great in it is small. Ultimately, its pursuits come down to power and wealth. The most a person with power can attain is to be like Pharaoh, who was drowned by

---

## Page 14207

Allah in the sea in retribution. The most a wealthy person can attain is to be like Korah, whom Allah caused the earth to swallow for harming Allah’s prophet Moses, so that he will continue sinking into it until the Day of Resurrection. These counsels of the Messiah and the messengers before and after him all enjoin worshipping Allah, devoting oneself to the Hereafter, and turning away from the fleeting splendour of worldly life.

Since worldly affairs are so paltry, I considered that the greatest gift one could offer a leader of his people would be to open a discussion of knowledge and religion, exchanging thoughts on what brings one nearer to Allah. Discussion of subsidiary matters rests upon fundamental principles.

You know that Allah’s religion is not determined by personal desires or by the customs of one’s forefathers and community. Rather, a discerning person examines what the messengers brought, what people agree upon, and where they differ. In his private relationship with Allah Most High, he approaches Him, exalted is He, with sound belief and righteous deeds. Even if a person cannot disclose everything within himself to everyone, he still benefits to that extent.

If I see in the king a desire for knowledge and goodness, I will correspond with him and answer the questions he asks. It had occurred to me to come to Cyprus to further religious and worldly interests. But if I see conduct from the king that pleases Allah and His Messenger, I will deal with him as his actions warrant. For the king and his people know that Allah has displayed, among the miracles of

---

## Page 14208

His messengers in general and Muhammad in particular, signs by which He has strengthened His religion and humbled the unbelievers and hypocrites.

When the Mongol leader Ghāzān and his followers came to Damascus, he had already professed Islam. Yet Allah, His Messenger, and the believers did not approve of their deeds, for they did not adhere to Allah’s religion. I met with him and his commanders, and various exchanges took place between us that would take too long to recount; they must have reached the king’s ears. Allah humbled him and his soldiers before us, until we were striking them with our own hands and shouting at them. The ruler of Sīs, who was with them, seemed no more than the lowliest servant: one of the muezzins accompanying us shouted at him and insulted him, while he dared not answer. Indeed, Ghāzān’s ministers spoke of things that revealed his ill intentions towards him.

I was present when your envoys came to the coastal region. The Tatars told me about the matter in which the ruler of Sīs sought to mediate between you and him, holding out false hopes to you. The Tatars were among those who most reviled and humiliated the ruler of Sīs. Despite this, we treated the people of your faith kindly and defended them.

All the Christians know that I spoke to the Tatars about releasing the prisoners, and Ghāzān and Qutlū Shāh released them. I also spoke to Mūlāy about them, and he agreed to release the Muslims. He said to me:

“But we have Christians whom we captured in Jerusalem; they will not be released.”

I told him:

“No—all the Jews and Christians you hold who are under our covenant of protection must also be released. We shall secure their release and leave no prisoner behind, whether of our own faith

---

## Page 14209

or those under our covenant of protection.” We secured the release of as many Christians as Allah willed. Such are our deeds and our kindness, and our reward rests with Allah. Likewise, everyone knows the kindness, mercy, and compassion we show the Christian captives in our hands, as the last of the messengers enjoined upon us when he said near the end of his life:

“Observe prayer, and care for those whom your right hands possess.”

Allah Most High says in His Book:

“And they give food, despite their love for it, to the needy, the orphan, and the captive.”

Despite the Tatars’ submission to this faith and their professed affiliation with it, we neither deceived them nor behaved hypocritically towards them. Rather, we explained to them their corruption and departure from Islam, which made it necessary to wage jihad against them. We also explained that Allah’s divinely supported troops and victorious armies stationed in Syria and Egypt have continued to prevail over those who oppose them and triumph over their enemies.

During this period, when word spread among the common people that the Tatars were Muslims, the army held back from fighting them; even so, it killed ten-odd thousand of them, while fewer than two hundred Muslims were killed. When the army withdrew to Egypt and learned of the corruption and irreligion of this accursed faction, Allah’s troops marched forth, the earth resounding beneath their tread. They filled the plains and mountains, their numbers, strength, equipment, faith, and sincerity astounding minds and hearts. They were surrounded by Allah’s angels, with whom He has continually reinforced the community devoted to pure monotheism and sincere worship of its Creator.

The enemy fled before them and did not stand to face them. Then the enemy advanced a second time, and He sent upon it such

---

## Page 14210

punishment that destroyed men and horses, and it withdrew, humbled and exhausted. Allah fulfilled His promise and granted victory to His servant. The enemy now suffers grievous affliction, crushing reversals, and tribulation that has encompassed it. Islam, meanwhile, continues to grow in might and enjoy blessing upon blessing, for the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“At the turn of every century, Allah sends this community someone who renews its religion for it.”

This religion continues to advance and undergo renewal. I sincerely counsel the king and his companions—by Allah, besides whom there is no god, who sent down the Torah, the Gospel, and the Criterion.

The king knows that when the delegation from Najrān—all of them Christians, including the bishop and others—came to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, he called them to Allah, His Messenger, and Islam. They spoke to him about the Messiah and debated with him. When the proof against them had been established, they began to evade it. Allah therefore commanded His Prophet to invite them to a mutual invocation of curses, as He said:

“Whoever disputes with you concerning him after the knowledge that has come to you, say: ‘Come, let us call our sons and your sons, our women and your women, ourselves and yourselves; then let us pray earnestly and invoke Allah’s curse upon the liars.’”

When the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, proposed this, they consulted among themselves and said: “You know that he is a prophet, and that no one who has engaged in a mutual invocation of curses with a prophet has ever prospered.” They therefore paid him the jizya, entered the covenant of protection, and asked to be excused from the mutual invocation of curses.

Likewise, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, sent his letter to Caesar, who ruled the Christians in Syria and across the sea as far as Constantinople and elsewhere, and he was a king

## Page 14211

of noble character.

When he read the Prophet’s letter and inquired about his identifying signs, he recognized that he was the prophet whose coming the Messiah had foretold—the very one whom Allah had promised Abraham concerning his son Ishmael. He began calling his Christian people to follow him. He honoured the Prophet’s letter, kissed it, and placed it against his eyes, saying: “I wish I could reach him and wash his feet. Were it not for my royal position, I would go to him.”

As for the Negus, the Christian king of Abyssinia, when news of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, reached him through the Companions who had emigrated to his land, he believed in him and acknowledged his truthfulness. He sent his son and his companions to join him as emigrants. When he died, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, offered the funeral prayer for him.

When he heard the surah “Kāf Hā Yā ‘Ayn Sād,” he wept. When they told him what they believed about the Messiah, he said: “By Allah, Jesus does not exceed what you have said by so much as this twig.” He also said: “This and what Moses brought surely come from the same source of light.”

The practice of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was that any Christian who believed in Allah, His angels, His Books, and His messengers became a member of his community, enjoying the same rights and bearing the same obligations as its other members. Such a person received two rewards: one for his faith in the Messiah and another for his faith in Muhammad.

As for those among the nations who did not believe in him, Allah commanded that they be fought, as He said in His Book:

“Fight those among the People of the Scripture who do not believe in Allah or the Last Day, do not forbid what Allah and His Messenger have forbidden, and do not follow the religion of truth, until they pay the jizya with their own hands, humbled.”

---

## Page 14212

As for those who do not believe in Allah, they go so far as to revile Him, saying that He is one of three and that He was crucified. They do not believe in His messengers; rather, they claim that the one who was carried in the womb and born, who ate, drank, relieved himself and slept, is Allah and the son of Allah, and that Allah or His son dwelt within him and clothed Himself in him. They deny what Muhammad, the last of the messengers, brought and distort the texts of the Torah and the Gospel. Indeed, the four Gospels contain the contradictions and disagreements they do concerning what Allah commanded and made obligatory. They do not follow the truth. The religion of truth means acknowledging what Allah has commanded and made obligatory: worshipping and obeying Him.

They do not regard as forbidden what Allah and His Messenger have forbidden: blood, carrion and pork. Pork has remained forbidden from the time of Adam to Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace; no prophet ever permitted it. Indeed, Christian scholars know that it is forbidden. Nothing prevents some of them from declaring this except hope of gain and fear, while others are prevented by obstinacy, habit and similar considerations.

They do not believe in the Last Day. Although most of them acknowledge bodily resurrection, they do not acknowledge what Allah has told us concerning eating, drinking, clothing, sexual relations, bliss and punishment in Paradise and Hell. Most of their scholars are secret unbelievers: they conceal this and mock their common people—especially the women and monastics among them—for their feeble understanding.

Whoever is in this condition, Allah has commanded His Messenger to wage jihad against him until he enters Allah’s religion or pays the jizya. This is the religion of Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Moreover, the Messiah did not command jihad, especially jihad against the community

---

## Page 14213

of pure monotheism—nor did the disciples after him. O king, how can you regard it as lawful to shed blood, take women captive, and seize property without any warrant from Allah and His messengers?

Does the king not know that in our lands there are Christians living under covenants of protection and safe-conduct whose numbers none but Allah can count? Our treatment of them is well known. How, then, can they treat Muslim prisoners in ways that no person of honor or religion would accept? I am not speaking of the king, his household, or his brothers, for Abū al-‘Abbās is deeply grateful to the king and his household and acknowledges the kindness they have shown him. Moreover, many of them were captured only through treachery, and treachery is forbidden in every religion, revealed law, and system of governance. How, then, can you regard it as lawful to take possession of those captured through treachery? Moreover, the Muslims have among their men the fidāwiyya, who assassinate kings in

---

## Page 14214

their beds and on horseback—men whose exploits, both past and recent, have reached the king. Among the Muslims are also righteous men whose supplications Allah does not reject and whose requests He does not disappoint; the Lord is angry when they are angry and pleased when they are pleased. These Tatars, despite their great numbers and their affiliation with the Muslims, were beset by calamities beyond description when the Muslims became angry with them.

How, then, O king, can it be fitting for a people who border the Muslims on most sides to treat them in this manner, which no reasonable person would approve, whether a Muslim or someone bound by a covenant? Moreover, you know that the Muslims bear no blame whatsoever; rather, they deserve praise for what they have done. Their religion is the very one whose excellence all reasonable people unanimously acknowledge. Even the philosophers agree that no religion better than this has ever appeared in the world. Conclusive proofs have established the obligation to follow it.

Furthermore, these coastal lands have remained in their hands; indeed, even Cyprus was taken from them less than three hundred years ago. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, promised them that they would remain triumphant until the Day of Resurrection.

What assurance, then, does the king have that the Lord of all people and lands will not avenge these oppressed prisoners in his land, just as He avenges others? And what assurance does he have that the Muslims’ zeal for their faith will not move them to do to his land what they have done to others? If we see proper conduct from the king and his companions, we will treat them kindly. Otherwise, Allah will surely help whoever is wronged.

---

## Page 14215

And you know that this is among the easiest things for the Muslims to do. My sole purpose now is to address you in the best manner and to help in examining matters of knowledge, following the truth, and doing what is required. If the king has someone whose reason and religious integrity he trusts, let him discuss with that person the foundations of knowledge and the true nature of religions. He should not be content to be among those blindly imitating Christians who neither listen nor reason: they are only like cattle—indeed, they are even further astray.

The foundation of this is to seek Allah’s help, ask Him for guidance, and say:

“O Allah, show me the truth as truth and help me to follow it. Show me falsehood as falsehood and help me to avoid it. Do not let it become unclear to me, lest I follow my desires and go astray.”

And say:

“O Allah, Lord of Gabriel, Michael, and Isrāfīl, Originator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the seen, You judge between Your servants concerning that over which they differed. By Your permission, guide me to the truth concerning which there is disagreement. Indeed, You guide whom You will to a straight path.”

This letter does not allow for a fuller discussion than this. I desire for the king only what will benefit him in this world and the Hereafter, and that consists of two things.

(The first) concerns him alone: that he gain understanding of knowledge and religion, that the truth become clear to him and doubt be dispelled, and that he worship Allah as He has commanded. This is better for him than dominion over the entire world. It is what the Messiah was sent with and taught the disciples.

(The second) concerns both him and the Muslims: that he assist the prisoners in his land, treat them kindly, and command his subjects to treat them kindly

## Page 14216

and help us secure their release. For mistreating them makes the king answerable under his own religion and the religion of Allah Most High, and answerable to the Muslims. Helping to secure their release, however, is a good deed to his credit in his own religion, in the religion of Allah Most High, and in the eyes of the Muslims. The Messiah was foremost among those who urged such conduct.

It is utterly astonishing that Christians should take people captive—whether treacherously or otherwise—when those people have not fought them, while the Messiah says:

The religion of Islam commands us to help the poor and the weak. For many reasons, the king has an even greater obligation to help in this, especially since the Messiah urges it in the Gospel and commands mercy for all and goodness that extends to everyone, like sunshine and rain. If the king and his companions help us free the captives and treat them kindly, they will gain the greatest share of benefit from this in this world and the Hereafter. As for the Hereafter, Allah will reward and recompense them for it. This is something about which there is no doubt among Christian scholars

## Page 14217

who do not follow their desires; indeed, anyone who fears Allah and is fair-minded knows that they were taken captive unjustly, especially those seized through treachery. Among Christian kings, priests, monks, and ordinary people, there have always been those who surpass others in knowledge and religious devotion. He therefore treats them in a manner that benefits him in this world and the Hereafter.

Furthermore, the sayings of the prophets and the steadfastly truthful concerning the release of captives and the reward for freeing slaves are well known to anyone who seeks them out. Whatever the king does in his dealings with them, he will reap its fruits.

## Page 14218

“The martyr is granted six blessings: he is forgiven with the first drop of his blood; he sees his place in Paradise; he is clothed in the robe of faith; he is married to seventy-two of the maidens of Paradise with beautiful, wide eyes; he is protected from the trial of the grave; and he is kept safe from the greatest terror on the Day of Resurrection.”

Furthermore, there are many times as many Christians in their lands as there are Muslims among you. Among them are Christian leaders with few equals across the sea. ## Page 14219

those who affirm the truth and never lets the reward of those who do good go to waste.

Abū al-‘Abbās, the bearer of this letter, has spoken among us of the virtues of the king and his brothers, inclining our hearts towards him. I have therefore written to the king upon learning of his desire for goodness and his inclination towards knowledge and religion. In offering sincere counsel to the king and his companions and seeking their welfare, I am among the representatives of the Messiah and all the other prophets. For Muhammad’s community is the best community brought forth for mankind: they desire good for all people in this world and the Hereafter, enjoin what is right, forbid what is wrong, call them to Allah, and help them pursue what benefits their religious and worldly affairs.

If the king has received reports disparaging some of them or their religion, then either the informant was lying or he failed to understand the reports’ meaning and the actual circumstances. If, however, he truthfully reported sins, indecencies, or injustices committed by some of them, such things inevitably occur in every community. Indeed, the evil found among Muslims is far less than that found among others, while the good found among them has no equal elsewhere.

The king, and every sensible person, knows that most Christians depart from the precepts of the Messiah and the Apostles and from the epistles of Paul and other saints—even if most of what they retain of Christianity consists of drinking wine, eating pork, venerating the cross, and invented ordinances for which Allah has sent down no authority—and that some of them regard as lawful certain things forbidden by Christian religious law. This concerns what they themselves acknowledge. As for

---

## Page 14220

their failure to abide by what they do not acknowledge, that applies to them all. Indeed, we have an established report from the Messenger of Allah—the truthful one whose truthfulness is confirmed, may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

“The Messiah, Jesus son of Mary, will descend here among us at the white minaret in Damascus, resting his hands on the shoulders of two angels. He will break the cross, kill swine, abolish the jizya, and accept nothing from anyone but Islam. He will kill the messiah of misguidance, the one-eyed Dajjāl, whom the Jews will follow. The Muslims will gain power over the Jews, until trees and stones say: ‘O Muslim, there is a Jew behind me; kill him.’ Allah will exact retribution from the Jews on behalf of the Messiah son of Mary, the messiah of guidance, for harming him and rejecting him when he was sent to them.”

As for what has been related to us concerning the Christians, and what Allah will do to them by granting the Muslims victory and power over them, this is something I will not tell the king, lest it distress him. My sincere counsel to him, however, is that whoever has previously shown kindness to the Muslims and been favourably disposed towards them will fare well with them, in proportion to the good he has done. For Allah says:

“So whoever does an atom’s weight of good will see it.”

“And whoever does an atom’s weight of evil will see it.”

I conclude this letter by urging that Shaykh Abū al-ʿAbbās and the other captives be treated well and assisted, that the followers of the Quran in their custody be treated gently, and that no attempt be made to change the religion of any one of them. The king will see the outcome of all this. We shall repay the king for it many times beyond what he has in mind. Allah knows that I intend good for the king, for Allah Most High has commanded us to do so and has prescribed that we desire good for every

## Page 14221

person, to show compassion towards Allah’s creation, to call them to Allah and His religion, and to protect them from the devils among humans and jinn. Praise be to Allah, Lord of all worlds. May His blessings be upon His messengers, especially Muhammad, the last of the prophets and messengers, and may peace be upon them all.

He was asked:

Is Medina part of al-Shām (Greater Syria)?

He answered:

The Prophet’s city—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—is part of the Hijaz, by the agreement of the scholars. No one, Muslim or otherwise, has said that the Prophet’s city is part of al-Shām. Only someone ignorant of the boundaries of al-Shām and the Hijaz, and ignorant of what the jurists, linguists and others have said, would make such a claim.

However, people do say, “Medina is Syrian and Mecca is Yemeni,” meaning that Medina is closer to al-Shām and Mecca is closer to Yemen. Mecca is not part of Yemen, nor is Medina part of al-Shām.

During his final illness, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, commanded that the Jews and Christians leave the Arabian Peninsula—which is the Hijaz—so they were expelled by ʿUmar

---

## Page 14222

ibn al-Khattāb, may Allah be pleased with him, from Medina, Khaybar, Yanbu, al-Yamāmah, and the districts of these regions. He did not expel them from al-Shām; rather, when he conquered al-Shām, he allowed the Jews and Christians to remain in Jordan, Palestine, and elsewhere, just as he allowed them to remain in Damascus and elsewhere.

The soil of al-Shām differs from that of the Hijaz. This difference can be observed at the bend known as al-Suwān Pass: one finds that the soil there differs from the soil here, just as the soil of al-Shām differs from that of Egypt.

Whatever lies on this side of Wādī al-Munhanā belongs to al-Shām, such as Ma‘ān. As for al-‘Ulā, Tabūk, and similar places, they belong to the Hijaz. And Allah knows best.

## Page 14223

He replied:

Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds. As for their claim that the Muslims wronged them by closing these churches, this is a lie that contradicts the consensus of the Muslims. The Muslim scholars of the four schools—those of Abū Hanīfa, Mālik, al-Shāfiʿī, and Ahmad—and other imams, such as Sufyān al-Thawrī, al-Awzāʿī, al-Layth ibn Saʿd, and others, together with their predecessors among the Companions and Successors—may Allah be pleased with them all—agree that if the ruler demolished every church in territory conquered by force, such as Egypt, the Sawād region of Iraq, the Syrian mainland, and similar territories, exercising his legal judgment and following those who hold this view, he would not thereby be acting unjustly. Rather, those who hold this view are obliged to obey him and assist him in doing so. If they refused to submit to the Muslims’ ruling concerning them, they would be breaking the covenant, and their lives and property would thereby become forfeit.

As for their assertion that these churches have stood since the time of the Commander of the Faithful, ʿUmar ibn al-Khattāb—may Allah be pleased with him—and that the Rightly Guided Caliphs allowed them to retain them, this too is a lie. For it is known through mass transmission that Cairo was built more than three hundred years after ʿUmar ibn al-Khattāb—may Allah be pleased with him. It was built after Baghdad, Basra, Kufa, and Wāsit. The Muslims have unanimously agreed that, in cities founded by Muslims, it was not

## Page 14226

How much more, then, does this apply to Muslim cities! Indeed, if they had a church in territory conquered by force, such as Iraq, Egypt, and similar lands, and the Muslims built a city around it, the Muslims would be entitled to take possession of that church, so that no church would remain in Muslim cities without a covenant protecting it.

Thus, even if a church had existed on the site of Cairo or a similar city before its construction, the Muslims would have been entitled to take possession of it, since the territory was conquered by force. “O you who believe, fulfil your covenants.”

It has been said that these refer to what Allah and His Messenger have commanded. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, placed this verse at the beginning of the letter he wrote to Amr ibn Hazm when he appointed him governor of Najrān. The letter to Amr contains prescribed obligations, blood-money payments, and practices made obligatory by revealed law.

Allah also says to the believers:

“Remember Allah’s favour upon you and His covenant by which He bound you when you said, ‘We hear and obey.’”

The Quran commentators have mentioned that this verse was revealed concerning the Prophet’s taking the pledge of allegiance from the Ansār on the night of al-Aqabah. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had bound them by a covenant to what was already obligatory by Allah’s command: to listen to him and obey. Allah reminded them of that covenant so that they would fulfil it, although it imposed nothing beyond what Allah’s command had already made obligatory.

In this verse, He commanded them to remember His favour upon them and His covenant. Thus, He mentioned both grounds of obligation, for the obligation established by revealed law is also binding by virtue of His lordship—that is, His bestowal of blessings upon them. Hence the hadith states:

“Love Allah for the blessings with which He sustains you.”

For this reason, authors writing on the fundamentals of religion customarily begin by discussing the first blessing Allah bestowed upon His servants and the first duty incumbent upon them, and they discuss

---

## Page 14240

“the question of the obligation to thank the Benefactor”: whether this is obligatory by reason as well as by revealed law. This is why the Quran’s approach is to remind people of Allah’s blessings upon them, for these call for gratitude to Him, which consists in fulfilling the obligations prescribed by revealed law.

And His words:

“Allah certainly took a covenant from the Children of Israel, and We appointed twelve leaders from among them. Allah said, ‘I am with you. If you establish prayer, give zakah, believe in My messengers and support them, and lend Allah a good loan…’”

The passage continues up to His words:

“So, for their breaking their covenant, We cursed them and hardened their hearts.”

This covenant concerned what was already obligatory upon them: establishing prayer, giving zakah, believing in the messengers, and supporting them. He stated that He cursed them and hardened their hearts because they broke their covenant, not merely because they disobeyed the command. This indicates that the punishment for violating these obligations, reinforced by covenants, is aggravated by the breach of covenant.

And His words:

“And from those who say, ‘We are Christians,’ We took their covenant, but they neglected a portion of what they had been reminded of.”

The same applies to them. And Allah Most High says:

“Among them are those who made a covenant with Allah: ‘If He gives us of His bounty, we will certainly give charity and be among the righteous.’”

“But when He gave them of His bounty, they withheld it greedily and turned away in aversion.”

“So He caused hypocrisy to take root in their hearts until the Day they meet Him, because they broke their promise to Allah and because they used to lie.”

For being among the righteous

---

## Page 14241

is obligatory, and prescribed charity is obligatory; it has also been reported that the charity meant here is that pledged by vow. This explicitly establishes that a vow makes binding what was already obligatory under revealed law. If a person neglects it, he is punished for breaking his promise—that is, his vow. A vow is a solemn promise, as reported concerning Arab usage, and this verse calls a vow a promise.

And His words:

“I will not send him with you until you give me a solemn pledge before Allah that you will bring him back to me, unless you are overwhelmed.” When they gave him their solemn pledge, he said, “Allah is Witness over what we say.”

Returning him to his father was already obligatory upon them, even without a solemn pledge.

Permissible warfare includes defending legally protected lives, property, and sexual inviolability against an aggressor. The concession was granted specifically in peacemaking and warfare because these two situations rest upon bringing hearts together or setting them against one another. When hearts come together, there is peace; when they turn against one another, there is war. Such attraction and aversion can arise from imagined impressions just as they can from realities. Hence poetry can effectively draw people closer or drive them away, powerfully stirring desire and aversion within them, even when its words do not correspond to reality, but work through imagery or figurative comparison.

Since, in lawful peacemaking and warfare, imagining something unreal can serve the same purpose as imagining something real, and equivocal expressions do no more than suggest something unreal while the speaker intends only what is true, such speech is true and truthful from the speaker’s standpoint, while giving the listener an impression that draws him closer in a manner loved by Allah and His Messenger, or drives him away in a manner loved by Allah and His Messenger. This is like drawing him closer or driving him away through poems employing imagery and figurative comparison, and like

---

## Page 14242

stories containing illustrative parables. For parables in verse or prose, when true and consistent with reality, belong to the kind of poetry that is wisdom. If they contain striking similes and powerful imagery, they serve to draw people closer or drive them away.

Chapter

As for the saying that some ordinary people attribute to the Prophet—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—

this is a lie attributed to the Messenger of Allah—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—which no scholar has transmitted. How could it be otherwise, when harming them may be justified or unjustified? Indeed, Allah Most High says:

How, then, could he prohibit harming disbelievers unconditionally? And what sin is greater than disbelief? However, in Sunan Abī Dāwūd, al-‘Irbād ibn Sāriyah—may Allah be pleased with him—reports that the Prophet—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—said:

the Messenger of Allah—may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

Those Muslim rulers whom Allah Most High has granted success have continually renewed these conditions upon them. Thus ‘Umar ibn ‘Abd al-‘Azīz—may Allah have mercy on him—renewed them during his caliphate and diligently followed the Sunnah of ‘Umar ibn al-Khattāb—may Allah be pleased with him—

## Page 14249

What do the esteemed scholars say (*) concerning a group of non-Muslims under Muslim protection who have been required to wear clothing other than their customary dress and adopt an appearance different from their usual one? The sultan has required them to change their turbans so that they differ from those worn by Muslims. This has caused them great harm on the roads and in the open country, emboldening fools and the rabble against them, who have subjected them to severe abuse. It has encouraged people to humiliate and assault them. May the ruler therefore allow them to return to their former dress and restore their previous situation, provided that they remain distinguishable by an identifying mark? Would this contravene Islamic law or not?

Ibn al-Qayyim said:

Someone deprived of divine guidance and turned away from the path answered them that this was permissible and that the ruler could restore their previous situation.

Our shaykh said:

“The request for a ruling then reached me. I said, ‘They may not be allowed to return to their former dress. They must be kept in the attire that distinguishes them from Muslims.’

“They went away, revised the request, and brought it back in a different form. I said, ‘They may not be allowed to return to their former dress.’

“They went away and brought it back in yet another form. I said, ‘It is the very same question, even if presented in several different forms.’”

Ibn al-Qayyim said:

Then Shaykh al-Islām went to the sultan and addressed him in words that astonished those present. They unanimously agreed to keep them in that attire. All praise belongs to Allah, and all favor comes from Him.

## Page 14250

He was also asked:

Concerning monks who share in most of the worldly pursuits of other people: they engage in trade, acquire farms and dovecotes, and undertake other activities commonly pursued by people today. Their monasticism consists merely in their clothing, abstaining from marriage and meat, devotional practices involving impurity, and similar observances. Christians who wish to avoid paying the jizya (poll tax) have now begun adopting this form of monasticism to secure exemption from it. They also receive funds from endowments and votive offerings. Is it permissible to collect the jizya from these people or not? Is it permissible to allow them to reside in Muslim lands while exempting them from the jizya or not? Please give us a ruling, and may you be rewarded.

He replied—may Allah be pleased with him:

All praise belongs to Allah.

The monks concerning whom scholars have disagreed over whether they may be killed and whether the jizya may be collected from them are those mentioned in the report transmitted from Abū Bakr al-Siddīq, the successor of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), may Allah be pleased with him. When he sent Yazīd ibn Abī Sufyān as commander for the conquest of Syria, he said in his instructions to him: “You will find people who have

---

## Page 14251

secluded themselves in hermitages; leave them undisturbed in what they have secluded themselves to do. You will also find people who have shaved the crowns of their heads; strike those shaven parts with the sword, for Allah says:

‘Fight the leaders of disbelief, for they have no regard for their oaths, so that they may desist.’”

He forbade killing the former only because they are people who have withdrawn from others and confined themselves to hermitages. Each is called a recluse. They give their coreligionists no assistance whatsoever in anything harmful to Muslims, nor do they mingle with them in their worldly affairs. Rather, each contents himself with enough to subsist on. Scholars therefore disagreed over killing them, just as they disagreed over killing those who do not harm Muslims by deed or word, such as the blind, the chronically disabled, the elderly, and others like them, as well as women and children.

The majority say that only those who assist them in fighting in some way may be killed; otherwise, they are treated like women and children.

Some, however, say that disbelief alone makes killing lawful, and that women and children were excepted only because they are property. The collection of the jizya is likewise determined on this basis.

As for a monk who assists his coreligionists by deed or word—for example, by offering counsel to which they turn in matters of warfare, or by providing some form of encouragement to fight—scholars agree that he is to be killed if he is overpowered, and that the jizya is collected from him, even if he is a recluse living alone in his place of worship. How much more, then, does this apply to those who are like other Christians in their livelihoods, their mingling with people, and their acquisition of wealth through trade, agriculture, and crafts,

---

## Page 14252

and their establishment of monasteries where others congregate? They are distinguished from others only by things that intensify their disbelief and make them leaders in disbelief, such as acts of worship involving impurities, abstention from marriage and meat, and clothing that is a distinctive mark of disbelief. This is especially so because they sustain the Christian religion through the deceptive tricks they display—about which learned men have written works—their corrupt acts of worship, and their acceptance of their coreligionists’ votive offerings and endowments.

Among them, the sole condition for being a monk is abstention from marriage. Nevertheless, they allow him to be a batrak, a batraq, a priest, or another leader of disbelief whose commands and prohibitions they follow. They may also acquire wealth just as others do. Scholars therefore do not dispute that these are among the Christians most liable to be killed in wartime and to have the jizya collected from them in peacetime. Nor do they dispute that they belong to the same category as those leaders of disbelief about whom al-Siddīq, may Allah be pleased with him, made his statement and recited the words of the Most High:

“Fight the leaders of disbelief.”

This is further clarified by the words of Allah, Glorified and Exalted:

“Indeed, many of the rabbis and monks devour people’s wealth unjustly and turn others away from the way of Allah.”

The Most High also says:

“They have taken their rabbis and monks, as well as the Messiah, son of Mary, as lords besides Allah, though they were commanded only to worship one God. There is no deity except Him. Exalted is He above whatever they associate with Him.”

Would any scholar, then, say that the leaders of disbelief who turn their ordinary followers away from the way of

---

## Page 14253

Allah, devour people’s wealth unjustly, and consent to being taken as lords besides Allah should neither be fought nor have the jizya collected from them, even though it is collected from ordinary people who cause less harm to religion and possess less wealth? No one who understands what he is saying would say this. The confusion arose only because the word “monk” is ambiguous and has several meanings. We have explained that the transmitted report is qualified and restricted in scope, and that it clarifies the report traced back to the Prophet on this matter. The scholars agree that the reason for the prohibition is what we have explained.

The jizya is therefore collected from those described here, without any doubt or disagreement among the leading scholars. It is to be taken from them, and no Muslim land conquered by force and subjected to the jizya may lawfully be left in their possession. Accordingly, scholars of the established schools—the Hanafīs, Mālikīs, Shāfiʿīs, and Hanbalīs—have not disputed that Egypt’s land was subject to kharāj (land tax). This is established by the authentic hadith in Sahīh Muslim, in which the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Iraq will withhold its dirhams and qafīz measures, Syria will withhold its mudd measures and dinars, and Egypt will withhold its irdabb measures and dirhams, and you will return to where you began.”

However, when the Muslims grew in number, they changed the assessment of the lands of al-Sawād, in the early Abbasid period, from a fixed land tax to a share of the produce. Likewise, they changed the arrangement in Egypt until they themselves received its revenues, as is the case today; hence the land tax was lifted from it. By the consensus of the Muslims, land of this kind may not be made an endowment for

---

## Page 14254

people such as these, who derive revenue from it without giving anything in return. It is thus clear that reclaiming these lands from them is obligatory by the agreement of the Muslim scholars.

They gained control of them only because of the many hypocrites among those professing Islam under the Rāfidī state, and this state of affairs continued. Because so many scribes and administrative officials come from their ranks and those of the hypocrites, they handle the Muslims’ wealth in this manner, as is well known of the practices of unbelieving and hypocritical officials.

Consequently, these unbelievers’ places of worship have endowments the like of which are not found for the Muslims’ mosques and residences devoted to learning and worship, even though the land was subject to kharāj by the agreement of the Muslim scholars. No one who believes in Allah and His Messenger would do such a thing. Rather, it is done only by unbelievers, hypocrites, and those Muslim rulers whom they have misled about this matter. Once the Muslim rulers understand the situation, they will act in this matter as Allah and His Messenger have commanded. Allah, glorified and exalted is He, knows best. May Allah bless Muhammad.

## Page 14255

He—may Allah have mercy on him—was also asked about a Jewish man who possesses a document which he claims is in the handwriting of ʿAlī ibn Abī Tālib. He invokes it to refuse payment of the jizya (poll tax), which he has not paid for some time.

He replied:

Every document that the Jews claim exempts them from the jizya, whether attributed to ʿAlī or anyone else, is a forgery for which they deserve punishment, in addition to the collection of the jizya from them. The outstanding jizya must also be collected from this man. Allah knows best.

He—may Allah have mercy on him—was also asked:

If Jews and Christians keep wine, is it lawful for a Muslim to pour it away, break their vessels, and forcibly enter their homes for that purpose, or not? Is it permissible to forcibly enter Muslims’ homes when it is known or suspected that there is wine inside, though none of it is openly apparent, in order to pour it away, break the vessels, and spy out where it is kept, or not? Is doing this forbidden for the person who carries it out if he has been ordered to do so by the ruler? Or is the mere order, without coercion, sufficient to excuse him? And if

---

## Page 14256

he fears that disobeying the order will expose him to harm, does that constitute an excuse for him or not?

He replied:

Praise be to Allah. As for non-Muslims under a covenant of protection, although they are allowed what they are entitled to under their religion, they may not sell wine to a Muslim, give it to him as a gift, or assist him with it in any way. They may not press grapes to make wine for a Muslim, carry it for him, or sell it to a Muslim or a protected non-Muslim. All these prohibitions are conditions imposed upon them under the covenant of protection. Whenever they do such things, they deserve a punishment that deters them and others like them. As to whether this invalidates their covenant and makes their lives and property forfeit, there are two views within the school of Imam Ahmad and among others.

Likewise, they may not enlist the influence of anyone they serve, anyone among them who has professed Islam, or anyone else, to engage openly in any wrongdoing. Rather, just as they must be punished, so too must anyone who assists them in any of these matters, whether through his influence or otherwise.

If a protected non-Muslim drinks wine, is he subject to the prescribed punishment? The jurists hold three views: some say that he is; others say that he is not; and others say that he is if he becomes intoxicated. This concerns cases in which he does so openly among Muslims. As for what they do privately in their homes, without harming Muslims in any way, they are not to be interfered with.

Accordingly, if they will not desist from openly displaying wine, assisting Muslims with it, or selling it or giving it as gifts to Muslims unless it is poured away

---

## Page 14257

at their expense, then it is to be poured away, in addition to whatever punishment is imposed upon them—whether the punishment for one who breaches the covenant or some other punishment.

He was asked:

Concerning Jews in one of the Muslim cities: they have frequently been selling wine to individual Muslims and have amassed considerable wealth from this. The Muslim ruler has stipulated that they must not sell it to Muslims and that, if they do so, they will become subject to the same measures as enemy belligerents. What punishment do they deserve? May the ruler confiscate the wealth they have earned from selling wine, or not?

He replied:

Praise be to Allah. For this, they deserve a punishment that deters them and others like them from such conduct. According to one of the two scholarly views within the school of Ahmad and elsewhere, this invalidates their covenant. If their covenant is invalidated, their lives and property become forfeit, and they become subject to the same measures as unbelieving belligerents.

The ruler may confiscate these funds, which they have wrongfully received from the wealth of Muslims. He should not return them to those who purchased wine from them, for if those purchasers knew that they were forbidden to drink, buy, and sell wine, yet bought it nonetheless, they are in the same position as Muslims who sell wine. Whoever sells wine does not acquire lawful ownership of its price. Thus, if the purchaser has taken the wine and drunk it, he must not

---

## Page 14258

be allowed to retain both the payment and what he received in exchange. Rather, this money is to be taken and spent for the benefit of the Muslims, as has been held concerning a prostitute’s earnings, a soothsayer’s fee, and similar payments for a prohibited item or service, where the sinner has already received the consideration in full.

This differs from the case of a protected non-Muslim selling wine privately to another protected non-Muslim: he is not prevented from doing so. Once both parties have taken possession of what is due to them, a Muslim may transact with the seller using the money he received for the wine. As ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, said: “Leave its sale to them, and take its proceeds from them.”

Indeed, beyond this, the ruler may demolish the premises where wine is sold, whether a shop or a house. ʿUmar ibn al-Khattāb did this when he demolished the shop of Ruwayshid al-Thaqafī and said: “You are only Fuwaysiq (a petty sinner), not Ruwayshid (a little rightly guided man).” Likewise, ʿAlī ibn Abī Tālib burned down a village where wine was sold. Ahmad and other scholars have explicitly affirmed this.

---

## Page 14259

He was asked about a Jew who said, “These Muslims—dogs, sons of dogs—are banding together against us,” after some Muslims had quarrelled with him.

He replied—may Allah have mercy on him:

If he intended his insults to target a particular group of Muslims, he is to receive a punishment that will deter him and others like him from doing such a thing. But if it becomes apparent that he intended Muslims in general, then his covenant is thereby annulled, and he must be put to death.
